pages.bodyCopy:
Why Your Back Still Hurts Weeks After a Car Accident, And What to Do About It

Understanding Back Pain Relief Following a Car Crash

You were in a car accident a few weeks ago. At first, you thought the pain would go away on its own. But here you are, still dealing with back pain every day. Sitting hurts, standing feels stiff, and even lying down doesn’t give you the relief you expected. What’s going on?

You’re not alone. Many people experience lingering pain after a crash, even when there are no obvious injuries. The good news? There are ways to find back pain relief following a car crash, and Elevate Wellness in Bountiful and Clinton, UT, is here to help.

Causes of Back Pain After a Car Accident

The force of a crash can do serious damage to your back, even if you don’t feel it right away. Here are some of the most common reasons your pain is sticking around:

1. Whiplash and Soft Tissue Injuries

Whiplash isn’t just a neck problem. The sudden movement can strain muscles, ligaments, and tendons all along your spine. This can cause stiffness, soreness, and reduced mobility.

2. Herniated or Bulging Discs

The impact of a crash can push your spinal discs out of place. This can press on nerves, leading to pain, numbness, or tingling in your back and legs.

3. Spinal Misalignment

Even a minor accident can throw your spine out of alignment. When your vertebrae aren’t lined up properly, it can create pressure on nerves and muscles, causing persistent pain.

4. Inflammation and Scar Tissue

Your body tries to heal itself by creating inflammation and scar tissue. But too much of it can limit movement and cause ongoing discomfort.

5. Hidden Fractures or Joint Damage

Sometimes, small fractures or joint injuries don’t show up right away. Over time, they can lead to pain and stiffness that won’t go away on their own.

Immediate Back Pain Relief Tips

If you’re dealing with pain, here are some things you can do right now:

1. Use Ice and Heat Therapy

Ice reduces swelling, while heat relaxes tense muscles. Try applying ice for 15 minutes, then switch to heat after a few hours.

2. Rest, But Not Too Much

Taking it easy for a few days is fine, but too much rest can make things worse. Gentle movement helps your body heal faster.

3. Over-the-Counter Pain Relief

NSAIDs like ibuprofen can reduce inflammation and ease discomfort. But they’re not a long-term solution.

4. Stay Hydrated

Water helps your body recover and keeps your spinal discs healthy. Aim for at least eight glasses a day.

5. Avoid Heavy Lifting or Strenuous Activities

Give your back time to heal by avoiding anything that puts extra strain on your spine.

Gentle Exercises for Recovery

Moving your body the right way can help ease pain and prevent stiffness. Here are a few simple exercises to try:

1. Pelvic Tilts

Lie on your back with your knees bent.

Tighten your stomach muscles and flatten your lower back against the floor.

Hold for a few seconds, then release. Repeat 10 times.

2. Knee-to-Chest Stretch

Lie on your back and bring one knee toward your chest.

Hold for 15-30 seconds, then switch legs.

Repeat 3-5 times on each side.

3. Cat-Cow Stretch

Get on your hands and knees.

Arch your back up like a cat, then slowly lower it down while lifting your head.

Repeat 10 times.

4. Gentle Walking

Walking helps keep your muscles active and prevents stiffness. Start with 5-10 minutes a day and gradually increase your time.

The Risks of Ignoring Chronic Pain

If your pain isn’t going away, don’t ignore it. Chronic back pain can lead to:

1. Reduced Mobility

Stiffness and discomfort can limit how much you move, leading to muscle weakness and more pain.

2. Long-Term Nerve Damage

Herniated discs and spinal misalignments can put pressure on nerves, causing long-term pain, numbness, or even permanent damage.

3. Mental Health Struggles

Dealing with pain every day can take a toll on your mood, increasing stress, anxiety, and even depression.

4. Compensatory Injuries

If your back hurts, you might change how you move to avoid pain. This can lead to new injuries in your hips, knees, or shoulders.

The Benefits of Seeking Professional Help

If your pain isn’t getting better, seeing a specialist can make all the difference. Here’s how Elevate Wellness can help:

1. Chiropractic Care

Spinal adjustments can help realign your spine, relieve pressure on nerves, and improve mobility.

2. Massage Therapy

Targeted massage can reduce muscle tension, break up scar tissue, and improve blood flow to speed up healing.

3. Physical Rehab

A guided rehab program can help restore strength, flexibility, and function in your back.

4. Personalized Treatment Plans

Every injury is different. The team at Elevate Wellness in Bountiful and Clinton, UT, will create a custom plan that fits your needs.

FAQs: Common Concerns About Back Pain Relief Following a Car Crash

How long should back pain last after a car accident?

Mild pain can go away in a few days, but more serious injuries may take weeks or months to heal. If your pain lasts more than two weeks, see a professional.

Can a minor accident still cause back pain?

Yes! Even low-speed crashes can cause spinal misalignment and soft tissue injuries.

Should I see a doctor if my X-ray was normal?

Yes. Soft tissue injuries, herniated discs, and nerve damage don’t always show up on X-rays. A specialist can perform a more detailed evaluation.

What if my pain started weeks after the accident?

Delayed pain is common. Inflammation and scar tissue can build up over time, causing pain to appear weeks later.

Is it too late to get treatment if my accident was months ago?

No! It’s never too late to seek treatment. Many injuries can improve with the right care, even months after an accident.

Key Takeaways

Back pain after a car crash can come from soft tissue injuries, herniated discs, or spinal misalignment.

Ice, heat, and gentle movement can help relieve pain.

Ignoring pain can lead to long-term issues.

Seeking professional care from Elevate Wellness can help you recover faster and avoid chronic problems.

If you’re in Bountiful or Clinton, UT, and struggling with back pain relief following a car crash, Elevate Wellness is ready to help. Don’t let pain control your life. Contact us and get the care you need today!

pages.bodyCopy:
Some patients may be hesitant to seek chiropractic care. Knowing more about a treatment or the process of something can put our minds at ease. Elevate Wellness wants to share more about our practice and the history of the industry and how chiropractic treatment and alignment, came to be.

The word “Chiropractic” is derived from the Greek words cheir which means ‘hand’ and praktos, meaning ‘done.’ Put together meaning done by hand. Alignment and adjustment have been traced back to the Greek physician, Hippocrates. In the 16th-19th century, spinal manipulation was commonly associated with “bone setters’ who learned the craft passed down from family generations. These bone setters also treated joints that were out of place, called subluxations.

In 1895, Canadian doctor Daniel David Palmer started work to bring more spine care into the open. He learned more about alignment and helping with pain in the lower back and spine. Palmer became the “founder” when he “adjusted” the spine of a deaf janitor and claimed to restore his hearing.

Fight For Acceptance

Palmer went on to found the Palmer School of Chiropractic, where he taught his methods to the first eager students and showed them the practice. Statutes to practice chiropractic care as a profession were not set until much later. It was common for those who practiced alignment to be jailed or fined for practicing without a license before the 1960s.

The conflict between chiropractors and organized medicine took time to resolve. Chiropractors were often charged with violating the medical practice act and were not seen as real doctors. At the peak of the struggle, around 450 chiropractors were sent to jail in a single year.

While there are fewer legal actions taken against chiropractors today, many interested patients have mixed feelings about whether or not the treatment will work for them. Many patients are satisfied with the care they receive but a study in 1973 in Utah found that patients see this as part of their overall healthcare.

Chiropractic and alignment care have transitioned from being seen as “alternative medicine” to a more mainstream form of physical healthcare throughout history. More people visit a chiropractor today and consider it a viable option for their condition.

Why Work With Us?

Dr. Simmonds is our licensed and trained chiropractor who has received training and knowledge from other doctors and education. We work to provide our patients with a comfortable experience and teach them about what chiropractic alignment can do for their whole body.

If you are interested, we can tell you more about our history, and how we got to where we are with our practice today. Chiropractic care was seen as alternative medicine because it is a non-invasive and natural treatment. This helps patients to avoid surgery, taking painkillers or other medications for their symptoms.

The goal of chiropractic care, as well as what we strive for, is to get your body to heal in the most natural way possible. Dr. Simmonds practices the latest techniques and helps remove nerve interferences due to misalignments in the body. Proper chiropractic care can help to relieve stress, improve pain symptoms, help the body heal from injury and help you have more energy.

Symptoms do not even have to be present for you to get the most out of our treatment. We work with each patient to develop a custom plan for what they want to accomplish. Proper chiropractic treatment helps maintain proper spine health, increase the function of the nervous system and helps you have a stronger immune system. Chiropractic treatment helps you to feel better in more than just one area of your life.

If you have been hesitant about chiropractic treatment, feel free to visit our office in Bountiful, UT, and speak with Dr. Simmonds about any questions you have. Learning more about treatment will help to calm your nerves and finding an office that you are comfortable with can be a big step. Contact us today!

pages.bodyCopy:
If you have back pain or problems in your spine, it affects your entire life. It’s hard to do things when they hurt, and when your spine is what hurts, that impacts everything. It limits your mobility and makes every kind of movement painful. When considering treatment options, you may have come across Spinal Decompression Therapy. As with many chiropractic treatments, there are those who wonder if spinal decompression therapy even works. Why not just get spinal decompression surgery, instead?

Here’s what you need to know about spinal decompression therapy and whether or not it is an option for you.

What Is Spinal Decompression Therapy?

Spinal decompression is a process where the spine is stretched. It eases pressure on spinal discs with slow and controlled stretching. It’s a noninvasive treatment method that is meant to help spinal injuries without surgery. It pulls weight off the spine, allows discs to go back in place, and helps to relieve pinched nerves and stimulate blood flow to hurt areas, ergo stimulating the body’s natural healing process. It’s a natural method of treatment, meant to help your body heal itself.

Why Does Your Spine Matter So Much?

Your spine is one of the most important parts of your body. Your central nervous system is in your spine which means that when something is off with your spine, it affects your whole body. A herniated disc can cause leg pain in addition to back pain. Your neck being out of alignment can disrupt the signals your optic nerves send to your brain, ergo impacting your vision. Your spine being hurt means you will find it much harder to move. Your spine matters a lot, which means it’s vital to take care of it.

How Can Spinal Decompression Help?

Spinal problems like herniated discs cause lots of pain, and can lead to restricted movement. Decompressing the spine makes it less likely to degenerate, as we put a lot of pressure on our spine every day. Over time, all that pressure can be quite hard on it, especially if you have a job where you sit all day, as sitting places more pressure on your spine than if you were standing, especially if you have poor posture. Problems with the spine also lead to problems in other areas, like legs, butt, etc, as mentioned above.

Spinal decompression helps by stretching out your spine, relieving pressure and stimulating blood flow.

How Does Spinal Decompression Therapy Work?

Spinal decompression therapy is an outpatient treatment process. Sessions run between half an hour to an hour, and many people report feeling some relief even after their first session. It may be combined with other forms of treatment.

How it works is that you lay on a table of a decompressing machine and are strapped down. The machine’s computer determines what stretching level is best for you and gently pulls your body from a resting position into a stretched-out one. As stretching generally entails, it holds you there for a short period before releasing you, then starting the process again for the duration of the session.

The computer adjusts to you and senses if your muscles are resistant. If they are, it will change the force and cycle of the stretching in order to help relieve the tension in your muscles, as opposed to pulling them and causing more damage. The machine is controlled by a chiropractor, so there is no need to worry about if it might break and not adjust to you.

Spinal decompression can also be done manually. It shouldn’t be a painful treatment. You should just feel a stretch in your spine. There’s no need to take your clothes off at all. It can also be coupled with other treatments, as well as stretches to be done at home.

What Is Spinal Decompression Good For?

The goal of this treatment is to relieve pain and pressure on joints and nerves. It’s good for: sciatica, back and neck pain, stenosis, muscle weakness, bulging or herniated discs, degenerative disc disorders, and more. It helps relieve pain, arthritis, realign spinal discs and joints, and relieves pressure on nerves. It also improves oxygen and blood flow. It’s not meant to merely relieve pain, but also to help fix the problem causing it.

While good for many, spinal decompression therapy is not a good treatment option for all. Some people for whom spinal decompression therapy is not recommended for include: pregnant people, people with broken vertebrae/implants/artificial discs, etc, those with tumors or infection, who are on blood thinners, who had a failed back surgery, and more.

What Affects How Effective It Is?

The efficacy of this treatment depends on the same factors you would consider for any other. Things such as the skill level of your provider and how credible the doctor who diagnosed you is all play factors into whether or not it actually works.

Are You Considering Spinal Decompression Therapy?

Generally, it’s believed that surgery should be a last resort for your problems, so we recommend you to try spinal decompression therapy first.

Here at Elevate Wellness, we offer spinal decompression therapy. We know how important your spine is to your overall health, and want to help you with any problems you may have not merely by treating the pain, but the root of the problem itself. If you would like to schedule an appointment or if you have any questions, please feel free to contact us at Elevate Wellness today!

pages.bodyCopy:
The body undergoes many changes during pregnancy. Chiropractic treatment provides many advantages, though many women are concerned that it isn’t safe to get chiropractic care while pregnant. However, this is simply not true. In fact, seeing a chiropractor while pregnant can lead to many benefits to your health, including a more comfortable labor! At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we have the necessary expertise to provide superior chiropractic care during pregnancy.

Back Pain is Common During Pregnancy

As the baby develops and the body changes, it is common for the new changes to place a great deal of strain on the spine and the back. This often results in back pain. Chiropractic treatment can often help to reduce back pain that may be present during pregnancy, as well as resolve any underlying problems that may be causing your back pain.

Consult with your Care Provider

Most experts agree that there are no risks associated with chiropractic treatment during pregnancy. However, it is still essential to consult with your OBGYN prior to beginning chiropractic treatment. They will be aware of any existing concerns with your pregnancy that may impact the safety of your chiropractic treatment. Once they have given you the green light, you can receive many advantages from utilizing chiropractic treatment.

Chiropractic Care Can Help

The changes during pregnancy can cause the spine and joints to fall out of alignment. Chiropractic care is a great way to realign the spine and joints that have been impacted by your pregnancy. This can both relieve pain and impacts the nervous system.

Advantages of Chiropractic Care During Pregnancy

Since chiropractic care can help to impact the nervous system, there are many unexpected advantages that you may gain from receiving chiropractic treatment during pregnancy. Chiropractic care can help to reduce nausea, as well as limit the number of headaches that you may experience. The right treatment can help to minimize swelling, as well as relieve sciatic pain. Many women experience higher quality of sleep when receiving chiropractic care during pregnancy.

Is Chiropractic Care Safe While Pregnant?

The American Pregnancy Association has stated that there is no particular reason to avoid chiropractic treatment during pregnancy, as there aren’t any specific risks associated with chiropractic care. However, it is still important to ensure that you consult with your care provider prior to beginning this type of treatment. It is also important to choose a chiropractor that has experience specifically in providing chiropractic treatment during pregnancy. Our team at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic offers pregnancy-specific chiropractic services to meet all of your needs.

Easier Labor

Chiropractic treatment has actually been shown to make labor easier. The right services can help to position the baby properly and expedite the labor process. Many women actually see their chiropractor more often during the third trimester of pregnancy to help alleviate unpleasant symptoms.

When you are pregnant, you may experience many negative symptoms that can be relieved through chiropractic treatment. The experts at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic can help to provide the ideal chiropractic care during pregnancy. For more information about the advantages of seeing a chiropractor while pregnant, contact us at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic today!

headings.text: How Poor Posture Causes Shoulder Pain
Why Pulling Your Shoulders Back Won’t Help
Do You Need Help Fixing Your Posture?

pages.bodyCopy:
Everyone has heard how important good posture is. Growing up, you’ve probably been told to “Sit up straight!” and warned that you’ll develop a hunch if you don’t. Yet in spite of all the evidence showing us how and why good posture is important, it’s easy to hunch and slouch, either from wanting to make yourself seem smaller or from sitting down all day.

While your neck and your back are the most common parts of your body linked to your posture, your shoulders play a vital role too. If poor posture is left uncorrected long enough, you may end up with shoulder pain. If you’ve tried to fix your posture and your shoulders hurt, this can be for a number of reasons ranging from the impact of long-term poor posture and improper attempts at correcting your posture.

How Poor Posture Causes Shoulder Pain

People often overlook the impact your posture can have on your shoulders. Hunching and slouching causes your upper back to bend forward, which affects your shoulders. This can change the position and how your shoulders move over time, leading to bad posture shoulder pain.

Loss Of Strength

Poor posture affects your muscles, leading to muscular imbalances which can result in muscle pain. This is because when you slouch, some of your muscles tighten while others loosen. This muscular imbalance makes it so that your shoulder muscles can’t produce the same amount of force as they would be able to if they were balanced. This weakens your shoulders, as well as stretching the muscles in your back while loosening the ones in your chest. Since your muscles become imbalanced, they lose strength they’d otherwise have if you maintained proper posture.

Lessened Range Of Motion

Slouching doesn’t just affect the strength of your muscles, it also limits your range of motion. You can notice this immediately, not just over an extended period of time. If you have poor posture and attempt to do something even as simple as circling your arm, it may be stiff or hurt. If you then try to do the same thing with corrected posture, you’ll likely notice that it instantly becomes a bit easier or less painful.

Improper Movement Leading To Injury

Your shoulders aren’t meant to be hunched forward. Prolonged poor posture can misalign the positioning of your shoulder blades, which can lead to injury at your rotator cuff when you try to move your arms. Since poor posture limits your range of motion, it also heightens your risk for wear and tear injuries, tendinosis, and tendonitis.

Why Pulling Your Shoulders Back Won’t Help

One of the most common responses when people talk about posture is for others to automatically pull their shoulders back in an attempt to improve their own. Merely pulling your shoulders back won’t fix the hunching of your upper body and neck, though. This is because your shoulders sit over your rib cage.

This means that in order to fix your posture, sitting up straight means that your breast bone and your pubic bone shoulder are aligned on top of each other. Puffing out your chest and pulling your shoulders back won’t put your spine in alignment or fix the position of your rib cage, and ergo, your shoulders.

How To Fix Your Posture

Fixing your posture won’t happen immediately. In many cases, especially if poor posture has gotten to the point where your shoulders hurt, correcting your posture will feel wrong. This is because your body has grown accustomed to hunching, so working to change that is changing what your body has grown used to, which it will naturally resist. In order to prevent injury and to correct your posture, it will take time and effort, but it can be done.

To fix your posture, it’s going to take conscious effort all day long. Good posture is simply a part of your day to day life. Strengthening your back and core muscles will make it easier to maintain good posture. Sitting up from your hips instead of pulling your shoulders back will help keep your rib cage properly aligned. Pinching your shoulder blades lightly together and rolling them up and back can help too.

Changing your posture requires awareness of how your body is positioned always, and making those constant adjustments until it becomes something your body does automatically.

How Chiropractors Can Help

If you’re struggling with fixing your posture, especially if it’s because of shoulder pain, chiropractors can help. Chiropractors can observe how you sit and walk and test your strength and range of motion in order to determine how best to help. Poor posture can put a lot of pressure on your spinal discs, so they may also take a look at your back.

Chiropractors can help by adjusting your spine in order to increase movement and reduce tension, so that it will be easier to adjust to better posture. They can also work with your muscles to help strengthen them, so that they can hold good posture, and so that it is more comfortable when you work to sit or stand properly. They can also guide you through stretches and rehabilitating exercises which will reduce tension and strengthen your muscles.

Fixing bad posture on your own can be difficult, because it’s not as simple as “just sit up straight!” There can be underlying issues resulting from poor posture. Chiropractors can help guide you back to good posture, so that you can go about your life without pain or injury.

Do You Need Help Fixing Your Posture?

Elevate Wellness knows how important your posture is for your health, and also how difficult it can be to fix your posture by yourself. We can help you regain good posture, and help treat any pain resulting from bad posture. Contact us at Elevate Wellness today to schedule a consultation.

pages.metaTitle: 7 Chiropractor Approved Summer Activities | Elevate Wellness Chiropractic
pages.metaDescription: If you experience joint pain, these summer activities can help you to feel better and improve your overall health. Read below.
pages.bodyCopy:
Summer activities are a great way to get some physical exercise. For those with joint pain, exercises such as running or jumping can cause severe pain. Here is a list of activities that are low impact, chiropractor recommended summer activities for your joints and can actually help alleviate some of the pain you may be experiencing.

Stretch Before Anything

Before you begin any physical activity it is best to stretch and warm up your body. Moving and stretching your muscles helps prevent injury or further pain and gets them ready before jumping right into a strenuous exercise. Stretching gets your body going and ready to move and keeps it moving.

Swimming

Summer isn’t summer without swimming. Luckily swimming is one of the best summer activities you can participate in to help back and joint pain. Aerobic exercise is really helpful for those with chronic pain. Even casual swimming or aerobic exercises can help with physical fitness. Water helps to give you some exercise without putting more pressure on your joints and swimming also helps to lower your blood pressure. If you feel you need some exercise this summer but want less pain, hop on in the pool.

Biking

Summer is the perfect time to explore on your bike. Biking is low impact for your body and is recommended for current chiropractic patients. It is important to maintain good posture and take breaks as needed for your joint or back pain.

Yoga

Like stretching, yoga can help to alleviate pain and prevent future joint pain. Yoga is included in this list of summer activities because the warmth from the sun actually helps improve your flexibility. There are many health benefits to yoga than it just being a low impact exercise. It can help lower back pain, benefit your heart health and improve your sleep.

Hiking

Hiking is a great way to get outdoors and explore nature. Take your time while hiking and use a walking stick to help with pain if the hike is more challenging. Walking and hiking can easily boost your health and have relatively low impact. If the heat is bothersome for you, it is best to hike or walk in the early morning or evening when it is still light out.

Strength Training

If you experience pain while exercising, strength training might not seem appealing. But building up your muscles is a summer activity that can help protect your joints and ligaments. You don’t have to start with the heaviest weights to get results, but you can build up to bigger exercises. Talk to your doctor or chiropractor to make sure you have a routine that allows you to rest and recover.

Relaxing In A Hammock

Relaxing seems to come hand in hand with the summer months. Relaxing in a hammock is a great summer activity for those who experience chronic pain. Raising your legs in a hammock can help with blood circulation and the flexibility of the hammock allows your body to take the pressure off your joints.

Summer Activities To Avoid

Naps can be helpful for rest but laying down and taking a nap can cause inflammation in those that experience joint pain. Resting your body is important, but if after a nap you feel that your joints are stiff, maybe avoid napping during the day.

Visit Your Chiropractor

One of the most important summer activities that you should not skip is to visit your chiropractor regularly. We can help provide some relief if you have done too much activity or are feeling stiff. Chiropractors help with all kinds of pain and can help your body to heal more naturally.

Elevate Wellness is open Monday through Thursday to make sure that your body is summer ready. Getting low impact exercise combined with visiting our office can help you feel more energized and ready to take on the day. Contact our office to set up an appointment today.

pages.bodyCopy:
If you experience back or neck pain, are struggling with digestion or stress, chiropractic treatment could be a solution for you to consider. A chiropractor visit doesn’t just handle injuries, they can help aid in a multitude or issues and get your body the relief it needs.

If you have been considering chiropractor treatment, there may be more to their services than you first realized. Chiropractors can help to align your spine, neck and other parts of your body, but they can also give you tips to manage pain daily and work with you to live a more full life.

Pain Relief

Of course the biggest reason people choose to participate in a chiropractor visit is for pain relief. Whether it be from a car accident, sports injury or chronic pain, chiropractic treatment helps patients to feel relief and do more.

The biggest areas that patients experience pain are the neck and back, which cause lots of discomfort and can keep you from work or recreational activities. Chiropractors can help to minimize or eliminate the pain through massage therapy, k-laser therapy or spinal decompression.

Better Sleep

Many of us would love to get better quality sleep. With a chiropractor visit, helping to limit the pain in your body, it will not have to work as hard while you sleep. Our bodies do the most work while we sleep, helping us to heal. If you have a lot of stress or can’t sleep from pain, it can take your body longer to heal, and affect your sleep.

Chiropractors can use manipulation to increase blood flow in your body which can accelerate healing. Aligning the spine can also help to accelerate healing and give you less problems while laying down.

Pregnancy Relief

When you are pregnant, your body experiences many rapid changes often in a short period of time. Elevate Wellness can help you maintain proper alignment and can help improve your birthing process.

Having a chiropractor visit while you are pregnant can help shorten labor times, make you more comfortable during your pregnancy, have fewer interventions during labor and delivery and help babies have more room to grow freely in the womb. By aligning the pelvis and the spine of the expecting mother, we can help the labor and delivery process go much smoother. We see many expecting mothers in our office and frequently hear from our patients that pregnancies with chiropractic care are much smoother than those without.

Blood Pressure Normalization

Hypertension is usually caused due to stress. Stress creates tension in your muscles, joints, bones and can raise your blood pressure significantly. Most people turn to medication to keep up with their blood pressure but chiropractic care has shown to help significantly decrease blood pressure.

Chiropractors help to relieve stress and when you are not in pain, your stress level will go down. Relieving tension on the top of the neck can help to lower blood pressure rates.

For Those With A Desk Job

Those with a desk job sit hunched over a keyboard or at an uncomfortable chair for the majority of the day can benefit from a chiropractor visit. This can cause discomfort and misalignment in many parts of your body. For those with desk jobs, neck and back pain are a real issue, because they sit in the same position day after day.

Chiropractic care can help to relieve unnecessary pressure on your back, neck and shoulders. Over time, if not taken care of, this pressure can cause your discs to slip or herniate which can be very painful. A chiropractor visit can help prevent herniated discs and improve your comfort at work.

You Play Sports Or Are Athletic

For those who love to be athletic or who play high school or college sports can benefit from regular chiropractic treatment. When you visit a chiropractor you will get a better range of motion and perform better.

Having a consistent chiropractor visit can help to prevent future injury and improve your performance as an athlete. We can also discuss techniques to help you avoid injury and extra stress on your body.

Alternative To Medication

Many patients want to avoid pain medication or other medication at all costs. Chiropractic treatment will help you to avoid pain pills and allow you to go throughout your day without throbbing pain. A chiropractor visit can help your body to heal instead of just masking the pain for a small amount of time.

Work With Elevate Wellness

If you are looking for a chiropractor in Utah, Elevate Wellness is here to help. Located in Bountiful we help to serve many cities in Utah.

At your first chiropractor visit we will discuss your health history and concerns so that we can treat you in the best way possible. Dr. Simmonds will provide recommendations and provide information to help you decide what is best for you and your health.

Even if you don’t currently have symptoms or your pain is mild, chiropractic care is still recommended. Chiropractic care is a proactive way to maintain proper health and keep from injury. If you have more questions about our process or want to learn about our doctor, you can visit our website to read more. We know how uncomfortable pain can be and how it can affect your life. We want to help you get more motion back and go throughout your work day without debilitating pain. Elevate Wellness is open Monday through Thursday to help serve you.

Benefits

Pregnant mothers turn to chiropractic treatment to help with pain and discomfort during pregnancy. Growing a human comes with the moving of organs and bones to help give the fetus to have room to move in the womb. Prenatal chiropractic care helps limit the pain of stretching and moving in the body.

While pain relief is a big factor in choosing chiropractic care, there are actually more benefits to proper alignment. Adjusting the spine and pelvis to their correct positions can give the baby more room to move and adapt in the womb. Chiropractic treatment can help the baby move into the pelvic bowl correctly and provide them with room to grow.

Other benefits that can come from prenatal chiropractic care include:

Controlling symptoms of nausea

Relieve neck, back, and joint pain

Lowering potential of cesarean delivery

Maintain a healthier pregnancy

Webster Technique

When researching chiropractors and prenatal chiropractic care, look for one that is certified in Webster Technique. Dr. Simmonds with Elevate Chiropractic is Webster Technique Certified. This technique is a pre-natal chiropractic procedure that focuses on the pelvis and surrounding structures. This technique helps to support the growth and development of your baby and yields excellent results.

Is It Safe?

Visiting a chiropractor who is certified to work with pregnant women is safe and effective. Chiropractors have been trained to work specifically with pregnant women and have unique tables to accommodate protruding stomachs.

Prenatal chiropractic care techniques also focus pressure away from the abdomen and give exercises that are safe to perform during pregnancy. Stretches and exercises are known to help those who are pregnant and improve the quality of birth. Chiropractic can help amplify the good things that you are already doing.

Elevate Wellness And Pediatrics

Many children come get brought in for other reasons such as colic, reflux, ear infections, nursing difficulty, digestive problems, and constipation.

Children are resilient but they can still have effects on their nervous system. Trauma from birth or other falls and bumps can cause stress on the body. Spinal misalignment can affect the growth of the child and the development of their nervous system. Dr. Simmonds is also a member of the International Chiropractic Pediatric Association (ICPA) and has the training to know how to properly work with children. Please bring your child into our office today to learn more about all that we can offer.

More About Our Office

Elevate Wellness Chiropractic started in 2020 in Bountiful and Dr. Simmonds has brought a passion for care to the community. We are a family-based business and want to treat our patients like family. We treat a variety of issues and pain that occurs in the body besides providing prenatal chiropractic care.

Elevate Wellness also prides itself on helping athletes and sports-related injuries. Dr. Simmonds knows firsthand how helpful chiropractic care can be for those who have had sports-related injuries. Healing naturally can make all the difference in getting back to normal life. We are here to help you on your health journey and listen to your needs.

Each patient has a unique healthcare plan and we only perform procedures that are best for you. Coming in for treatments can help reduce the risk of injury and pain. Studies have shown that chiropractic care is beneficial and can help the body’s natural healing process become more automatic. Contact us today to schedule an appointment.

pages.metaTitle: Is Chiropractic Treatment The Solution To The Opioid Epidemic? | Elevate Wellness Chiropractic
pages.metaDescription: Severe pain is usually treated with opioids and pain medication. The risk of opioid addiction is high and can be avoided with chiropractic care.
pages.bodyCopy:
The common solution for surgery or chronic pain is pain killers or opioids. The use or overuse of these pain pills has caused an opioid epidemic throughout the United States, but especially Utah. In Utah, an average of 323 people die from a prescription opioid drug overdose every year. The solution for the Utah opioid epidemic may not be as simple as limiting access to opioids or going to a chiropractor, but it could be a more promising solution for those that experience extreme pain.

How Chiropractic Treatment Can Help You Avoid Opioids

Historically, back pain has been one of the most common reasons why opioids are prescribed to patients. But on the flip side, there is really no evidence to show that opioids provide relief for chronic pain. Whether your pain is from surgery, an accident or is chronic, there are better options than prescription opioids.

Beyond the risks of prescription overdose, opioids can make the problem seem that it is less severe than it actually is, or make the patient think their condition is fully healed. This can lead to overexertion or delay the healing process. Chiropractic and other non-drug approaches to pain management can be the first step in eliminating the pain completely and keeping the opioid epidemic from growing.

The American College of Physicians updated its guidelines in 2017 to suggest the use of non-invasive and non-drug therapies for back pain first rather than opioid use. Only when the non-drug therapies do not limit the pain is when other medicines such as ibuprofen and muscle relaxants should be recommended. The last resort should be opioids and should only be used after all methods of massage, acupuncture, heat therapy and spinal manipulation have been tested for the patient. This can limit the chance of overdose and help to heal you from your pain in a more natural way.

With Elevate Wellness Chiropractic we have studied and mastered several chiropractic techniques to improve spinal biomechanics and reduce nervous system interference. We practice the safest chiropractic techniques and help to bring balance to the spinal column and pelvic girdle.

Over time, it is common to see misalignments that can separate the vertebrae, causing pain through tilted and twisted vertebrae. What often occurs is pinched or compressed nerves, leading to pain. These subluxations can lead to a number of ailments throughout the body.

Not only can chiropractic care help your back and neck pain, but we can treat issues such as headaches, whiplash and help to prevent future injury.

A Look At The Numbers

According to this study with PubMed, “patients with spinal pain who saw a chiropractor had half the risk of filling an opioid prescription. Among those who saw a chiropractor within 30 days of diagnosis, the reduction in risk was greater as compared with those with their first visit after the acute phase.”

According to Cleveland University “Recent research has found that one day of opioid usage carried a 6% chance of being on opioids one year later. After eight days of use, that chance increased to 13.5%, and after 31 days of use, the chance spiked to nearly 30%.”

A study by BMC Family Practice found that many patients did not know the potential of how the care of acupuncture and chiropractic treatment could help their pain. The study shows that more education and better accessibility to chiropractic care.

Work With Elevate Wellness

We are dedicated to providing the highest quality care chiropractic care and focus on restoring your body to its proper state. Our treatments are non-invasive and we want to help you provide you with relief without pain medication. We offer care for infants, children and adults which is appealing to many because the use of painkillers can be very hard to give to your child.

Using pain killers to treat pain does not have to be the default option anymore. We can provide the best chiropractic treatment, massage or heat therapy to keep you feeling pain free and have the best range of motion.

During your first visit we discuss your health history and talk about what you feel the best treatment is for your body. If you are wanting to feel better and avoid the risk of opioid addiction, we can help.Elevate Wellness uses proactive chiropractic treatment and spinal decompression that can help you heal from auto accidents, sports related injuries, chronic pain and even help pregnant women with spinal alignment. We want to help discuss your pain and create a treatment plan that works best for you. Contact our office to schedule an appointment today.

pages.metaDescription: Start your day with stretches to improve mobility and relieve tension. Chiropractors recommend stretches that focus on the back and neck.
pages.bodyCopy:
Beginning your day with stretching, yoga, a workout, or meditation can help improve your immune system and help your muscles wake up and start your day. Individuals that feel muscle tightness, achy, or weak in the morning, will often skip morning stretches. Stretches can help safeguard the body from injury and help relieve tension. Here are 7 stretches that chiropractors feel can be beneficial to start your morning.

Chest Stretch

For those who sit at a desk every day, this stretch can be essential to alleviate stress. Sitting and looking at a computer screen can create tension in the shoulders, neck, and back.

In order to do this stretch, start by raising both arms until they’re level with your shoulders and out from your body, forming a T-shape. Learn through a door frame with your hands and arms pushing against the wall while your body leans forward through the door. This moves the stretch into the front of your chest.

Hip Flexors Stretch

This stretch starts with using a chair or dresser for balance. Bend one knee and grab the ankle behind your thigh. Push your hip forward on that side to feel the stretch at the front of your hip, then repeat on the opposite side.

This stretch helps to loosen hips and tension in the legs from sitting all day.

Lower Back Stretch

In order to complete this stretch, lie on your back and bring your knees up to your chest. Next, pull both knees down toward your chest, relax, and hold for around 30 seconds.

All back stretches can help limit debilitating back pain and help improve mobility and motion.

Pelvic Tilt

Lie on your back with knees bent, the small of your back should not be touching the bed or floor. Tighten your abdomen so that the small of your back now touches flat the floor or bed. Hold the position for 5 seconds and then release. Repeat the stretch at least three or four times.

This stretch can help relieve back pain, tighten abdominal muscles and increase the strength of pelvic floor muscles.

Piriformis Stretch

Piriformis stretches are used to help with knee and ankle pain and help your joints to stay more stable.

To perform the stretch, lay flat on your back with your right leg crossed over your left. Gently pull the right knee towards the chest until you feel the stretch in your buttocks. Hold the stretch for 30 seconds, release and repeat 3 times. Then repeat three times on the opposite side of your body.

Spinal Twist

Keeping your legs facing forward and firmly planted, turn your upper body to the right while you place your right hand behind you for stability. To push the stretch farther, you can place your left hand on the outside of your right thigh. Hold the stretch for 10 seconds and repeat on the other side.

Performing the spinal twist stretch can increase blood flow and circulation. Twists also reduce back pain and help with flexibility.

Neck Mobility Stretch

Start by sitting with your legs together and then begin rotating your neck in a circle. Imagine your ears touching your shoulders and rotating slowly five times in each direction.

Using this stretch can help improve the range of motion in your neck, and reduce muscle soreness in the neck, shoulders, and back. Tension often builds in the neck and shoulders, so this stretch can help relieve the tension before you start your day.

Chiropractic Treatment With Elevate Wellness

Chiropractic treatment can help treat a variety of issues including back pain, ear infections, asthma, Sciatica pain, Tendinitis, whiplash, and more. We help patients who are facing all kinds of tension, muscle weakness, and more, with a unique care plan designed specifically for you. Our team wants to serve your needs and help to get you back to feeling better from day to day.

Chiropractic care has been shown to limit the use of medication, avoid surgery, and bring back the range of motion. During your first visit, we discuss your health history and establish some goals that you want to accomplish. We often begin treatment during the first visit and help implement your customized care plan. Contact Elevate Wellness to schedule your appointment today!

headings.text: The Link Between Sitting And Back Pain
How Do Neck And Back Pain Begin?
Stay Healthy While Using A Standing Desk

pages.bodyCopy:
Back pain is one of the most common ailments for adults. Bad posture and improper desks are some of the leading causes of back and neck pain in adults. Alleviating back pain can be difficult when you are constantly putting strain on these muscles and your spine. While the idea of alternating between sitting and standing while working can be appealing, there are some considerations to keep in mind when incorporating a standing desk into your work day.

The Link Between Sitting And Back Pain

Long periods of sitting can put pressure on the spine. Most people who work a desk job begin to slouch or have compressed spinal discs because of this pressure and the weight of gravity. Prolonged sitting can increase the risk of back pain by as much as 50% so any type of movement throughout the day is encouraged to promote normal posture.

Noticing your posture throughout the day while sitting can help alleviate some pressure on your joints and spine. Standing desks are a way to more subconsciously improve your posture instead of constantly focusing on the straightness of your back while working. Standing, taking a walk, and stretching are all great ways to help limit pain while working a sitting job.

Posture Considerations

When switching to a standing desk or implementing some standing during your workday will promote upright posture. Here are some of the benefits that standing desks can provide.

Reduce Slouching

Standing is what promotes a more natural spinal alignment as compared to a slouched position. As gravity pulls our weight down, we tend to bend over or slide down in a chair. While this may feel more comfortable, it is not natural for the spine. Slouching causes neck, back, and hip pain.

Engaging Core Muscles

While standing is more relaxing on the spine, it can become tiring or put pressure on other areas of the body. Your core muscles will be more engaged when you are standing. This can help improve your strength, work ab muscles, improve digestion, and more, but it can also become tiring after a while. Your feet and legs may start to hurt after standing for 8+ hours a day.

Improve Blood Flow

Sitting for your job has been linked to higher blood pressure, increased risk of heart attack, and tight muscles. Standing up, even for just a few hours of the day can help achieve better blood flow to your heart and other muscles. Improved blood flow helps lower your risk of blood clots and other heart issues.

How Do Neck And Back Pain Begin?

The root cause of neck and back pain may not be the chair you are using or the actual act of sitting. Sedentary lifestyles, outside of work can add to your pain and health issues. Even though a standing desk may help to alleviate some back pain, it can put pressure on other parts of your body.

Most neck and back issues are caused by spinal misalignment. Our spines are responsible for communication from the brain to other parts of the body. Slipped disc or spinal misalignment can lead to stiff neck, back pain, muscle weakness, and more.

Stay Healthy While Using A Standing Desk

Standing can also have negative affects on the body. The development of muscle pain and fatigue, especially in your feet, legs, and hips are common complaints when using a standing desk. By not standing correctly, you can also put strain on your ankles and back, exacerbating your lower back issues. Using a combination of standing and sitting desks will help alleviate the pressure on your body. Getting enough exercise and having a proper diet will also help combat the risks of sitting desks.

Chiropractic Services From Elevate Wellness

Since a majority of issues originate in the spine, we suggest chiropractic care for many muscle and joint issues. Elevate Wellness Chiropractic has helped patients of all ages achieve more well rounded health with chiropractic adjustments. Aligning the spine will help your body communicate better and send proper nutrients to the rest of your body. While chiropractic is not a reversal of the effects of sitting desks, it can help give you better movement and energy for a more active lifestyle. Chiropractic can reduce pain, so you have more energy to participate in physical exercise outside of work.

Whether you experience pain, want to be a better athlete, or are pregnant, Elevate Wellness has evidence based treatments for you. Dr. Casey Simmonds has seen first hand how chiropractic can change your life. Reach out to our office and book a consultation today!

When an Ice Pack is Best for Your Injury

Ice Packs, Warm Compresses, and Chiropractic Care
Comprehensive Care for Every Injury at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

pages.bodyCopy:
When you’re dealing with an injury, there are many steps you can take to begin treating your discomfort. While over-the-counter pain medications are a good option for some individuals, they aren’t always the best solution for everyone. Ice packs and warm compresses are great options for those who prefer other therapies to address their discomfort.

However, these two therapies aren’t created equal, and you must understand when an ice pack or warm compress is best. In this blog, we’ll discuss how these therapies aid in injury recovery, which is best for you, and how best to pair them with chiropractic treatment to speed up recovery.

The Importance of Cold Therapies When Treating Injuries

Cold therapies like ice packs are a great way to reduce inflammation and irritation caused by an injury. In most cases, individuals will use ice packs to address inflammation immediately following an injury. Once ice is applied, the blood vessels are constricted, reducing blood flow to the area. As the blood vessels constrict, you’ll notice a reduced swelling that occurs after an injury, also known as edema. While ice packs are the most common cold therapy, some individuals may also take ice baths or use cooling sprays to remedy their injury.

When an Ice Pack is Best for Your Injury

Cold therapies like ice packs are most beneficial for treating new injuries that lead to immediate swelling. If you are dealing with the following injuries, an ice pack may be your best treatment:

Sprained Wrists or Ankles: These sprains are often characterized by immediate swelling, making ice packs best for immediate comfort.

Muscle or Joint Sprains: If you’re experiencing muscle and joint sprains from physical activity, ice packs can help reduce pain and inflammation.

Swollen Limbs: As mentioned above, ice packs are best for treating swelling. Ice is your best treatment if the swollen area is hot to the touch or red.

Headaches: Although headaches aren’t external injuries, utilizing ice packs can reduce the discomfort you’re experiencing.

The Importance of Heat Therapies When Treating Injuries

Although heat therapies may not always be the most popular choice for treating an injury, they are great for aiding recovery. Heat therapies like warm compresses are essential for stimulating blood flow, which can boost nutrient presence near the injury site. Additionally, if you are tense due to your injury, heat therapies can help your muscles loosen up. Tension may otherwise limit blood flow to the area, increasing your recovery time. In addition to warm compresses, hot baths, showers, or warm towels are great, easy-to-use heat therapies.

When a Warm Compress is Best for Your Injury

Warm compresses are a great way to address any muscle tension you may be experiencing, especially after physical impacts like car accidents or sports injuries. If you’re dealing with the following injuries, you should consider using a warm compress:

Muscle Spasms: If used when your muscles are actively spasming, a warm compress can help it relax.

Whiplash: While ice packs are great for addressing whiplash in the immediate aftermath of an accident, heat is a great way to treat any remaining discomfort.

Back Pain: Stiff muscles often cause this discomfort, which heat therapies like warm compresses can quickly remedy.

How to Use Cold and Heat Therapies Safely

While ice packs and warm compresses are great at reducing discomfort following an injury, they can also do more harm if you don’t use them appropriately. Neither of these therapies should be used for any longer than 20 minutes at a time. Additionally, you should provide a buffer between these therapies and your bare skin.

When using heat therapies, don’t use anything warmer than 113°F, as this may result in burns. When using cold therapies, immediately remove the pack if your skin becomes numb or increasingly pale. By using these therapies safely, you should be able to recover from your injury quickly.

Ice Packs, Warm Compresses, and Chiropractic Care

Cold and heat therapies are a great first step towards recovery. However, when used with chiropractic care, you may experience an even faster recovery time. When you schedule an appointment with a trusted chiropractic team, they will perform a comprehensive exam to determine the root cause of your injury and begin crafting a personalized treatment plan. With their spinal decompression therapies, advanced laser technologies, and adjustments, you can trust that you’re on the road to recovery.

Comprehensive Care for Every Injury at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

The first step to recovering from an injury is finding a reliable chiropractic team. At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, our team has provided comprehensive care to patients across the Wasatch Front for years. Whether you’ve recently been in a car accident, experienced a workplace injury, or want to prevent injuries before they occur, we’re here to help you every step of the way.

If you would like to schedule an appointment with our team to help with your at-home treatments, don’t hesitate to contact us today.

headings.text: Recover from Long Flights at Elevate Wellness

pages.bodyCopy:
Long flights can be hard on the body, especially for those who struggle with back pain. Extended periods of sitting, limited space, and less-than-ideal seating can all add up, leading to stiffness, discomfort, and sometimes even injury. Fortunately, with some proactive strategies, you can minimize strain on your spine and protect your back during those long hours in the air.

If you’re about to take a long flight and want to protect your back during the trip, keep reading to see what our team recommends.

1. Choose Your Seat Wisely

Airplanes aren’t known for being the most spacious places, which is why you need to be mindful when picking your seat. If possible, select a seat that provides extra legroom, like those in exit rows or bulkhead seats for a long flight. While upgrading to premium economy or business class isn’t always in the budget, these seats often offer better lumbar support and allow for more movement. Aisle seats are also helpful as they allow you to get up easily to stretch.

2. Pack Supportive Items

As airplane seats become thinner and thinner, it is essential to pack supplementary items to make your trip more comfortable. A lumbar support pillow can be a game-changer for your back. Airplane seats are not designed with spinal support in mind, so bringing a small pillow or a rolled-up blanket to place in the small of your back can help maintain a healthy spinal curve. If you’re prone to neck pain, a supportive neck pillow can relieve strain on your upper spine.

3. Stretch Before Boarding

Sometimes, the best way to protect your spine during a long flight is by taking action before boarding. Stretching before the flight is essential to warm up your muscles and increase flexibility. Focus on stretches that target the hips, hamstrings, and lower back, such as hip flexor stretches, hamstring stretches, and gentle back twists. These stretches will help prevent stiffness from setting in too quickly during the flight.

4. Maintain Good Posture

Poor posture is one of the main culprits behind back pain during flights. But, during a long flight, you might begin to slip out of your traditionally good posture habits. Aim to sit back with your lower spine against the seat to protect your back from irritation throughout the trip. Keep both feet flat on the floor to promote a neutral spine position, and avoid crossing your legs, which can misalign the spine.

5. Get Up and Move Regularly

Movement is key to avoiding back pain. Try to get up and walk around every 45 minutes to an hour if possible. Standing and moving even briefly helps relieve spinal compression, reduce muscle stiffness, and promote better blood circulation. While this might not be a great option for every flight, it is important that you get up during long flights to protect yourself from the stiffness and discomfort that may lead to poor posture and trauma to your spine.

6. Do In-Seat Stretches

If getting up isn’t feasible, in-seat stretches can still help you protect your spine during long flights. Try seated spinal twists, knee-to-chest stretches, and ankle rolls to keep your muscles active. Even small movements can keep your spine mobile and prevent stiffness. However, when doing in-seat stretches, ensure that you are mindful of your neighbors and that you aren’t disrupting their flight.

7. Stay Hydrated

While you might want to enjoy a soda or juice during your flight, it is important that you prioritize drinking water. Hydration is essential for spinal health. Proper hydration helps keep the spinal discs, which act as shock absorbers, well-lubricated. Bring a water bottle onboard if possible and sip regularly to avoid dehydration, which can worsen back pain and cause muscle cramps. When flight attendants offer water, take this opportunity to have a drink as well.

8. Engage Your Core

Your abdominal muscles play a major role in protecting your spine from trauma. Engaging your core muscles while seated can help support your spine throughout a long flight. Tighten your abdominal muscles, and focus on maintaining this engagement for several seconds at a time. This practice helps stabilize your lower back, reducing the strain on your spine. It is a good habit to begin forming before your flight to ensure you can keep it up during your flight.

9. Avoid Heavy Lifting

Lifting heavy bags into the overhead compartment can strain your back, especially if you’re already dealing with discomfort. Use your legs rather than your back to lift, and ask for assistance if needed. Alternatively, consider packing lighter or checking your luggage to ensure you don’t have to lift your luggage overhead. Your back will thank you for this.

10. Consider Pre- and Post-Flight Adjustments

Finally, seeing your chiropractor for a pre-flight adjustment can help ensure your spine is aligned and ready for the long journey ahead. A post-flight adjustment can also relieve any tension or misalignment that develops during travel. Regular chiropractic care helps improve spinal mobility and strength, which is especially beneficial for frequent travelers.

Recover from Long Flights at Elevate Wellness

While long flights can be challenging for your back, these tips will help protect your spine and reduce pain. If you’re preparing for a long trip and are concerned about back pain, consider scheduling a chiropractic appointment with our team at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic in Bountiful, Utah. With years of experience helping patients protect their spines, we’re confident we can do the same for you. If you would like to schedule a pre- or post-flight appointment with our team, don’t hesitate to contact us today.

If you are experiencing back pain, it is highly likely that there is an underlying problem that is causing you pain. Chiropractic treatment can often aid in managing back pain. When you work with our experts at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, you will often be able to minimize back pain and restore your comfort. Here are a few of our tips for managing back pain.

Practice Good Posture

Good posture is essential in preventing weakness and injuries in the spinal area. Posture problems can lead to serious issues with the health of your back. It is important to ensure that you practice good posture throughout the day, both when sitting and when walking. Focusing on strengthening your core can often help you to practice better posture.

Get Active

A sedentary lifestyle often leads to back pain and other health issues. If you have back pain, it can be beneficial to increase the amount of time that you spend exercising. Consult with your care provider prior to substantially changing up your exercise routine. This will enable you to safely increase your exercise without sustaining an injury.

Maintain a Healthy Weight

Extra weight tends to place a great deal of strain on the back. When you shed the extra pounds, you can minimize this strain and prevent injuries. If you are having difficulty managing your back pain, it may be helpful to try to lose some weight and reduce the strain on your back. .

Home Remedies

There are several remedies that can help you to manage back pain and relieve your discomfort. Back pain is often a result of inflammation, so taking anti-inflammatory medications, such as ibuprofen, can help you to relieve your discomfort. Other strategies for managing back pain include using hot compresses or ice packs to help reduce the inflammation in your back.

Chiropractic Care

Chiropractic care is extremely beneficial for managing back pain. When you visit your chiropractor, you will often be able to identify the underlying issue that is resulting in your back pain. Then your chiropractor can create a plan to help you resolve the problem and alleviate your discomfort.

Take up Yoga

There are many ways that yoga can help you manage your back pain. Yoga helps to improve flexibility, which often serves to reduce the likelihood that you will sustain an injury. Taking up yoga can also help to provide stress relief. This will help you to minimize the amount of tension that remains in your back.

Proper Lifting Form

Improper lifting frequently leads to injuries. These injuries will increase the amount of back pain that you experience. Whenever you lift something heavy, you will need to ensure that you are practicing proper form in order to prevent injuries.

Reduce Stress

Stress often translates into tension in your back. This tension can cause discomfort, as well as injuries. When you take steps to reduce your stress, you will be able to minimize back pain and restore your comfort. This can also help to enhance your immune system and provide many additional benefits.

You don’t have to simply grin and bear it when you are experiencing chronic back pain. Our team at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic is here to help. pages.bodyCopy:
Herniated discs can be incredibly uncomfortable and can even lead to substantial permanent damage. When you experience a herniated disc, it will be important to work with an expert to restore the problem. At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, our experts are dedicated to providing the services that are necessary in restoring the health of your spine. Here are a few important things that you should know about herniated discs.

Discs

There are discs all throughout your spine. They range from your neck all the way down through your spine, though herniated discs are more common in the lower back. These discs serve to cushion the bones in the spine in order to prevent damage. This helps protect the spine by absorbing shocks that regularly occur to your spine from daily activities, such as walking or running.

The 2 Components of a Disc

Each disc in your spine consists of two parts, an inner part and an outer part. The inner portion is soft and gelatinous, serving to absorb shock. Then the disc has a tough outer ring to help protect this inner portion.

What are Herniated Discs?

Herniated discs occur when the inner part of the disc is able to protrude through the outer portion, leaving it vulnerable. This may be caused by injury or weakness. A herniated disc tends to result in a substantial amount of pain and discomfort.

Symptoms of Herniated Discs

There are several symptoms of herniated discs that you should be aware of. If you notice these symptoms, you will need to ensure that you receive the appropriate treatment to restore your health. Herniated discs often result in pain and numbness, often on a single side of the body. They may also cause pain that will worsen at night or while you are walking or standing. Herniated discs can cause muscles to weaken inexplicably. They also often result in sensations of tingling, burning, or aching in the affected area.

Common Causes

There are several common causes of herniated discs. Understanding these causes may help you to identify a herniated disc when you experience. Age often enables the outer layer to weaken, which allows the inner portion to protrude through. Certain movements and improper lifting strategies may also cause a herniated disc. Excess weight is another factor that contributes to herniated discs, because the extra weight will place more strain on your spine.

Treatment

The appropriate treatment will depend on your exact situation. Herniated discs can cause permanent nerve damage, so it is important to ensure you have them treated properly. In some cases, a herniated disc can be resolved with effective exercise to strengthen the area, as well as a physical therapy regimen. In more severe cases, surgery may be necessary to fix the herniated disc.

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we offer an array of services to help protect the health of your spine. When you are experiencing pain in your back, you will often benefit from visiting our office for the appropriate diagnosis. To learn more about our chiropractic services, contact us at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic today!

You experience a sharp pain running through your legs. You ask yourself, “Why am I feeling this?” and “Where is this pain coming from?”

In this article, we’ll provide you with some information on sciatica, a potential cause of the pain that you’re feeling. If you’re experiencing pain in your feel, legs, butt and lower back, then this might be due to sciatic nerve pain. We’ll share some ways that a chiropractor can help with this pain.

Keep in mind that while this article provides tips on sciatica, you should go to a licensed and experienced professional for help with this issue. This article should not be used as a substitute for getting help.

Sciatic Nerve Pain (Sciatica) and Its Symptoms

Sciatic nerve pain or sciatica often results in pain in your feet, legs, lower back and bottom. To give you a little more information about how that happens, you have to understand the sciatic nerve in your body. The sciatic nerve is a major nerve that runs through your body. It has 5 different nerves connected to the overall nerve. These 5 nerves makeup the sciatic nerve.

Here are some symptoms of sciatic nerve pain to keep an eye out for:

Aches and pains in your lower body, especially in your legs and back.

Struggling with bodily functions. For example, missing the bathroom when you are experiencing the urgency to urinate. This can also include difficulty with managing bowel movements.

Numbness in your lower body.

Difficult with motor functioning (i.e., you have a hard time walking or moving around).

Traditional Ways of Treating Sciatic Nerve Pain

If you’re experiencing sciatica, you may need different interventions. For example, a first level intervention might be taking medication for your sciatic nerve pain. Other interventions may include no treatment at all. The reason that you might not get any treatment is because sciatica goes away after a few weeks. It’s important to note that it may also return after subsiding. Additionally, it can be very difficult to tolerate while you’re experiencing the pain.

Finally, the last resort might be getting surgery. A lot of people find this method to be invasive. Some people also do not feel comfortable with this method.

How A Chiropractor Can Help With Sciatica

If you’re experiencing sciatic nerve pain, a chiropractor is one way of experimenting with alternative and holistic medicine. For example, a chiropractor will use alternative therapies to help you manage your sciatica.

Experience Less Side Effects and Risks With A Chiropractor

Getting surgery comes with its own risks. It’s also threatening. If you’re thinking of sciatica and how it may go away on its own, getting a surgery also seems unnecessary. Additionally, while taking medications is associated with less risks, medications do have side effects. Some side effects include feeling tired and sleepy. If you’re taking medications like antidepressants which are supposed to help with sciatica, you may also experience weight loss or gain and change in appetite.

But with a chiropractor, you can get the benefits of medicine without having to manage the side effects. For example, your chiropractor may try things like massages and exercises that relieve sciatic nerve pain. What these alternative therapies do is relieve the pain while lowering the costs associated with relieving the pain.

Get Treatment For Sciatica With Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

You shouldn’t have to live with the pain of sciatica. You also shouldn’t have to deal with the side effects and risks associated with traditional treatments of this type of pain.

Get help with sciatic nerve pain in the state of Utah with Elevate Wellness Chiropractic. We can help you using alternative and holistic therapies. Contact us at 801-214-0454. You can also reach out to us to schedule an appointment.

headings.text: Treating Scoliosis in 2 Ways With A Chiropractor
Elevate Wellness–Chiropractic Care Taken To Another Level

pages.bodyCopy:
“I’m really struggling with walking,” You think to yourself. “I wonder if I should see a doctor?”

If you’re struggling with pain when walking or are starting to notice that you’re experiencing difficulty while walking, then it’s time to explore the possibility of having scoliosis. To help you understand what scoliosis is, this article will provide you with some of the key information you should know about this condition. It will also help you figure out what you should do if you suspect that you have scoliosis.

Please note that the information we provide in this article shouldn’t be used in place of professional advice. Please see a chiropractor like those found at Elevate Wellness in order to know if scoliosis is the real issue behind the pain that you’re experiencing.

What is scoliosis?

Scoliosis is when the spine is curved. This curving on the spine happens before puberty occurs. Once the curvature occurs, it usually becomes an issue later on in life. The severe scoliosis ranges from mild to severe cases. Severe cases usually involve some type of surgery so that the spine can be made straighter. According to the American Association of Neurological Surgeons, 2-3% of people in the United States have scoliosis. That’s about six to nine million Americans.

Symptoms of Scoliosis

Signs of Scoliosis range from mild discomfort to extreme pain. Here are signs to keep an eye out for:

You experience difficulty walking. Scoliosis can make walking difficult because of issues due to posture. Lack of correct posture adds to difficulties with walking.

You’re experiencing fatigue.

You’re feeling a lot of pain and body aches

You’re struggling with loss of height. When you’re posture changes due to a curved spine, you experience a loss of height

Your clothes don’t fit well anymore.

These are just some of the issues associated with scoliosis. There are many other signs to keep an eye out for.

Treating Scoliosis in 2 Ways With A Chiropractor

With the help of a chiropractor, you can treat scoliosis. Here are 2 ways that a chiropractor can help you with this condition.

1. A chiropractor can help you with noninvasive methods

In severe cases of scoliosis, an individual is told that they will need to have a surgery where a pulley is placed in their back. This pulley helps straighten out your back. For individuals who don’t want this invasive method, a chiropractor can do a chiropractic adjustment. Chiropractic adjustments help with spinal misalignment (spinal misalignments are a sign of scoliosis). For mild cases of scoliosis where medication is seen as a solution to chronic pain, a chiropractor can try methods that have less side effects. That’s because medications have side effects. But with a chiropractor, you can try different exercises and even massage therapy to help you with your condition.

2. A chiropractor can help you learn techniques you can use on your own

A lot of times, learning techniques to manage scoliosis on your own can help you with this condition. That is, rather than waiting for medications or other methods to help you, a chiropractor can teach you techniques that you can use on your own. The techniques that your chiropractor teaches you will range from simple to complex exercises. Additionally, a chiropractor will go over lifestyle changes that can help you manage your condition.

Elevate Wellness–Chiropractic Care Taken To Another Level

At Elevate Wellness, we can help you with scoliosis and many other conditions. Reach out to us at 801-214-0454 or here. We can help you in a variety of ways–from chiropractic adjustments to massage therapy to lifestyle changes. We look forward to hearing from you!
