What Do You Do If You Think You Have Neuropathy?
How Can A Chiropractor Help Neuropathy?
Do You Want To See A Chiropractor For Neuropathy?

pages.bodyCopy:
Are you experiencing numbness or tingling? What about sharp, burning pain from your extremities? Are your muscles weaker than normal and are you struggling to balance? Chances are, you might be suffering from a condition called neuropathy. Neuropathy is a degenerative nerve condition which causes a lot of pain and numbness in your body. If you have neuropathy, chiropractors can help you.

What Is Neuropathy?

Neuropathy is when the peripheral nervous system, which is the network of nerves outside your brain and spinal cord, has nerves that have been damaged or destroyed. This affects how your nervous system works, disrupting how nerves communicate. It can affect different parts of your body. Neuropathy can be a mild problem or it can be quite severe. Depending on the severity of the neuropathy, symptoms and treatments vary.

What Are The Symptoms Of Neuropathy?

As neuropathy is a condition that affects your nerves, the symptoms you experience relate to what nerves can do. Most commonly, you may experience pain, numbness, tingling, and weakness, in your extremities or wherever the neuropathy is in your body. Your nerves impact your senses, so you may also struggle with sensitive skin, problems balancing, and weakness in your muscles.

What Causes Neuropathy?

There’s no singular reason behind why one might develop neuropathy. There are many underlying causes.

Diabetes. This is the most common cause of neuropathy, with the majority of people who suffer from diabetes complaining of pain and numbness in their extremities.

Nerve Compression Syndrome. This is when there’s direct pressure on a nerve. As such, it can cause neuropathy, typically where the nerve is being compressed.

Chemotherapy. Chemo is hard on your body in many ways, one of which is how it can damage the peripheral nerves.

Aging. About 8% of adults over 65 in the United States reported experiencing neuropathy.

Trauma. Injuries can cause neuropathy in how they hurt your body.

There are many other reasons why neuropathy can develop, including: medications, autoimmune disorders, vascular diseases, inherited disorders, and more. Sometimes, neuropathy can happen with no known cause.

Can You Prevent Neuropathy?

There are actions you can take to reduce your risk of developing neuropathy. Some of which include:

If you have diabetes or any other medical conditions, you can make sure you are communicating with your doctor about any concerns and prevention methods.

If you worry about your medications being a cause, you can also talk that over with your doctor.

In addition, you can do simple methods of injury prevention, like keeping clean floors so that you don’t fall and hurt yourself.

What Do You Do If You Think You Have Neuropathy?

See a doctor! A doctor can run tests to see if you have neuropathy. If you think you may have neuropathy, it is important to get it diagnosed and treated, as it can develop into a serious problem and potentially lead to permanent nerve damage.

How Is Neuropathy Treated?

There are a number of treatments for neuropathy. It’s important to note that while some cases of neuropathy are curable, this isn’t the case for all of them. In the cases in which it can’t be cured, treatment is more so focused on symptom management and damage prevention.

Here are some treatments for neuropathy. Doctors can prescribe medication for the pain. You can have mechanical aids, like braces and splints, to reduce pain by keeping your nerves in alignment. You can try different kinds of therapies, like occupational or physical.

How Can A Chiropractor Help Neuropathy?

Chiropractors specialize in treating problems within alignment. Your central nervous system is within your spine, an area chiropractors know very well. If your body is misaligned, it can lead to nerve problems and pain and numbness. Because your central nervous system is in your spine, if your back isn’t aligned, it can cause problems in your peripheral nerves. Any problems within your central nervous system can lead to other nerve problems, like neuropathy.

So, how can a chiropractor help neuropathy? Chiropractors can help you find the underlying cause of your nerve pain, as well as pain relief. They work to try to treat the condition leading to neuropathy. A chiropractor will also work to prevent the progression of nerve damage.

A chiropractor can provide a natural form of treatment for neuropathy that is non-invasive. They can improve your standard of living in a gentle way. If you’re suffering from neuropathy, you may consider seeing a chiropractor among your treatment options.

Do You Want To See A Chiropractor For Neuropathy?

Here at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we offer chiropractic treatments for neuropathy, as well as other conditions. If you have any questions or would like to set up an appointment, contact us at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic today!

headings.text: What Are The Symptoms Of Whiplash?
How Can A Chiropractor Help Whiplash?

pages.bodyCopy:
We use our necks all the time, so when an injury like whiplash impairs their movement, it affects everything. We can’t easily turn our heads, nod, or anything if our neck is hurt. Luckily, chiropractors can both diagnose and treat whiplash so that your neck is back to normal as soon as possible.

What Is Whiplash?

Whiplash is a neck injury that occurs from a sudden and forceful back and forth movement of the neck, like the lashing of a whip. This motion can injure the bones in your spine, the spinal disks, ligaments, nerves, muscles, and the tissue of your neck. It can also be called a neck sprain or strain, but these terms encompass other types of injuries that aren’t necessarily whiplash.

What Causes Whiplash?

It is most commonly caused by car accidents, with the abrupt change from being in motion to crashing to a stop. It can also result from a number of other things too, though, such as a sports accident, a fall, physical abuse, and a number of other different traumas that can cause this kind of neck movement.

After car accidents, sports are another common cause of whiplash because of the nature of the activity. Collisions resulting from contact sports as well as any number of activities that can cause this movement can lead to whiplash.

Whiplash can result from physical abuse because if you are punched, shaken, pushed, or otherwise hurt by someone else, it can cause your neck to make that forceful back and forth movement of whiplash. Since shaking can be a cause of it, babies can frequently be victim to this, because if people shake their babies, their heads will snap back and forth.

What Are The Symptoms Of Whiplash?

Symptoms of whiplash typically appear within a few days, but in some cases, it can take weeks to notice. Some of the common signs of symptoms of whiplash are as follows:

Neck pain

Stiffness

Soreness

Headaches

Vision problems

Limited movement

Worsening pain with neck movement

Dizziness

Fatigue

Irritability

Difficulty concentrating

Tingling or numbness in the arms

Ringing in the ears

Memory problems

Sleep troubles

Depression

Shoulder pain or tenderness

These are some of the common signs and symptoms of whiplash, but there can be others not listed here. If you’ve suffered an injury that could result in this kind of neck injury, it’s best to seek out help right away in order to avoid complications and to get on the road to recovery as soon as possible.

How Is Whiplash Treated?

Whiplash is treatable and many people find themselves recovering within weeks, so long as they follow their set treatment plans. In some cases, whiplash can result in further injury and chronic pain, though, so it’s important to seek out treatment as soon as possible after the injury.

Depending on the severity of the injury, you may be required to wear a foam collar in order to immobilize your neck. Some people are fine to recover with at home stretches, exercises, and medication, while others require more intensive care including physical therapy.

Treatment generally involves a variety of methods aimed at helping your pain, restoring your neck’s range of motion, and assisting you with getting back to life as normal with no fear of developing chronic pain or complications.

How Can A Chiropractor Help Whiplash?

A chiropractor can treat you in a number of ways. Generally, when you go to a chiropractor, they will conduct a physical examination and ask for information about the injury and your personal history in order to determine both the cause and how best to treat it.

The chiropractor’s goal is to reduce the inflammation in the neck, restore its motion, and reduce your pain through adjustments and exercises that won’t just help you now, but also help to prevent long-term damage.

Chiropractic Treatments For Whiplash

Everyone is different and the causes for their injuries differ, too. This means that what your treatment plans look like will differ from someone else’s because it’s targeted to your personal circumstances. Some of the ways that chiropractors treat whiplash include:

Spinal Manipulation.

Spinal manipulation is aimed at moving the joint back in the way from which it was restricted through the use of chiropractic adjustments.

Muscle Relaxation And Simulation.

This helps to relax tense, tight muscles in order to help it regain mobility.

Exercises

Chiropractors may use a number of different exercises to help regain range of motion and maintain neck stability. These can typically be done both with the chiropractor and at home.

In addition to these treatments, a chiropractor may also employ a number of other methods to treat whiplash. These include: soft tissue therapy, ultrasounds, and interferential electrical stimulation, amongst others. All of these are meant to help stimulate the muscles, reduce inflammation and pain, and restore motion to your neck.

Are You Suffering From Whiplash?

Elevate Wellness can help you with any whiplash injuries. We’ll conduct examinations to find what injuries happened and then personalize a treatment method to you. If you’re suffering from whiplash, we’ll get you feeling better. Contact us at Elevate Wellness today to schedule a consultation or for any questions you may have!

headings.text: Daily Stretching: A Crucial Winter Wellness Tip for Injury Prevention
#4. Don’t Spend Too Much Time Hunched Over
#5. Ensure You Have The Right Outerwear

pages.bodyCopy:
Depending on the kind of person you are, winter is either the best time of the year or the season for hibernating and only going outside when you absolutely have to. Regardless of whether you love or hate it, it’s no secret that winter weather brings with it increased risk for injuries, with the cold and the ice and all. Luckily, we’ve compiled a list of seven helpful winter chiropractic tips to help you keep your body in good condition and avoid injury, no matter if you’re a winter sports fanatic or if you only venture outdoors to go to work and the store and the like.

Daily Stretching: A Crucial Winter Wellness Tip for Injury Prevention

Stretching is often something people just associate with athletes and dancers and very few people stretch on their own. However, stretching is one of the best winter chiropractic tips we can give you because of how everyone can benefit from it. You don’t need to be able to touch your toes or do a split, but simple stretches like child’s pose and downward dog and calf stretches and the like will boost your body’s mobility and flexibility.

When your muscles and joints are stiff, this increases the likelihood of injury, especially when it’s icy or when the cold makes you even stiffer. Regular stretching will loosen your muscles and joints, which is especially important in cold winter weather.

#2. Warm Yourself Up Before Activities

A common mistake people make is trying to jump right into activities like shoveling snow before taking the necessary precautions to warm their bodies up. This is a crucial winter chiropractic tip, regardless of whether you’re a skiing enthusiast or if you just need to shovel your driveway. Warming your body up with stretches and exercises like jumping jacks and squats and a brisk walk will reduce your risk of injury. While this is more commonly known among athletes, if you aren’t sporty, it’s still vital for you to warm yourself up before doing any sort of winter activity!

One of the most common reasons we see new patients during the winter months is due to back pain and other such issues that result from shoveling snow, slipping and falling, and more. While warming up before doing any outdoor activity won’t guarantee that you won’t get hurt, it will make it less likely, which is why this is one of the most frequent winter chiropractic tips chiropractors will give.

#3. Maintain An Exercise Routine

We get it – it’s cold outside, if you try to do anything outdoors, there’s this entire process of bundling up, and if you drive to the gym, you’re risking potentially icy roads and decreased visibility due to snowfall. In spite of this, it’s important to find some way to stay active, for the health benefits and to reduce your risk of injury. You don’t need to log intense cardio workouts or do heavy weights or anything unless you want to. Even taking a walk around the block or going up and down the stairs in your home are a great way to keep active during the cold winter months.

#4. Don’t Spend Too Much Time Hunched Over

People are more likely to be on their phones when they’re spending more time indoors, so for one of our winter chiropractic tips, we recommend trying to limit your screen time, or to be mindful of your posture while you’re on your phone. Many people hunch over and don’t really think about their posture when they’re clicking through social media, but poor posture can result in neck pain, shoulder pain, back pain, and more. Try to remember to sit up straight with your shoulders aligned with your hips and not to constantly have your neck bent over your device.

#5. Ensure You Have The Right Outerwear

A common reason why people slip and fall is because they’re walking in the snow or on ice without the proper footwear. You want to ensure that you have shoes with grippy soles and good traction in order to keep you more stable. It’s not just improper footwear that can cause problems, which is why one of our winter chiropractic tips is to have the right outerwear, which yes, includes your footwear, but also extends to warm sweaters and coats and bottoms and the like. The colder you are, the stiffer you are, which puts you at higher risk of injury.

#6. Be Mindful Of Your Diet

It’s so much easier to stray away from healthy eating in the winter months, with all the holiday treats and the snacks while you’re bored inside and opting for hot chocolate instead of water in order to stay warm. While treats and snacks and hot chocolate are all wonderful in moderation, too much of anything isn’t good for you. While this may not be a winter chiropractic tip you’d expect, chiropractors know how your diet impacts your health and your body’s ability to protect itself and stay in good condition. Indulge in treats, but be mindful of how much you do, and make sure you’re still eating well and staying hydrated with water.

#7. Schedule Regular Chiropractic Visits

By seeing a chiropractor regularly, you’ll set yourself up for success this winter by keeping your body in better condition and through having someone who can help keep your body in alignment and treat pain and other issues that may flare up. We know, we know, you expected this from winter chiropractic tips, but we recommend it because it’s proven to help and will indeed make getting through the winter months safer and easier on your body.

Elevate Wellness offers top notch chiropractic services. With our expertly trained professionals, you can rest assured that you’ll be receiving excellent treatment that is personalized to you and your needs. For more winter chiropractic tips or to set up an appointment, don’t hesitate to contact us today!

pages.metaTitle: Why Chiropractors Call Themselves Doctors Explained
pages.metaDescription: Learn why chiropractors at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic are called doctors. Schedule your appointment in Bountiful or Clinton today!
pages.bodyCopy:
For many people, when they think of doctors, their mind goes to medical doctors, leading them to wonder why chiropractors call themselves doctors if they don’t have medical degrees. While medical doctors are certainly one type of doctor, and among the most commonly known, they are not the only doctors out there. People who get PhDs are doctors, yet many of them do not practice medicine. Chiropractors call themselves doctors because they are – just not in the way you most commonly think.

How Chiropractors Are Doctors

In order to be a medical doctor, you need an M.D. degree, which chiropractors don’t have. You can’t see a chiropractor for many issues you’d see a medical doctor for because they are not trained in how to treat problems, like broken bones and the like. Chiropractors call themselves doctors because they are doctors of chiropractic care, which refers to the practice of utilizing non-invasive adjustments with your hands in order to correct alignment problems and improve how your body functions.

As you may expect, since chiropractors treat the body, they’re required to have in-depth training in order to lawfully practice. This includes:

A Bachelor’s degree with a focus on “pre-med” or the sciences, such as biology, kinesiology, exercise science, human biology, anatomy, and more.

A 4 year healthcare degree from a university or college that is accredited.

A state license that they need to pass a national board exam in order to obtain.

Proven competence with working with patients, generally one year.

Continuing education requirements in order to keep their licenses.

In most states, chiropractors are designated physician-level providers. Many insurances cover chiropractic care, including the U.S. Departments of Veterans Affairs and Defense, Medicaid, Federal Workers’ Compensation, state worker’s compensation programs, and more.

What Chiropractors Can’t Do

Chiropractors have a bit of a bad reputation due to a few bad apples claiming that chiropractors can provide services they simply aren’t qualified for and that their treatments can help issues that science hasn’t proven. Every field has people like this that can smear the public idea of the profession as a whole, unfortunate as it is. It’s a big part of why people are so skeptical over why chiropractors call themselves doctors and ask if chiropractic care is even legitimate.

Chiropractic care is legitimate, but like everything else out there, it has its limitations. If you run into a chiropractor claiming they can do any of the following things, you’ll know that they’re not legitimate and that you should continue your search to find a qualified chiropractor who is legitimate and honest, who you’ll be able to entrust your care to.

Chiropractors cannot:

Prescribe medications. Chiropractic as a whole is a field that is very proud of how its treatments are all natural and non-invasive. Chiropractors will always strive to get to the root of the problem so that you can avoid having to take meds whenever possible. Aside from the nature of the field as a whole, prescription medicine can generally only be prescribed by medical professionals and psychiatrists. While chiropractors are doctors, they’re not medical doctors, so they cannot prescribe medication.

Conduct surgery. You need extensive, specialized training in order to be a surgeon, which chiropractors don’t have. Just because chiropractors call themselves doctors (because they are), doesn’t mean they can treat every health issue out there. Besides, chiropractic care is focused on non-invasive treatments to restore body functions and assist in rehabilitation and strengthening. Surgery is as invasive as it gets!

Treat traumatic injuries. There are many injuries that chiropractors can treat, such as whiplash, back pain, hip pain, and more. They cannot help you with fractures or other such traumatic injuries, although they can help you in the rehabilitation process after a medical doctor has done their part.

Advertise themselves as medical practitioners. This has happened a lot over the course of pandemics in history, which makes the majority of legitimate chiropractors look bad when they’re not. Chiropractic care helps you maintain better overall health, helps you heal faster, and helps you regain strength and mobility – but they cannot claim to be a substitute for medical doctors. When you have chiropractors call themselves doctors, and they’re claiming to be medical doctors, that’s when it simply isn’t true.

What Chiropractors Can Treat

Just because chiropractors can’t treat every problem doesn’t mean that it’s wrong that chiropractors call themselves doctors. They wouldn’t be required to go through such extensive training, be covered by insurances, and be honored as doctors on a state and federal level if they weren’t. Chiropractors can treat a wide array of issues, and many medical doctors will refer you to chiropractors for treatment for ailments such as spinal disk issues and sports injuries and back pain and the like.

In many cases, people find it beneficial to see a chiropractor before they see a medical doctor. This is because since chiropractic care gets to the root of the problem, in many cases, chiropractic care can eliminate the need to take the next step of going to a medical doctor.

Some of the reasons why people see chiropractors are:

Leg pain

Hip pain

Back pain

Neck pain

Muscle tension

Sprains

Pelvic pain

Shoulder pain

Headaches

Alignment problems, like scoliosis

Whiplash

Stress

Sleep problems

Helping align the pelvis for birth

And more

Chiropractors call themselves doctors because they have every right too, with all the specialized knowledge and experience their field necessitates in order to treat people. headings.text: When To See A Chiropractor After A Car Accident
Why See A Chiropractor After A Car Accident?
Do You Need To See A Chiropractor After A Car Accident?

pages.bodyCopy:
An unfortunate reality of today’s world is the commonality of car accidents. Regardless of who was at fault or whether the accident was mild, leaving your car with barely a scratch, or if it was severe, it can be very beneficial to see a chiropractor after a car accident. One of the first things people think of after a car accident is going to the hospital, especially if there are immediately apparent injuries.

What many people don’t realize is how helpful it can be to see a chiropractor after a car accident too, after seeing a doctor. Here’s what you need to know about why it can be helpful to see a chiropractor after a car accident and the issues that chiropractors can help you with.

When To See A Chiropractor After A Car Accident

Of course, one of the first things you should do after being involved in a car accident is to seek medical attention. Even if you don’t feel any pain at the moment, in a few hours, after the adrenaline wears off, you could find that you have injuries you didn’t even realize were there. After seeking medical attention, you should then see a chiropractor, even if you don’t think you’ve sustained any injuries at all.

It’s recommended that you see a chiropractor within three days of the car accident in order to ensure that any injuries, obvious or hidden, that you’ve suffered can be treated as soon as possible. The sooner you seek treatment, the more likely it is that you’ll be able to make a full recovery and be restored to good health.

Why See A Chiropractor After A Car Accident?

Chiropractic care is a key component of recovering from a car accident. There are a number of reasons for this. Here’s what you need to know about the top reasons to see a chiropractor after a car accident.

#1. Diagnosis Of Hidden Injuries

As mentioned above, adrenaline is very deceptive. It’s how our bodies make it through traumatic experiences and what allows them to do things they wouldn’t be able to normally, such as lifting cars in order to free a child trapped under one. However, adrenaline can also hide the signs of injury, making people refuse imminent medical treatment because they mistakenly believe that they’re fine.

The reality is that many injuries, such as whiplash, can take weeks or months to manifest. Visiting a chiropractor sooner rather than later will ensure that your injuries are found, diagnosed, and treated. A chiropractor will be able to conduct an in-depth evaluation that will find signs of any injuries, such as soft tissue damage, whiplash, muscle strain, spinal misalignment, and more.

#2. Immediate Treatment And Diagnosis Matters For Insurance

If you’re working with insurance or an attorney, the sooner you obtain documentation of your injuries, the better for your case. Being able to have your injuries diagnosed and on record right away will minimize the other party’s insurance company trying to claim that the injuries you sustained weren’t related to the crash. This is part of why it’s recommended you see a chiropractor after a car accident, preferably within 72 hours of the fact – not only to get treatment, but also to make things easier for your insurance and attorney.

#3. It Provides Instantaneous Relief

It’s very, very common for people to start to experience aches and pains as soon as immediately after a car accident occurs. These only worsen as time goes by, making it so that you can be incredibly stiff and in a lot of pain the following day. When you see a chiropractor after a car accident, they will be able to help provide instant relief for your stiffness and pains with their adjustments and manipulations and other chiropractic treatments designed to realign your body, alleviate tension, and relax your muscles.

#4. Chiropractors Can Help With A Number Of Injuries

When you’re in a car accident, your body is put under a significant amount of force and pressure that can easily knock it out of alignment. This can result in many different injuries, many of which chiropractors can help with.

Some of the symptoms following car accidents that chiropractors can help with include:

Whiplash

Headaches

Neck pain

Back pain

Shoulder pain

Limited range of motion

Blurred vision

Herniated discs

And more

Do You Need To See A Chiropractor After A Car Accident?

If you’ve suffered a car accident, it’s important to seek out treatment as soon as possible. Elevate Wellness offers professional chiropractic treatments that can help you rehabilitate and get back to life as normal. Contact us to schedule a consultation.

headings.text: Understanding the Different Types of Headaches and Their Causes
How Can Chiropractors Help With Headaches?
Do You Need Our Chiropractors’ Help With Headaches?

pages.bodyCopy:
Every day, millions of people suffer from headaches. They can range in type, causes, and severity, but all headaches affect your quality of life and impact your ability to think clearly and enjoy your day-to-day activities. There are many different treatments out there that people seek out in order to alleviate their pain, including the various ways chiropractors help with headaches. Here is what you need to know about the different types of headaches and how chiropractors help with headaches.

Understanding the Different Types of Headaches and Their Causes

Headaches can be caused by many different conditions and factors, and range in frequency and severity. Most people only have the occasional headache here and there, but some experience excruciating migraines or cluster headaches. How chiropractors help with headaches will depend on your type of headache. They’ll always seek to assess and diagnose your type of headache and any triggers in order to determine the proper treatment method for you.

There are three common types of headaches: tension headaches, cluster headaches, and migraines.

Tension headaches are the most common type of headaches. They’re usually mild to moderate in pain, and aren’t typically considered dangerous by medical professionals. Tension headaches can be either episodic or chronic. They’re episodic if you get them less than 15 days out of the month and chronic if you have them more days than you don’t.

Cluster headaches are rare, but cause extreme pain. They occur in clusters, with each headache lasting 1-3 hours. Their frequency can range from several times a day to every other day, followed by remissions that can last months or years. While not life-threatening, they’re excruciatingly painful.

Migraines cause pulsing sensations or throbbing pain that can be severe, usually accompanied by sensitivity to light and sound and nausea and vomiting. Some people experience auras prior to an attack. Migraines can last anywhere from hours to days at a time.

Causes Of Headaches

There are many different potential causes for headaches. When chiropractors help with headaches, they will always ask you questions about any potential triggers you may have noticed that could have caused the headache. Headaches can be caused by many factors, from your genetics to the foods you eat to muscle tension to a spine out of alignment and more.

In order to ensure chiropractors help with headaches in a way that is beneficial to you, they will always try to find the underlying cause to ensure effective pain management and relief. Some common causes of headaches include:

Muscle tension

Stress

Hormonal changes

Poor posture

Staring at screens for long periods of time

Sleeping too much or too little

Smoking

Dehydration

Alcohol

Fatigue

Eye strain

And many more

How Can Chiropractors Help With Headaches?

The problem many doctors, both medical and chiropractic alike, see with headaches, is that they can cause an increasing dependency on painkillers that get less effective as your body gets used to them, making you need more and more in order to find relief. Unfortunately, trying to relieve headaches can often result in even more headaches due to medication overuse.

This is why it’s so important to understand the cause of your headaches so that you can treat the root cause and avoid potentially making them worse rather than helping them. Chiropractors help with headaches in just that way. When you seek out chiropractors’ help with headaches, they’ll ask about the frequency, severity, and duration of your headaches, and whether anything seems to cause them.

Chiropractors help with headaches by coming up with a treatment plan customized to you and your needs. This can include anything from dietary adjustments to spinal manipulations to chiropractic massage and more. While there’s nothing wrong with painkillers here and there, you don’t want to end up with painkillers worsening your headaches rather than helping them.

Chiropractors help with headaches through providing natural treatment methods that are designed to target the root problem in order to find lasting relief and pain management. For example, if your spine is out of alignment, this limits your neck’s range of motion and can cause problems with your nerves, muscles, and blood supply, which can lead to headaches. By realigning your spine, these problems are resolved and your headaches can be alleviated.

Do You Need Our Chiropractors’ Help With Headaches?

Elevate Wellness offers chiropractic treatments for headaches. We use manual therapy, soft tissue therapy, education about lifestyle changes, and more in order to provide you with lasting relief. Contact us today to schedule a consultation and let us help you find your way to a pain-free life!

headings.text: 5. Slow Down: Essential Tips for Preventing Spring Injuries
#7. Ask For Help When You Need It
#8. Don’t Take On Tasks That Could Strain Areas With Pre-Existing Issues
#9. Don’t Ignore Any Signs Of Pain

pages.bodyCopy:
From spring cleaning to gardening to spring sports, there is no shortage of things to do as the weather warms and flowers start to bloom. Unfortunately, these common spring activities can cause significant back pain and other injuries if you’re not careful. Prevention is key to avoid common spring injuries that can occur from these activities. The last thing you want is for an injury to keep you from enjoying the fresh spring air.

From back pain to shoulder pain to falls, there are many common spring injuries that can be avoided with the proper care. That’s why we’ve compiled this list of things that you can do in order to avoid common spring injuries so you can get the most out of this lovely season. Let’s dive in!

#1. Warm Up Properly

Many people don’t realize how strenuous spring activities like spring cleaning and gardening can be. Warming up isn’t just for those of us who take advantage of this season to hit the mountain trails or take up running again. It’s for everyone who is about to use their body for an extended period of time. Simply warming up your muscles can go a long way to help you avoid common spring injuries.

#2. Wear Proper Shoes

Good shoes are essential to avoid common spring injuries, especially those that occur when running or gardening. You need shoes that will provide you with proper traction, support, and that won’t strain your muscles.

#3. Use Ergonomic Equipment

Spring is the time to get out and start doing yard work and gardening again, but many people don’t realize that they can avoid common spring injuries like back pain simply through using ergonomic tools that fit your body well.

#4. Ensure You Lift Properly

This time of year, we’re lifting a lot. Whether you are spring cleaning and carrying things all around your house or you are gardening and carrying things all over your garden or whatever else, it’s crucial that you use proper lifting techniques to avoid common spring injuries from improper lifting. You want to ensure that you are lifting with your legs, not your back. Bend at your knees, not at your waist, and keep whatever you are lifting close to your body.

Lifting with your back is one of the most common causes of back pain, so simply exercising proper lifting techniques can go a long way to keep you in good condition all spring and year long.

5. Slow Down: Essential Tips for Preventing Spring Injuries

Tempting as it can be to tackle everything that needs to be done at once in order to get it all out of the way, you don’t want to take on too much at once. Slowing it down and doing your spring cleaning bit by bit or increasing the difficulty of your hikes bit by bit gives your body time to adjust to the movement and to recover. Overuse is a common spring injury that is easily avoided by simply slowing down, so you don’t wear out.

#6. Take Breaks

If you’re tired and feel like you need to take a break, take one! Breaks are important in order for your body to avoid common spring injuries that can result from overuse and wear and tear and exhaustion. The seeds that need to be planted will still be there later.

#7. Ask For Help When You Need It

There’s no shame in asking for help, indeed, asking for help when you need it can be one of the easiest ways to avoid common spring injuries that can result from overexertion or from injuries from trying to do something your body either cannot do or cannot do on its own. If you need help lifting something, ask for it. If you cannot reach something, ask if someone else can.

#8. Don’t Take On Tasks That Could Strain Areas With Pre-Existing Issues

If you’re already struggling with issues like shoulder pain and then you try to spend the day weeding your garden, and thus, putting a lot of strain on your shoulders, this is a recipe for disaster and injury.

#9. Don’t Ignore Any Signs Of Pain

A little soreness at the end of a long hike or a day in the garden can make you feel accomplished. But if you feel pain, that’s your body telling you that you’re going too far and that you either need to take a break or stop. Simply listening to your body can help you avoid common spring injuries a great deal.

#10. See A Chiropractor

Chiropractors can help keep your body in good condition by ensuring that it is in alignment. They can improve your range of motion, reduce inflammation, and alleviate pain. Chiropractic care can help keep your body in good condition, so that you are less prone to injury. A great way to avoid common spring injuries is through seeing a chiropractor, so your body is in good condition.

Elevate Wellness can help you avoid common spring injuries with professional chiropractic care. Contact us today to learn more or to set up an appointment.

#6. Do You Often Treat My Condition?
#7. How Long Will My Treatment Last?

Are You Looking For A Chiropractor?

pages.bodyCopy:
When you are trying to find a chiropractor, it’s good to know what questions to ask your chiropractor prior to starting treatment in order to ensure that it’s going to be a good fit. You’re relying on them to provide you with exceptional care to help you feel better, so you want to ensure that you can trust them and that you’ll be able to get the most out of your treatments.

That’s why we’ve compiled this list of questions to ask your chiropractor so that you’re prepared and can help determine whether or not they are the right fit for you. Prior to even calling a chiropractor to set up an appointment, you’ll want to check and see whether or not they are registered. If they aren’t, keep searching, as this means that they are not fit to practice and you are at risk of not receiving good treatment and even being injured if you see them.

That said, once you’ve ensured that the chiropractor you’re considering is registered, here are some questions to ask your chiropractor. A good chiropractor will be happy to answer any questions that you may have; if they aren’t, this is a red flag and a sign that you should continue your search. While this is a good list of questions to ask your chiropractor, it’s always good to have questions of your own prepared, too.

#1. What Are Your Qualifications?

Chiropractors need a Doctor of Chiropractic degree (D.C.) from an accredited school and be licensed in the states they practice in. If they lack either of these things, they are not qualified to practice chiropractic care. Some chiropractors will also complete additional training in order to gain additional knowledge to better treat their patients.

#2. What Is Your Work Experience?

Some people prefer to see chiropractors who have decades of experience under their belts, while others want to see someone younger who is trained in more recent techniques. It’s good to know your chiropractor’s work experience, especially if you’re seeing them for a specific issue, as some may focus more on one kind of issue than another.

#3. Can You Provide References?

Anyone can write their own testimonials on their website. Among the most important questions to ask your chiropractor is whether or not they can provide you with references from real people who have been to their clinic. If your chiropractor is reluctant to provide you with references, this is a red flag and a sign you should continue your search. You can also look on third-party review sites in order to find reviews.

#4. What Techniques Do You Use?

It’s common for chiropractors to specialize in certain chiropractic techniques. It’s good to include a question about that in your list of questions to ask your chiropractor, especially seeing as sometimes, conditions won’t respond to one technique, but will to another. Another of the questions to ask your chiropractor is what technique or techniques they would use for your specific concerns.

#5. What Does A Visit To Your Office Entail?

Different chiropractors have different approaches, and visits to their offices will differ depending on what their appointments are like. It’s always good to know what you’re getting into before you show up, so that you are prepared.

#6. Do You Often Treat My Condition?

You don’t want to see a chiropractor who doesn’t know what to do in order to help you. A chiropractor who is experienced with your condition will be able to provide you with better care, as they know what methods to use and what works in order to help you heal.

#7. How Long Will My Treatment Last?

This is one of the questions to ask your chiropractor that is 2-pronged. For one: if your chiropractor tells you how long your treatment will last before they’ve even seen you, run. Chiropractors need to conduct a detailed evaluation in person in order to determine the best treatment for you. For two: it’s good to have a general idea of how long you can expect to be in treatment.

Everyone is different, and depending on your body and how it responds to treatments, treatment lengths can vary. Your chiropractor should be able to give you a general idea of how long your treatment will last, as well as how they are going to measure your progress.

#8. Will You Provide Preventative Advice To Support My Recovery?

Chiropractors are supposed to help you, but unfortunately, some care more about the money than about actually helping you. Thus, it’s important to include in your questions to ask your chiropractor whether they are going to give you preventative advice in order to keep this condition from occurring again.

A good chiropractor will want to ensure that you heal and that you stay in good health and will happily tell you what you can do in order to avoid injuries.

Are You Looking For A Chiropractor?

pages.metaDescription: We all experience some kind of stress in our day-to-day lives. Chiropractic care can help relieve stress and get you back to full function.
pages.bodyCopy:
All humans experience stress, sometimes multiple times in a day. But if you are experiencing stress over prolonged periods, it can affect your health. The process to relieve stress is not always as simple as taking a break, dealing with stress disorders or anxiety can make it hard to feel like you are in control. While chiropractic treatment can’t cure all problems, there are studies and research that show that consistent treatment by a chiropractor can help reduce and relieve some of your daily stress.

The first step is knowing what causes you stress and what type of stress you are experiencing. Talking with a doctor about what pain you experience, what seems to make it worse, and how you want to feel, will get you on the road to feeling better, faster.

The Three Types Of Stress

Acute- This is the most common type of stress that we experience. This can occur multiple times a day and usually comes on with instances such as getting stuck in traffic, getting pulled over, arguing with a spouse, or giving a speech. This usually develops quickly and can present itself in headaches, stomach pains, or rapid heartbeat.

Episodic Acute Stress- This type of stress occurs when you frequently experience acute stress. Most “Type A” personalities or people who worry a lot are more prone to this type of stress. Experiencing episodic acute stress consistently can lead to depression or heart disease.

Chronic- Chronic stress is stress that persists over time and is constant. This can be harmful to our health and cause symptoms that are debilitating. This can be caused by abuse, poverty, a poor work environment, or dysfunctional marriage. When left untreated, people with chronic stress can develop problems like insomnia, obesity, hypertension, heart disease, and more.

Because stress can present itself in so many different ways, it also may lead to more anxiety and muscle tension. Experiencing stress puts a strain on all parts of your body. Chiropractic treatment works to help move that stress out of your physical body.

Relieve Stress From Muscle Tension

When we become stressed or nervous, we tense up our muscles. When individuals experience high amounts of stress for long periods, these muscles become harder to relax. You may also let yourself sit or stand a different way when you are experiencing stress. Over time, this puts strain on your body and your muscles may send signals to you that you are in pain and need to relieve stress and tension.

Chiropractors adjust your spine and can even work specific muscles to help your body become more balanced and relaxed.

Adjust Posture

Your posture, especially if you sit at a desk all day, can affect your spine and how your body holds tension. Because chiropractic treatment works with the spine, aligning your spine can help you to have better posture, and reduce the amount of pressure put on them.

Chiropractors can also help give you education on how to adjust your posture and what you can do when you work at a computer all day. Getting up to walk or stretch every 30 minutes can help reduce tension in your spine.

Spine Alignment

As your backbone, the spine does a lot of work to help our bodies function every day. When you tense up from stress, your spine begins to move. Chiropractors know where the proper alignment of the spine is and can help your spine be able to communicate properly with the brain. Because our spine helps us function, its proper alignment can help relieve stress, keep us from getting sick as often, and have more energy.

Massage To Help You Relax

While you may not need to go to a licensed chiropractor for this, massage helps the body relax. A massage therapist or a chiropractor can work the knots and tension out of your muscle groups and help reduce the amount of tension you feel. Massage also helps to decrease the stress hormone of cortisol. Massage can help your nervous system come back to a more relaxed state and take it out of flight or fight mode.

Advice For Outside The Office

While patients can not perform adjustments or chiropractic treatment on themselves, there are small ways that you could help alleviate some pain at home. Having a healthy diet and exercise helps your body to release good chemicals and function properly. There is also food that can help reduce stress. If your stress is also affecting your mental health or is connected, seeing a professional therapist may help to put your mind at ease, helping your body to relax as well.

Meditation, spine stretches, and relaxation techniques can also be suggested to help outside of the office. This advice can help you to sleep better and feel more relaxed throughout the day.

Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

Our team at Elevate Wellness wants to help you understand why you are experiencing pain and works to help your body heal naturally. Dealing with pain each day can be exhausting so we work with you to target the specific pain you’re feeling and get you back to better movement.

Stress is common in our world, and should not be taken lightly. We work with patients of all stress levels and help you to relax and feel more present in your body. Dr. Casey Simmonds knows the best treatment for patients of all ages and is certified in Webster’s Technique, an area of prenatal chiropractic care. Simmonds is also a member of the International Chiropractic Pediatric Association and has trained with other doctors in the EPIC Pediatrics group.

We want to help you overcome dysfunction and long-term pain. Functioning as a human can be hard enough without back, neck, or other nerve pain. Visit our office in Bountiful, UT, today and see what we can do for you. Our office is open Monday through Thursday and works with patients from young to old.

pages.title: Changes In The Seasons And The Connection To Pain | Elevate Wellness Chiropractic
pages.metaTitle: Changes In The Seasons And The Connection To Pain | Elevate Wellness Chiropractic
pages.metaDescription: Lower temperatures and changes in the seasons can affect joint pain. Learn more about how seasons affect muscles and joint and how to limit pain.
pages.bodyCopy:
With fall and winter approaching, lower temperatures and fluctuating sunlight can lead to more people experiencing back or joint pain. You may have heard that joints start to hurt when a storm is coming but is that really true? Here are the facts about temperature linked to pain and how the changes in the seasons can affect your pain symptoms.

Barometric Pressure

When someone mentions that they have pain flare-ups before a storm, this often is because of changes in barometric pressure. Studies have yet to find any real correlation between changing temperatures causing pain, but the expanding and contracting of joints in the cold could cause.

Lower temperatures have also been shown to make the liquid in your joints thicker, which leads to your joints and body being stiff and hard to move. While the cooler temperatures may not necessarily cause your pain, they often don’t help.

Another reason that changes in the seasons can affect pain is because our body is more focused on heating lifesaving organs and body parts. Circulation begins to slow to our feet and hands which can be a cause of pain. Less blood flow often means tingling or aching in fingers and toes.

Movement

During the winter, more people tend to stay inside and get less exercise. This could be a contributing factor for those with arthritis or other joint pain. Because you are moving less, your joints get stiff and muscles tend to ache more from lack of movement. Exercise and chiropractic alignment can help your joints move properly and allow them to have more motion during the winter months.

How To Deal With Changes In The Seasons

Living in a place that sees changes in the seasons all year round, it may not be possible to get away from changing pressure and cold temperatures. Places with harsh winters are going to experience cooler temperatures, so it is important to dress warm and layer up if you are going out. There are some solutions and helpful tricks that can help alleviate some of the joint pain you may be experiencing.

1- Get lots of Vitamin D. While there is less light from the sun during the months of fall and winter, your body needs Vitamin D to perform at its best. Taking Vitamin D supplements and getting out in the sun as much as possible can help with aches and pains that come from cooler weather.

2- Stay hydrated. Drinking plenty of water has multiple benefits for your body, including helping minimize the symptoms of pain.

3- Keep up on light exercise. When you are in pain, the last thing you think about is exercise, but moving your body can actually help you feel better and have more energy. Light stretches, walking, or indoor swimming can help keep muscles strong.

4- Stay positive. Seasons don’t last forever and while winter can drag on for a long time, the sun will come back again. Keeping a positive attitude and working to be happy each can stop the pain from ruling your life.

Visit Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

Our chiropractors at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic are trained to treat a variety of injuries and pain symptoms. Whether you have been in a car accident, have damaged joints, or have chronic headaches, chiropractic exercises can help you. For those who experience constant pain, or who play contact sports, treatment is highly suggested.

Chiropractors work to align your spine, which is responsible for helping your body do many tasks. Misalignment of the spine can cause more than just back pain and is often the cause of inflammation. Chiropractic treatment helps the body to get back to healing naturally and eliminates the overuse of medications and helps patients avoid surgery.

If you feel that chiropractic treatment could help your pain through changes in the seasons, contact us today and chat with our doctors. We are here to serve you and work with patients of all ages.

4- Restore Range Of Motion

pages.metaDescription: Experiencing a traumatic brain injury can feel like the end of the world. Chiropractic care can help the symptoms of traumatic brain injuries.
pages.bodyCopy:
A traumatic brain injury or concussion can take years to properly heal, or cause lifelong side effects that will alter the way you function from day to day. There are around 300,000 concussions each year most of which are from sport-related injuries and can often go unreported. Traumatic brain injuries can cause memory loss, epilepsy, and other ailments. Proper chiropractic care can help limit the amount of brain damage you experience and heal your body in a holistic manner. If you have experienced a concussion or other traumatic brain injury, contact Elevate Wellness today to see what we can do for you.

Accidents That Can Cause Brain Injuries

While the most common cause of brain injuries in sports or car accidents, there are other causes that some may not be aware of. Some causes of traumatic brain injuries include:

Serious falls

Firearm-related injuries

Auto accidents

Oxygen deprivation

Near drowning

Infections

Poisoning

Stroke

Tumors

While this list is not exhaustive, these experiences should warrant a visit to a hospital or doctor to ensure that you have not developed a brain injury. Once you have been diagnosed with a traumatic brain injury you may feel hopeless, but chiropractic care has been found to have numerous benefits for those with brain issues.

The Role Of Neuroplasticity

Your brain is built to be flexible and adapt and can benefit from chiropractic care. Your brain can create new neuropathways and have physiological changes from interactions with the environment around you. Neuroplasticity plays a part in the central nervous system and spinal cord injuries and neuropsychiatric disorders.

Brain healing after traumatic brain injuries comes with emotional, psychological, and lifestyle adjustments to help heal you from a traumatic brain injury. Ideal spine alignment and posture do a lot to help heal the mind and body. The brain and nervous system maintain constant communication through cerebrospinal fluid, and when it is off-kilter your brain function is affected. Chiropractic care can help connect your spine and teach your brain a new way of functioning.

The Difference Between WAD And TBI

Often after a car accident, people experience Whiplash-Associated Disorders (WAD) which can feel and look similar to a traumatic brain injury or concussion. Each condition comes with similar symptoms that patients may experience from either a WAD or mild TBI. Chiropractors will need to know the difference between which injury you have in order to best treat you.

Be An Active Participant In Your Care

The best benefit of working with a chiropractor is that you play an active role in your care. Working with multiple doctors or surgeons means you have many medical opinions and often do not know what methods are being used to treat you. Chiropractors discuss your treatment with you through each stage and only perform actions that fit with your recovery goals.

Chiropractic is also a non-invasive technique that can help your body heal from traumatic brain injuries without strong pain medication or surgery. Your spinal cord helps to keep your body communicating effectively and healing naturally. Your treatment will be completely up to you and can be combined with other treatment methods.

Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

During your first visit with us, we will discuss your health history and concerns to best design your treatment. With all of your history and diagnosis, we can create a customized care plan that will improve your condition and limit symptoms.

Dr. Simmonds has worked with many sports-related injuries, car accident symptoms, and patients who just want to feel better about their health. Studies continue to show the benefits of chiropractic care and how it can work to serve more than one purpose. No matter the symptoms you are experiencing, chiropractic adjustment can help. Headaches, injuries, swelling, immune system problems, and more can all be helped by working with a licensed chiropractor.

If you are ready to see the benefits of chiropractic care we can help answer your questions and improve your range of motion and quality of life. Elevate Wellness treats patients of all ages in and outside of Bountiful, UT. Contact our team today!

pages.title: 7 Tips For Maintaining Good Posture | Elevate Wellness Chiropractic
pages.metaTitle: 7 Tips For Maintaining Good Posture | Elevate Wellness Chiropractic
pages.metaDescription: Maintaining good posture takes time and patience. There are exercises you can do to help improve your sitting and standing posture.
pages.bodyCopy:
Creating a habit of maintaining good posture doesn’t happen in a day, but small steps can be taken to help you improve your posture day by day. Chiropractors encourage patients to work on their posture in order to help with back, neck, and leg pain. Stretches, posture ergonomics, and chiropractic treatment can help you stand taller and pain-free.

1- Exercise Regularly

The best way to work on your posture is to have consistent physical activity. Yoga and pilates can help you notice how you already hold your body and show you where you need to work on your balance or stamina. Exercise can help with muscle toning and improve your strength which will help you hold your weight properly.

2- Wear Comfortable Low-Heeled Shoes

Wearing the right shoes during work, exercise, or recreation, will help you maintain good posture and limit other pain points. Support for your legs and feet can prevent pinched nerves, and muscle strains, and will help you maintain good posture. The right shoes help to keep your center of gravity aligned and prevent slouching or unbalanced walking.

3- Talk Walks While At Work

Working at an office job can cause stress on your body and ruin your posture. Keeping a good sitting posture is important while working at a desk, but taking walks at work will help keep your spine in the correct position and prevent hunching over.

While walking, you can work on your walking and standing posture. Picture your head attached to a string and to the ceiling directly above you, keeping your head facing forward and not looking down at the ground. This simple visualization will help with maintaining good posture.

4- Carry Your Bag Correctly

If you constantly carry a backpack or purse, you can maintain good posture by limiting weight in the bag and carrying purses in a cross-body style. This will help distribute the weight evenly and prevent shoulder pain, back pain, or neck pain. It may be hard to avoid carrying a bag, so making sure to distribute the weight and avoid wearing the pack for too long will help maintain good posture.

5- Work On Text Neck

With the constant use of cell phones today, text neck is almost inevitable. The constant looking down causes hunching and affects your posture even after you have stopped looking at your device. Working to improve text neck can start with just moving your phone to more eye level while you are sitting or standing. This will keep your spine in the right position and prevent wear on your muscles.

6- Keep A Healthy Weight

The weight you carry can affect your posture if not balanced correctly. Those who are overweight may have a hard time holding their heads high or may experience pain in their legs and back because of the extra weight. More weight can weaken abdominal the muscles, pelvis, and spine. These weakened points in your body can make maintaining good posture difficult.

7- Be Aware Of Your Posture Throughout The Day

Working to improve your posture starts with being aware of how you are sitting and standing throughout the day. If you are more aware of when your posture starts to slip, you will be able to correct it. Over time, you will not have to think about perfecting your posture, and maintaining good posture will just come naturally.

Forming a habit takes time and practice. While you are working on better posture, it may seem like a lot of work to notice what position your body is in at all times, but once you start to do it, your muscle memory will make it less taxing.

Dr. Simmonds has learned about many functions of the human body and specializes in helping with sports injuries and athletic preparation. Chiropractic care is beneficial for those who are experiencing pain symptoms and those who are not. Chiropractic care provides an alternate route to patients who are candidates for surgery or who want to avoid strong pain medication. Work with our team to improve your daily function with Dr. Simmonds today.

pages.bodyCopy:
For those who have considered becoming a chiropractor, there are some important steps you should take in order to run a proper practice. Chiropractic is the largest natural health profession in the world and is expected to grow 12% by 2026. This step-by-step guide will help you learn about the skills and knowledge you will need to become a chiropractor. Running your own practice, learning about the human body, and improving adults’ range of motion are big draws for future chiropractors.

Chiropractic Education And Training

There are many chiropractic schools that offer hands-on training and help you get into the profession sooner. Many people work on a bachelor’s degree in biology, exercise science, or kinesiology before they apply to chiropractic schools so they have a better understanding of the human body. Most chiropractic schools take about three and a half years to complete or 42,000 instructional hours.

Before becoming a chiropractor you will likely need to complete a clinical internship and pass a series of exams administered by the National Board of Chiropractic Examiners. There are also some programs that will let you complete a bachelor’s degree while simultaneously attending chiropractic school.

Physical Skills

Chiropractors need more than just an educational background to make their practice work. Because chiropractors work with the adult human body most often, it often requires them to be physically fit so they can apply the right amount of pressure on joints and the spine. Having good coordination is also an important physical aspect of becoming a chiropractor because they use their hands and wrists all day.

Interpersonal Skills

Running a health practice means you will need communication, organizational, and decision-making skills. Chiropractors meet with many patients daily who will have questions about their treatment. Communication will help you diagnose problems, help patients trust they are in the right hands, and make running the business side of your practice much easier.

Decision-making skills will help you determine the unique way to treat each patient. Not all bodies are the same so chiropractic treatment will vary between people. This can also help you refer patients to other doctors or chiropractors if needed.

Being presentable, timely, and organized are all other interpersonal skills that will help in becoming a chiropractor. Working with children, teens, and adults can be challenging, but if you show your personality, people will connect with you.

Top Reasons For Becoming A Chiropractor

What are some major reasons why the profession of a chiropractor is becoming more popular?

Not only can chiropractors work in a variety of settings, but they may also be able to open up their own practice. This work flexibility helps you to fill more fulfilled and offers flexibility for people with families or other hobbies.

Becoming a chiropractor will allow you to be your own boss. This gives you more freedom and helps you take on a leadership role while avoiding being micromanaged.

Chiropractors also make a Salary of around $145,000 a year. This is a nice advantage for chiropractors who have spent a long time in school or who are wanting to make a reasonable living in an expensive economy.

The biggest benefit of being in any health profession is helping people to live better lives. Chiropractic is a noninvasive process that helps patients avoid strong medications or surgery that may not work. Becoming a chiropractor helps you heal people naturally and build friendships with your clients. Chiropractors get up close and personal with people every day, so if you are not a people person, becoming a chiropractor may not be the best profession for you.

Meet Our Chiropractor At Elevate Wellness

Dr. Casey Simmonds knows firsthand how chiropractic care can help with injuries and pain points. After a sports injury, he believed he would never be able to play football again. After working with a chiropractor he saw restored motion, reduced inflammation, and better mobility.

While Dr. Simmonds specializes in sports chiropractic, he knows how to help pediatric patients, those who have been in a car accident, and more. Neck pain, back pain, behavioral issues, and more can all be improved by working with our licensed chiropractor. Becoming a chiropractor is not an easy process but it is well worth the time and money.

Elevate Wellness is here to answer any questions you may have about the profession or your treatment. Work towards your health goals with us today!

pages.bodyCopy:
Broken bones or bone fractures can be extremely painful and have many implications on your daily life. While injuries like bone spurs, fractures, bone deterioration and more should be handled by the proper medical professional, it is possible treating broken bones with chiropractic care.

Those with severe breaks may be candidates for surgery and the recovery time for major breaks or fractures can be extensive. If you have a broken bone or have recently had surgery for a broken bone, continue reading this blog to see what Elevate Wellness Chiropractic can do for you.

Minor Side Effects After Chiropractic Adjustment

It is important to note that some patients experience soreness or other side effects after chiropractic treatment. While these adverse effects are minor, they may be more frustrating when you combine broken bones with chiropractic care.

Some side effects after chiropractic include

Headaches

Fatigue

Mild muscle soreness

Nausea

Dizziness

Because chiropractors are working on your neck, spine, and back (in most patients), you may experience some head throbbing or dizziness. This is normal for about a day after your adjustment, but these symptoms should not persist. Working with a professional chiropractor will help align your spine or other parts of your body to help you heal more naturally.

Improving The Healing Process

The biggest benefit of utilizing chiropractic care is the benefit of faster and better healing. Treating broken bones with chiropractic care is possible because when your spine can communicate with the brain clearly, your body better understands what to do to heal your alignments. Your spine is a major component of the nervous system, which helps to limit inflammation. Limiting pain in the body is possible when proper spinal alignment occurs.

Chiropractors will look at your bone density before beginning treatment. They will work to improve your bone strength and thus reduce the risk of future fractures or breaks. Chiropractic can help reduce stiffness in your joints or bones while healing which can result in less pain.

Preventing Spinal Subluxations

If you have spinal subluxations (misaligned discs or separation of the articular surface of the joint) this can make having a broken bone even more painful. Spinal subluxations cause very complex and different muscle pain which can lead to joint pain, hemorrhaging, and excess scar tissue. Chiropractors help with manual stretching and give patients “exercises” to complete at home to limit subluxations. Treating broken bones may look like having surgery to align the broken bone and visiting a chiropractor to help limit swelling and improve the healing process.

Misalignments in the spine can affect how your brain communicates with nerves in your body. Having damaged nerves and muscles around broken bones can make the healing process more painful.

Treating broken bones with chiropractic care doesn’t always mean that a chiropractor will specifically adjust the bone itself. They may be able to help by using other techniques to help bulging discs or spinal miscommunication.

When A Chiropractor Shouldn’t Treat Broken Bones

Not all injuries are created equal and there are times when treating broken bones with chiropractic care is not ideal. If a patient has osteoporosis, it is not suggested to participate in chiropractic adjustment. Arthritis and bone tumors have also been reported to not be positively treated with chiropractic care.

When you have a broken bone, it is best to consider surgery so that your bone can heal properly and limit the risk of breaking again. While chiropractors can help eliminate the need for surgery in some patients it may not be an option for you.

However, chiropractors offer other advice that can be helpful when you have a broken bone. Recommending exercises, stretches, nutrition, and posture adjustments can all be done by a professional chiropractor. All of these practices can help aid you on the road to recovery.

If your other doctors recommend not being adjusted by a chiropractor, you may still visit one to see if they can provide you with alternative advice for healing naturally with stretching or posture adjustment.

Chiropractic With Elevate Wellness

Our chiropractor, Dr. Simmonds, at Elevate Wellness understands the pain that comes with injuries. We all know that dealing with muscle aches, fatigue, whiplash, broken bones, or other ailments can make it difficult to enjoy life. Elevate Wellness Chiropractic is here to help patients who are struggling with a variety of issues and help them heal more naturally. Treating broken bones with chiropractic care is possible at Elevate Wellness.

Chiropractic care is proven to help improve flexibility, range of motion, and need for strong medication, and help patients avoid surgery. Our friendly staff wants to help you in any way we can. Even if you are currently injured or want to improve your body, our experts are here to help! Work with us in Bountiful, UT, today!

pages.bodyCopy:
Most adults want to limit stress and improve their emotional well-being as they age. Chiropractic care can help with more than just physical implications and can actually help with mental stressors. Elevate Wellness has gathered some specific benefits of utilizing chiropractic care for limiting emotional stress.

1- Limiting Stress

As humans functioning in modern society, we see a lot of stress in our daily lives. Commuting to and from work, raising families, dealing with breakups, and maintaining relationships can all cause different amounts of stress. While not all stress is bad, limiting the amount of stress in your life can help you be a more focused and happier person.

Other studies have shown that physical exercise can help release endorphins that eliminate stress. Utilizing multiple tactics to improve your overall health will make daily tasks easier.

2- Anxiety And Depression

For those with mental illness, proper chiropractic treatment can help limit body tension and strained muscles. Chiropractic care can also help your spine communicate with nerves and your brain to improve the chemicals in your brain. Chemicals such as Neurotensin, Oxytocin, and Cortisol can be released during proper chiropractic care which helps eliminate stress and reduce inflammation.

3- Improving Sleep

Getting quality sleep helps to balance your emotional health. Your physical, emotional, and mental health can be improved by getting the right amount of sleep. Not only is it recommended that you get 8 hours of sleep, but quality sleep where you stay asleep is also helpful in limiting emotional stress.

Chiropractic has been shown to make falling asleep easier as well. Falling asleep quickly means you get more sleep and spend less time tossing and turning. Limiting pain in your body will help you get more restful sleep and thus help you have better emotional health.

4- Lower Blood Pressure

Another large benefit for patients is the ability of chiropractic care to lower blood pressure. Recent studies have shown that chiropractic sessions have lowered blood pressure after just 15 minutes. Reducing stress and anxiety can be accomplished through chiropractic manipulation and massage which will in turn help lower blood pressure and make your overall health more stable.

The best thing about chiropractic is that many of these advantages can be obtained all at the same time. During a few appointments, you will start to see better sleep, lower blood pressure, and better production of hormones.

5- Limit Headaches

Emotional stress can often lead to tension headaches or migraines. Chronic headaches limit your ability to do multiple daily activities. Chiropractors treat headaches caused by any factor and provide relief so you can make looking at screens, driving, reading, or other activities easier.

Those with depression, anxiety, OCD, or other mental strain can experience more headaches than others. Having mental stress can affect patients in a big way, so limiting emotional stress and headaches will help take some stress off your shoulders.

6- Better Blood Flow

Proper blood flow is important for your body to regulate tense muscles and give your body the nutrients it needs to function. Improving blood flow will help your body to move freely, stop nerve pain, and take away stress for those with medical anxiety. Spinal manipulations completed by a professional chiropractor will help increase nerve conductivity and improve joint and muscle function.

7- Aid In Relaxation

Massaging and alleviating tension can make your body feel more relaxed. Relaxation is needed for humans to function properly and handle stressful situations. Chiropractic adjustment can help reduce electrical activity in your muscles which can help your mind and body relax. Releasing tension in muscles will improve blood flow and soothe the fight or flight response in your body.

Limiting Emotional Stress With Elevate Wellness

Working with our experienced chiropractors can help you with a variety of issues and injuries. Chiropractic can help prevent further injuries, improve your mental health, and work in limiting emotional stress. Trusting a chiropractor can be scary, but we promise that we will help to make you comfortable and heard while seeking treatment with us.

pages.metaDescription: Getting quality sleep can help limit back pain and illness. If you are wanting to improve your sleep to limit back pain, read below for chiropractic tips.
pages.bodyCopy:
Getting an appropriate amount of sleep and getting quality sleep can help improve your physical and mental health. Proper sleep can help you overcome sickness, alleviate pain, and clear your mind. If you are someone who is constantly experiencing back pain, adjusting your sleep could help limit your symptoms. Improve your sleep habits or your sleeping position to avoid spinal misalignment and back pain.

Elevate Wellness can help adjust your spine to limit back pain while you sleep. Proper sleep positions and proper mattresses can help you avoid misalignment and get deeper sleep.

Find Better Mattresses

The type of mattress that you use can make a difference in your sleep and pain. Having a supportive mattress or one that curves along your body will help to cushion you as you sleep and provide support for your neck, back, and legs. This can help limit the pain by having proper weight distribution and limiting pressure on major pressure points that lead to pain.

Doing some research on the best mattresses for back pain will help you determine what mattress can help with your specific pain. The Sleep Foundation has a list of some of the best mattresses for lumbar support, best for those who sleep on their sides, best for spinal alignment, and more.

Regulating the temperature of your mattress can also help you get better quality sleep. Even if your mattress is not the top-ranked for support, staying asleep and avoiding excess movement and sweating can improve your quality of sleep and thus improve your health.

Different Sleepers Need Supportive Pillows

Using a pillow to elevate your head will improve your sleep and limit back pain. Pillows should be comfortable but also provide needed support for your neck and spine. Going to sleep in pain can make it hard to get some healing and restorative sleep.

If you continue to experience back pain, try searching for a nontraditional pillow and look for one that can support the natural curve of your neck. When a pillow is too high, it can put excess strain on the neck, shoulders, and back.

Sleeping Positions To Limit Back Pain

Different sleeping positions will also help you determine what pillow and mattress are best for you. For back sleepers, a thinner pillow will help provide support while you sleep. While those who sleep on their side may need a firmer or higher pillow.

You can improve your sleep by working on changing your common sleeping positions to more support options. If you are a side sleeper, putting a pillow between your knees and pulling them slightly up to your chest can limit strain on your back. It is best to avoid sleeping on your stomach because it puts the most strain on your lower back. If you do sleep on your stomach, a thick and elevated pillow will help with back pain.

Chiropractic Adjustment For Better Sleep

For patients who experience sleep apnea, snore, or struggle to stay asleep, chiropractic care can help limit your symptoms. Chiropractors can help your spine and body better communicate and circulate nutrients. Chiropractic can help with circulation, which will help sleep apnea patients get more oxygen.

Chiropractors can work to help you limit stress and tension in the body, which will make sleeping more comfortable. Limiting stress in your daily life, doing chiropractic-recommended stretches before bed, and going to your chiropractic appointments will help improve your sleep and stop waking up with back pain.

Improving the central nervous system function, improving blood flow, and relieving muscle tension can all be done by a professional chiropractor. Seeking chiropractic treatment may be the solution to your sleep problems.

Chiropractic Care With Elevate Wellness

Dr. Casey Simmonds wants to help patients sleep better and limit back pain. If you want to improve your sleep, doing what you can at home combined with our chiropractic treatment can limit back, neck, or shoulder pain.

Our Bountiful office looks forward to serving members of our community. We treat whiplash, headaches, back pain, neuropathy, spinal disc injuries, and more! During your first visit, we discuss your health history and what you hope to accomplish with treatment. Doing so helps us to understand what treatments will be most effective for you and determine how many sessions you will need. Contact our office to learn more about what we offer, or head to our website to read more about our treatment methods.
