pages.metaDescription: When do you know you are fully recovered after chiropractic care? Below is more about injuries and their recovery and chiropractic care timeline.
pages.bodyCopy:
Seeing a chiropractor is more often than not, a long-term commitment to keep your body healthy. Some patients see a chiropractor for an injury, while others do it to relieve constant body pain. How do patients know when they are fully recovered and no longer need to seek treatment? When is the right time to cut back on appointments? Elevate Wellness wants our patients to know when their health has improved and how our care can help them throughout their lifetime. This blog will discuss different injuries and what the timeline for chiropractic care looks like for each.

Weekly Or Monthly Chiropractic Appointments

Consistency is key with any health journey or something new if you want to see results. Weekly and monthly chiropractic sessions can help with the most painful conditions and help the most in the long term.

Waiting to seek treatment for pain will lead to body deterioration and the longer you wait to align your spine, the more pain you can experience. Feeling better physically and mentally is possible even just with a few chiropractic sessions. If you are looking to just feel better or improve your immune system, only a few appointments will be needed.

Auto Injuries

Whiplash, broken bones or sore muscles from a car accident can be something that you are fully recovered from. Chiropractic care can help aid in the healing process and make your recovery process much simpler. Depending on what injury you have experienced, you may only need chiropractic adjustment once a week for a few months until you are fully recovered.

Herniated Discs

Patients with herniated discs can see improvement in 1 to 3 sessions every 2 to 4 weeks. Excruciating pain is going to be treated on a case-by-case basis and each person will need different techniques to help.

Back Pain

80% of Americans experience back pain, so seeking medication or stretching for back pain is common. Lower back pain often is treated in 6 to 12 sessions during a 2 to 4-week cycle. After your symptoms have improved, chiropractors may suggest other exercises that you can complete outside of the chiropractic office and may limit the number of sessions you need on a weekly basis. Many patients may not ever consider themselves fully recovered from back pain, but learn to better manage the symptoms.

Migraines

Chiropractic can help limit migraines and find relief without the need for medication. Each case will vary and some chiropractors will use stretching, massage, or a combination of multiple methods and holistic approaches. If you have genetic predispositions to headaches, you may need more chiropractic appointments.

Stages Of Chiropractic Care

After an injury or consistent pain, your spine will need repetitive treatment in order to regain proper alignment. Below are the phases of chiropractic care and how they work to improve your body.

Initial Intensive Care: Intensive care immediately addresses pain and symptoms. This requires frequent chiropractic sessions to help a patient find relief. Spinal adjustments can be combined with other exercises, diet changes, and lifestyle improvements.

Rehabilitative Care: Acute symptoms will need to be reduced before you move into this phase. This is the phase where you will complete healing is possible and your body gains more strength. During the rehabilitative phase, lifestyle changes are even more important to maintain your health and progress.

Wellness Care: This is more of an elective phase in the process and refers to when a patient is completely free of symptoms. Gaining progress during the other two phases is only maintained when you stay conscious about good health.

Recovery With Elevate Wellness

Our team at Elevate Wellness looks forward to improving the health of the community. Improving your body and immune system can be accomplished with a chiropractic adjustment. No matter where you are on your health journey, we are here to help you accomplish your goals and work to make patients feel they are fully recovered.

Even if you don’t currently have symptoms, chiropractic can help you feel more energetic and improve your quality of life. Regular chiropractic care keeps your nervous system in check and helps you to live your best life, pain-free.

pages.metaDescription: When you go to a chiropractor, how do they know where to adjust? Here are the tools and skills that chiropractors use to adjust your spine.

headings.text: 1- The Difference Between Adjustment And Cracking

pages.bodyCopy:
Visiting the chiropractor leads to adjustment, and lining up joints, and may even come with cracking and popping noises as a chiropractor works on your neck, back, and spine. How do chiropractors know where to adjust? How do they know just the right points to limit your pain? In this blog, we will discuss how our chiropractor with Elevate Wellness works to improve your mobility and knows what areas could be leading to your pain. Chiropractors do go through training and education to know how to safely adjust the spine, it is best not to try chiropractic techniques at home without the proper training.

1- The Difference Between Adjustment And Cracking

When you crack or pop your joints at home, you are not fixing the problem. What happens when you hear a crack or pop is you pop a gas bubble in your joints. This only provides relief because it releases endorphins but it only moves your weakest joint.

Although you may feel better for a minute or a couple of days, doing this consistently is not helping subluxations and can actually further damage your body. Cracking your back at home can lead to muscle strain, tears, stretched ligaments, or arthritis. This can make your pain worse or limit your motion even further.

Chiropractors work to identify the subluxations that can lead to pain and will make adjustments that help the weak and stronger joints to work together.

2- Patient Assessment And Manual Therapy

Chiropractors will speak with each patient about what they want help with and ask them questions about their posture, range of motion, and more. Answering these questions will help a chiropractor to know where misalignments are occurring and where to apply pressure when working with you. Chiropractors often adjust on symptoms and what they have learned from schooling or past experience.

Once they are ready to adjust, they use manual therapy which helps to move body joints and the spinal column into its proper order. Doing this and realigning the spine will help limit pain. Controlled pressure will help achieve this and you may hear some cracking or popping.

3- Utilizing X-Rays And Other Scans

Another tool used by chiropractors is x-rays, which can help them look for internal inflammation, bulging discs, scoliosis, or other issues that occur in the spine and bones. Using this tool will help them show you where your pain is originating from, and know where they need to focus to improve your range of motion. X-rays can also help them determine how long you may need to seek treatment and they may give you exercises to complete at home.

Depending on what pain you experiencing or other issues you have, a chiropractor may order an MRI, CT scan, or other external tests to make sure that they can safely treat you. This will help them develop a plan for what areas need the most help and how to move forward.

Chiropractic Adjustment With Elevate Wellness

Elevate Wellness discusses your health history, does X-rays, and uses technology to make sure we make the right adjustments. Doing these steps will ensure that all adjustments and alignments are necessary and do not lead to further pain. We specialize in treating neuropathy, back pain, sports injuries, neck pain, whiplash, headaches, and more. Our chiropractor knows firsthand the benefits that can come from working with a properly trained chiropractor and now helps those in our community have better health. If you are looking to start chiropractic treatment, fill out our contact form here.

Standing knee lifts

Even stretching before you begin exercising can help limber your joints and prevent injury during exercise. Doing stretches before hard exercise and stretches after chiropractic treatment will help limit your pain and muscle tension. Static and dynamic stretches can help you in multiple ways when you are seeking chiropractic treatment including limiting back pain, improving your posture, and boosting your mood.

Some flexibility exercises that you can combine with chiropractic care include:

Standing hamstring stretch

Strengthen Bones And Muscles

When your spine is aligned your bones and muscles work better together and become stronger. When bones function properly, you take away extra stress and discomfort. Strong bones and muscles can help you feel younger and may even help limit pain in certain areas.

Chiropractic care can help your muscles function more systematically and prevent muscle injury. Aligning bones and joints help your brain be able to send signals to them effectively and helps build them up. Boost Your Mood And Self-Esteem

Regular exercise with chiropractic care can help improve your mood and help with mental health as well as physical health. Moving your body in any way can help release endorphins, improve your sleep, and help you recover faster from illness. All of these benefits can make life much more enjoyable and help you feel productive.

Chiropractic adjustments can also release endorphins from aligning your spine. These endorphins can come from pain relieving or reducing inflammation. Combining exercise with chiropractic care will help boost your self-confidence and energy levels throughout the day and give you a better quality of life for years to come.

Elevate Wellness loves to help patients feel better and wants to help them avoid intensive treatment. Working with our office should help you feel seen and improve your understanding of your body.

Exercise With Chiropractic Care With Elevate Wellness

Everyone in our office wants to help patients have a better quality of life. Our chiropractor, Dr. Casey Simmonds, knows firsthand how chiropractic can help after an injury. How Can Chiropractic Help Aid In Digestion?

pages.bodyCopy:
Dealing with digestive issues like irritable bowel syndrome, indigestion, dyspepsia, gas, and abdominal pain can be difficult. Digestive problems can distract you during your work, make it hard to enjoy eating, and may even keep you homebound. Those who struggle with these issues may try multiple medications or doctors to help reduce their symptoms, but one thing they may not consider is working with a chiropractor.

A chiropractor can help manage your stomach problems by improving your spine shape and your joint mobility. We want to share more information about how chiropractic helps with digestion and how it can help those with digestive diseases listed above.

Common Symptoms Of Digestive Problems

Each person will experience different symptoms and react to different foods depending on what digestive issue they have. There are some common symptoms that come with Chrons, IBS, indigestion, etc.

Some common symptoms to watch for can include:

Heartburn

Nausea

Bloating

Going to the bathroom more often than you should

Runny bowel movements

Blood in stool

Difficulty having bowel movements

Severe lack of energy

Noticing cramping in your stomach

Constipation

Gas

Subluxation In The Spine

The slight misalignment of your vertebrae is known as subluxation. If this occurs in certain areas of the spine it can lead to problems like diarrhea and constipation and disrupt the communication between the spine and the digestive system.

Chiropractors focus on improving subluxations and spinal miscommunication so that your entire body can function better. A chiropractic adjustment helps to reduce pressure on the spine and nerves, which can help your brain relay key information to the digestive system. Nerves in the body carry information to the brain that can help your body to process food or drinks. Adjusting your spine or abdominal muscles can help you limit constipation or bloating.

How The Digestive System Is Connected To The Spine

Understanding how your spine is connected to the digestive system may help you feel more open to chiropractic care. Chiropractors are versed in the spinal cord, vertebrae, and back, but these areas can help contribute to other mobility areas of the body.

Your digestive tract gets signals from your spinal cord so that your whole body can work to digest food, and nutrients, and expel unneeded waste. Your body contains nerves from the spine to your digestive system and if signals can not make it all the way to your brain, your digestive system will have a hard time working properly.

Chiropractors can look at the state of your spine and other body systems to see where they can make adjustments. Talking with your chiropractor about your goals and where you are experiencing pain can help you both understand where to adjust and help improve your digestion.

How Can Chiropractic Help Aid In Digestion?

Manual therapy is used by chiropractors to help realign spinal discs, vertebrae, and muscle groups. Your digestive tract can be blocked by misalignment or your body may not be able to absorb certain nutrients because of the misalignment of the spine.

When your chiropractor adjusts your spine, it helps you to digest minerals and vitamins and helps you feel more energized. Chiropractic treatment can help in digestion but it can also give you more energy to exercise and sleep better which can help you feel less bloated or have limited bowel movements.

Chiropractic With Elevate Wellness

Our team at Elevate Wellness can help improve mobility in patients and improve other issues such as headaches, digestion, injuries, and stress. Elevate Wellness and our chiropractor, Dr. Simmonds, can help patients of all ages to gain a better quality of life.

Pregnant women, athletes, and the elderly can all benefit from proper chiropractic care as well. Chiropractic can help your joints move better, prevent injury, and help your brain communicate with all systems clearly.

headings.text: Is Chiropractic Care For Seniors Safe?
How To Continue The Benefits At Home

pages.bodyCopy:
Seeking chiropractic care can be beneficial for people of all ages, but there are always risks when seeking a new healing method. Chiropractic care for seniors does have some significant pros and cons. Chiropractic care for seniors is possible and can help give them a better quality of life.

Many seniors experience back pain (over 6% experience debilitating back pain) so seeking medication or natural healing can be a helpful option. Spinal manipulation is the leading treatment for lower back pain, which can help limit other symptoms seniors experience. Whether seniors want to use chiropractic practices as a complementary method or prevention of future problems, Elevate Wellness can help.

Is Chiropractic Care For Seniors Safe?

The overall answer is, yes. For many different patients, chiropractic care happens weekly without any injury or side effects. Some patients do experience soreness or stronger symptoms of pain during their first few appointments. For seniors, some of these side effects can be debilitating or turn them off from chiropractic care.

Chiropractors are trained and know how to treat different bodily issues in a safe way. Chiropractors are doctors and often only adjust where you tell them to. Talking with your chiropractor about your goals and fears will help you feel more comfortable during your appointment.

Benefits:

Lowering The Risk Of Falls

Chiropractic can help seniors learn stretches and limit subluxations that can lead to better balance and leg strength. Utilizing chiropractic can help limit the risk of falls for seniors that have been falling more recently. Helping to improve posture and balance is a major benefit of chiropractic care for seniors.

Limit Symptoms Of Chronic Conditions

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, Arthritis, Crohn’s Disease, ALS, and Cystic Fibrosis can affect people of all ages, but more elderly people experience chronic conditions. These conditions and more can be improved by utilizing chiropractic care and proper exercise. While chiropractic care and spinal adjustment will not cure these chronic conditions, they can help you or a loved one experience fewer adverse effects or have a better quality of life.

Cons:

Soreness Can Occur

After adjusting muscles or joints that have not been used in a long time, you may experience soreness. For elderly patients, this soreness can be more severe or cause extreme nerve pain. A chiropractor will work to prevent pinched nerves and give you instructions to limit soreness, but this is a potential con of chiropractic care. Especially during the first few appointments.

Bone Fractures Or Breaks

As we age, our bones can become more fragile and susceptible to breaks. Visiting a chiropractor as an elderly person could increase the risk of bone fractures or breaks. While a chiropractor is trained and experienced, there is always a risk when it comes to working with the spine or other fragile areas. For elderly patients with osteoporosis or other bone diseases, it is best to consult with a doctor before seeing a chiropractor.

How To Continue The Benefits At Home

Seeing a chiropractor regularly will help seniors have better mobility, but there are some steps to help them take at home to ensure the benefits carry throughout the week.

Making their home safer can help limit the risk of falls or injury and help them still feel independent in their own home. Clearing the floor of debris or tripping hazards can be a major place to start. It can also be helpful to move around furniture and come up with a more open layout for them to maneuver through.

Some additional things that can help after chiropractic care for seniors include:

Keeping the home well lit

Doing stretches or light exercises in the morning

Wear shoes inside instead of socks and slippers

Put things on lower shelves to avoid strain and step stools

Get plenty of vitamins and sunlight

Chiropractic Care With Elevate Wellness

Dr. Simmonds knows firsthand how chiropractic can help improve your quality of life. Our office wants to help athletes, pregnant mothers, children, and older adults all have the best mobility possible. Whether you have a health condition or just want to prevent pain in later years, chiropractic adjustment can work for you. Call our office in Bountiful, UT to get started! We take most major insurances and our office staff is happy to answer any questions you may have.

headings.text: Tasks That Can Cause Repetitive Motion Injuries
Look For Ways To Modify Tasks
Chiropractic Care From Elevate Wellness For Injuries

pages.bodyCopy:
Working in an office or manufacturing job where you repeat specific tasks or motions multiple times a day, puts you at risk for repetitive motion injuries. Typing, assembling, sewing, or construction workers are all high-risk jobs. Many people in these industries wonder if there are ways to prevent these muscle and tendon strains and avoid excruciating pain. Some exercises can help limit tense muscles while you are at work, but chiropractic care can also help slow the development of these injuries and limit your pain.

Elevate Wellness provides high-quality chiropractic care for a variety of injuries. We can help your body have better alignment and limit inflammation in some regions of the body. Read this blog to learn more about how to prevent repetitive motion injuries while you work.

What Are Repetitive Motion Injuries?

Injuries like Carpal Tunnel, Tendinitis, Bursitis, and Rotator cuff injuries come from repeated motions. Other tasks that can cause these injuries include lifting heavy objects, maintaining bad posture for long periods of time, typing, or packaging items.

These injuries are caused by strained and torn tendons, nerves, and muscles. This causes shooting pains, numbness, and limited mobility in your arms and legs. You may also feel pain in your elbows, knees, fingers, and shoulders.

Tasks That Can Cause Repetitive Motion Injuries

One of the most common jobs that see repetitive motion injuries is an office or typing job. The process of typing, holding the phone, looking down at a computer screen, and bad posture can all lead to RSI’s.

Manufacturers can also develop carpal tunnel or tendinitis by doing the same installation or building motion all day. Drilling, cutting, and shoveling can all cause strained muscles. Doing things over and over can cause built-up tension and something as simple as picking up a pen could throw out your back.

Learn About Proper Work Ergonomics

Developing bad posture while working at a desk or standing in a manufacturing line will lead to pain in multiple areas of your body. One way to limit repetitive motion injuries is to learn proper ergonomics and sitting positions.

Some ways to improve your posture at work include:

Don’t sit with your legs crossed

Take time to stand and move around

Organize your workstation so you don’t have to overreach

Place your monitor at eye level

Use a headset to answer phone calls rather than cradling it between your shoulder and ear

Look For Ways To Modify Tasks

Modifying your typing, assembling, writing, or bending can help you avoid pent-up tension and the need for surgery. Implement proper lifting techniques into your routine or do stretches on your lunch break.

If you are constantly doing the same task at work, look into how you can mix it up, or do a different job for one week. Switch between tasks more often, or look into taking a break from work altogether. Doing so will help limit the early onset of these injuries.

Take Stretch Breaks

Taking breaks from your desk and performing stretches during the day will help you avoid injuries and muscle tension. Wrist stretches, walks, or seated stretches will help keep your muscles strong and avoid strain on muscle groups. Staying in one position for too long can lead to cramps or spinal misalignment.

Stretching before the workday is also a great way to help get your blood flowing and prevent muscle weakness. Doing some yoga or mild stretching before working at a desk or on a production line will help you feel awake and rejuvenated.

Chiropractic Care From Elevate Wellness For Injuries

Our team at Elevate Wellness works to treat a variety of injuries and help limit inflammation in the body. No matter where you are experiencing pain or if you don’t currently have symptoms of any injury, our tested chiropractic methods can help you gain a better quality of life.

Chiropractic is not just for back pain, it can be an excellent tool for many different struggles. Car accidents, repetitive motion injuries, torn muscles, scoliosis, and more can all be made more manageable with the right chiropractic care. If you think that chiropractic is right for you, give us a call and schedule a consultation!

pages.metaDescription: Wondering what the major differences are between chiropractors and physical therapists? Read for more about their practices below!

headings.text: Education Is Required For Both Chiropractors And Physical Therapists
Chiropractors: Focus On Nerves, Vertebrae, and Spinal Cord
Physical Therapists: Focus On Soft Tissue And Muscles

pages.bodyCopy:
For those who experience physical pain or have limited mobility, choosing between chiropractors and physical therapists could be confusing. Each of these manual therapies has its benefits, but they also have differences that can affect their effectiveness for specific patients. Both practices focus on helping patients gain a better quality of life.

Each therapy type is considered holistic healing and can be helpful in helping patients avoid surgery. Learn more about what chiropractors and physical therapists do in this blog.

Chiropractors Focus On Subluxations

Subluxations are partial dislocations in the body. They typically occur in a joint and this is what a majority of people seek chiropractic care for. These dislocations and other misalignments of the body and spine can lead to significant pain.

While many people think that chiropractors just crack backs, there is a lot more that goes into this natural healing process. Chiropractors are knowledgeable about the health of your spine and how to treat it without causing further damage.

The overall goal of chiropractic treatment is to help limit inflammation, help patients better manage pain, and give them a better range of motion.

Education Is Required For Both Chiropractors And Physical Therapists

No matter if you are looking into a chiropractor or a physical therapist, each provider needs education, training, and certifications in order to work with patients. This ensures that they understand bodily anatomy, how the joints and muscles work together, and that they don’t further injure patients.

Chiropractors and physical therapists require a college degree and certifications to practice. In certain states, there may be additional courses or certifications that allow them to work on children or pregnant mothers.

Chiropractors: Focus On Nerves, Vertebrae, and Spinal Cord

Each profession has a different approach to healing. This does not make one better than the other, but depending on your needs, one might be better for your specific situation. Chiropractors focus on your spine and the nervous system that works with your spine. Your body is made up of many interconnected systems, so when one system is blocked or stifled, other parts of your body can suffer as well.

Chiropractors work to limit inflammation that can cause blocks, and align your spine so that your spine can communicate with the brain. They also focus on restoring movement. Because chiropractors have a holistic approach, they also encourage patients to improve their diet and lifestyle while seeking chiropractic treatment.

Spinal Decompression

Chiropractic treatments can be more effective when paired with spinal decompression, especially for spinal disc conditions such as bulging or herniated discs. Spinal decompression therapy, which uses slow, controlled stretching to ease pressure on spinal discs, can even help you avoid the need for surgery.

Non-surgical decompression therapy helps restore the spine to its proper state and releases tension by using a sophisticated machine that calculates the correct amount of force to use by sensing muscle resistance.

Elevate Wellness also offers laser decompression therapy, which uses light energy to penetrate damaged tissue in the muscles and spine, stimulating the body’s natural healing capabilities. By healing inflammation, you may experience a greater range of motion and decreased pain.

Physical Therapists: Focus On Soft Tissue And Muscles

Chiropractors and physical therapists work with their hands, but physical therapists focus more on muscles and soft tissue, rather than systems in the body. They also work to improve mobility but use stretches, exercises, and other mobilization techniques. Many physical therapists use tape, heat, ice, and electric physical aids for their clients.

Physical therapists also help patients to avoid injury in the future. By providing stretching and mobility techniques to people like athletes, their bodies will be better prepared for rigorous activity and can make potential injuries much less severe.

Different Approaches To Treatment

While both chiropractors and physical therapists can use their hands in treatment, physical therapists often rely more on machines or other physical aids during treatment. Each therapy type has developed over time and continues to adopt new practices and tested treatments that they feel can help their patients.

Before you see any chiropractor or physical therapist, make sure to check their credentials and do as much research as possible. This will ensure you get the best treatment for your specific pain.

The two treatment approaches go hand in hand, and you may have to try both before determining which is best for you. Your doctor can help you decide which treatment options are likely to be most effective for your specific condition or symptoms.

Chiropractic With Elevate Wellness

Our chiropractor at Elevate Wellness has seen how chiropractic care can help after an injury. Dr. Casey Simmonds then started his own journey to become a chiropractor and opened his own practice.

In addition to standard chiropractic adjustments, Elevate Wellness offers specialty care in these areas:

Sports Therapy

Close to 90% of athletes utilize chiropractic care to increase performance and treat and prevent injuries. Sports therapy at Elevate Wellness can correct misaligned joints, which helps injuries heal quicker and prevent new injuries from occurring.

Neuropathy Treatment

Neuropathy is a nerve condition that causes numbness and tingling. Unlike medication, which only masks the pain and does not repair the underlying nerve damage, chiropractic adjustments help heal the nerves, leading to greater pain relief.

Prenatal and Pediatric Chiropractic

Chiropractic care can help ease pain caused by changes in the body during pregnancy and help expecting mothers stay comfortable. Additionally, some patients report smoother, shorter labor and delivery processes after receiving spinal and pelvic adjustments.

Infants and children can also benefit from chiropractic care. By making gentle adjustments, chiropractors can help young patients find relief from colic, reflux, digestive issues, or ear infections and can even help regulate their nervous system by making sure their spine is properly aligned.

pages.metaDescription: Wrist pain can get in the way of everyday activities. What should you do if you’re experiencing wrist pain? There are many different treatment options out there, including chiropractic care, to help you get back to normal.
pages.bodyCopy:
Wrist pain can get in the way of lots of everyday activities. Nearly everyone, office and construction workers, athletes, musicians, and crafters, all need healthy, functioning wrist joints to perform their daily activities. So what should you do if you’re experiencing wrist pain? Thankfully, there are many different treatment options out there, including chiropractic care, to help you get back to normal.

Causes

Wrist pain can be caused by many different types of activities or underlying conditions. Here are some of the most common:

Repetitive movement: Repeating the same movements over and over again can cause inflammation or stress fractures. These movements could be everyday activities related to work or hobbies such as typing on a keyboard, playing an instrument, using a screwdriver, knitting, or hitting a baseball.

Rheumatoid arthritis: This condition causes the body’s immune system to attack its own tissues. Wrists are commonly affected in those with rheumatoid arthritis.

Sudden impact: If you fall forward onto your hand, you may sprain, strain, or fracture your wrist. These injuries can also be caused by car accidents.

Carpal tunnel syndrome: This occurs when there’s increased pressure on the median nerve, which runs from the forearm to the palm of the hand. This pressure can be caused by high-force activities such as hammering and may lead to numbness, pain, or weakness in the hand, wrist, or fingers. Previous injury to the wrist increases the risk of developing carpal tunnel syndrome.

Chiropractic Treatments

The type of treatment for wrist pain varies widely depending on its cause. Minor sprains and strains often heal on their own when treated with ice, rest, and over-the-counter pain medication, but other conditions need specialized care from a medical professional. Chiropractic care has been shown to be effective in treating a number of different causes of wrist pain.

Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

Chiropractic care has been useful in treating carpal tunnel syndrome. Chiropractic adjustments can decrease inflammation in the wrist and relieve pressure on the median nerve.

Repetitive Stress Injuries

Patients with injuries caused by repetitive movement can also benefit from chiropractic care. Adjustments can provide relief from pain and discomfort, decrease inflammation, and increase joint flexibility and range of motion as you recover.

Because repetitive stress injuries result in stiffness, soreness, and stress in affected joints, chiropractors may use both manual therapy (joint manipulation) and soft tissue therapy (massage) to relax muscles and release tension.

Rheumatoid Arthritis

If you have wrist pain caused by rheumatoid arthritis, gentle chiropractic techniques may help you find relief; however, manual therapy on active flare-ups should generally be avoided since it can further damage fragile joints.

Even if the chiropractor never directly touches the affected joint, treatment of the surrounding area is still beneficial. For instance, if a patient is experiencing pain due to rheumatoid arthritis in their wrist, they might compensate for lack of range of motion by overusing their elbow, shoulder, or finger joints. Chiropractors can treat those secondary pains, decreasing the patient’s overall level of discomfort.

Additionally, chiropractors can use specialized treatments such as ultrasound waves, electrotherapy, lasers, or infrared saunas to treat rheumatoid arthritis pain.

Other Injuries

Chiropractic care can also help those experiencing wrist pain due to a fracture, sprain, or strain. As you heal, chiropractors can relieve pain and help you regain strength and range of motion. Like in instances where wrist pain is caused by rheumatoid arthritis, these injuries may lead to secondary pain elsewhere in the body, and chiropractors can treat these areas as well.

Prevention

Building bone strength can help prevent wrist fractures. Getting 1,000-1,200 milligrams of calcium a day can help make sure your bones are strong enough to withstand sudden impacts.

The type of gear and equipment you use in your everyday activities can also make a difference. Using protective gear such as wrist guards when doing athletic activities can prevent stress injuries and cushion falls. Ergonomic keyboards and wrist supports help wrists stay in a relaxed, neutral position, making it less likely to develop pain from repetitive movement.

Chiropractic care has also been shown to prevent injuries throughout the body by correcting misaligned joints, which helps injuries heal quicker and prevent new injuries from occurring. Elevate Wellness specializes in sports therapy, which is helpful for anyone looking to prevent future injuries.

Whole-Body Wellness

Elevate Wellness is dedicated to helping patients in the Bountiful, Utah, area achieve their health goals and receive care for their individual needs. If you’re exploring treatment options for pain or injury, consider Elevate Wellness to help you live your best, pain-free life!

headings.text: Chiropractic Care Can Help Your Posture
What Chiropractic Adjustment Can Do For Your Body

pages.bodyCopy:
A commonly searched question about chiropractic treatment is if an adjustment can make you taller. Chiropractors can do a lot to improve your posture, flexibility, and joint function, but can they help you reach your maximum height?

A chiropractic adjustment is known to stretch out your spine, but does that automatically make you taller? Read this blog to learn more about what chiropractic adjustment can do for your body.

How Spinal Adjustments Work

Chiropractors work on adjusting your spine and limiting subluxations. Problems with your spine are also the cause of many pain points in your body and can make other systems in your body malfunction. Chiropractors work to align your spine so that it can communicate with other systems like your digestive system, nervous system, and more.

While spinal adjustment can help you be more flexible, limit joint pain, and help digestion, there is no real evidence to suggest that chiropractic adjustment will make you taller. Your spine may adjust and help lift your shoulders and neck to a better position, but this doesn’t mean you will gain inches.

What Determines A Person’s Height?

Many people know that everyone’s height can vary depending on a few factors. Different families and individual members of the family can have different heights because of genetics. Genetics can play a big role in determining what your final height will be and there is often little you can do to make you taller. Some people grow at different rates as well and may not reach their full height until later in life.

Nutrition is a large part of your overall health, including your growth. Eating the right amount of food and all of your food groups will help you reach your appropriate height. Protein is also essential to growth and ensuring your body and spine can function properly. Vitamins and minerals are also important contributors to height. Vitamin A and Vitamin D can be the most helpful in helping you reach your maximum height.

Chiropractic Care Can Help Your Posture

When your spine is properly aligned and you don’t have back or neck pain, your posture can improve. Some people may believe that standing up straighter or having spinal adjustment makes them taller, but in reality, you already had that height ability. While the help of a chiropractor may make you stand up taller, your height is really predetermined by genetics and diet.

What Chiropractic Adjustment Can Do For Your Body

While spinal adjustment may not be able to make you taller, there are other amazing benefits that you can gain when working with a licensed chiropractor.

One benefit that many may not associate with chiropractic is better digestion. Once your spine can communicate effectively with your brain, all your other bodily systems can better communicate. Improving your digestive system can help with constipation, IBS, or bloating.

Chiropractic care is known for improving flexibility and giving patients an improved range of motion. Limiting inflammation helps your joints and muscles to move more freely, giving you the ability to exercise, reach, garden, or do any other hobby without pain. Improving motion and flexibility is a major benefit for athletes and the elderly.

Chiropractic care can help limit injury while exercising or playing a sport. Limiting subluxations, inflammation, and slipped discs with chiropractic adjustment will prevent further injury from occurring. Even if you do not have any pain symptoms, seeking chiropractic care can lower your risk of injury.

Elevate Wellness

Dr. Simmonds has seen firsthand how chiropractic care can help athletes heal from injury and help other patients have a more fulfilled life. Our office provides friendly service and comprehensive care to patients of all ages and lifestyles. We take pride in being a trusted chiropractic office and helping patients achieve their health goals.

Have questions about what we can do for you? Or just want to learn more about our office? Fill out our contact form to recieve more info!

pages.metaTitle: How Does Diet Affect Chiropractic Treatment? | Elevate Wellness Chiropractic
pages.metaDescription: You may not have considered how your diet can affect the efficacy of chiropractic treatment. Keep reading to discover three ways your diet affects chiropractic care.
pages.bodyCopy:
If you’re receiving chiropractic treatment for an ailment, you want the most effective treatment possible, but may not have considered how your diet can affect the efficacy of chiropractic treatment. Keep reading to discover three ways your diet goes hand in hand with chiropractic care.

Full-Body Health

Chiropractic care is part of whole-body wellness. A good diet and proper nutrition complement chiropractic care and contribute to your overall health. In order to get the most out of your chiropractic treatment and reach your individual health goals, you need to make sure you are paying attention to the foods you eat and how they affect your body.

If you have bad eating habits, your body won’t be able to perform efficiently and you may find yourself feeling sluggish and tired. An improper diet affects your nerves’ ability to share information, your organs’ functionality, and your body’s ability to repair muscle. As a result, your body may begin to break down, exacerbating the issues for which you’re receiving chiropractic treatment.

On the other hand, if you follow proper nutrition guidelines along with receiving chiropractic treatment, your body will have the vitamins and nutrients it needs to function properly and repair itself, increasing the efficacy of the treatment.

Your chiropractor can help you evaluate the foods you eat and give you suggestions on how to improve your overall health through your diet. You may also want to consider consulting with a dietician, since they have specialized knowledge about nutrition and its effects on the body.

Inflammation Reduction

Many physical ailments are caused by inflammation. When your immune system is activated, your body sends out inflammatory cells, which attack bacteria or heal damaged tissue. This is a helpful, necessary bodily function; however, some people experience chronic inflammation, in which the body sends inflammatory cells even when there is no danger.

Chronic inflammation occurs in people who have conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, asthma, heart disease, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer’s disease, autoimmune diseases, and cancer, among others. It can also affect people who smoke or drink alcohol in excess, exercise too much or too little, experience chronic stress, or are obese.

Chiropractic care is known to help relieve inflammation by identifying the root cause of the problem and treating the musculoskeletal system through modalities and adjustments.

In addition, many foods are known to be anti-inflammatory and work in tandem with chiropractic treatment to help you find relief. Including the following foods in your diet will help improve chronic inflammation and complement your chiropractic care:

Leafy greens like spinach and kale

Oily or fatty fish such as salmon, tuna, sardines, and mackerel

Olive oil and coconut oil

Vegetables like tomatoes, avocados, artichokes, red beets, and broccoli sprouts

Fruits such as strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, cherries, pineapple, papaya, grapes, pomegranate, and oranges

Tree nuts such as almonds, cashews, pistachios, walnuts, and Brazil nuts

Foods high in fiber such as quinoa, ground flaxseed, and oatmeal

Herbs and spices like turmeric, ginger, rosemary, and garlic

Greek yogurt

Green tea and matcha tea

If reducing inflammation is your goal, you should steer clear of these foods:

Refined carbohydrates (found in white flour, white bread, and white rice)

Processed meats such as bacon, hot dogs, and cold cuts

Full-fat dairy

Baked goods

Sweetened beverages like soda, hot chocolate, and coffee

Trans fats or partially hydrogenated oils (found in margarine, shortening, fried foods, and processed snacks)

Healthy Bones and Joints

Many people seek chiropractic care for issues with bone and joint health. People with poor posture, aching joints, broken or fractured bones, or even conditions such as osteoporosis or osteoarthritis can all benefit from chiropractic treatment.

Your diet also affects your bones and joints. Eating too many fatty foods with lots of calories can cause you to gain weight, which puts stress on your joints. This extra stress can lead to wear and tear in your bones, cartilage, tendons, and ligaments, causing pain and stiffness, which exacerbates the need for chiropractic care.

In addition to chiropractic treatment, in order to strengthen your bones and joints, you can make sure you get enough calcium, potassium, magnesium, and antioxidants while avoiding foods that will cause weight gain.

Chiropractic Care From Elevate Wellness

At Elevate Wellness, we help patients find relief from lower back pain, migraines and headaches, sciatica, neck pain and whiplash, neuropathy, spinal disc injuries, sports injuries, and more. We are proud to use cutting-edge technology and proven techniques to restore the body to its proper form and function. If you think chiropractic care can help you, schedule an appointment today. We can’t wait to see you!

pages.metaTitle: Chiropractic Care to Combat Sedentary Lifestyle Effects
pages.metaDescription: Elevate Wellness Chiropractic: Combat sedentary lifestyle effects with personalized care. Schedule your appointment today for improved posture and pain relief!
pages.bodyCopy:
In today’s modern world, we spend a lot of time sitting, whether it be in the car, at our desks at work, or in front of the TV at home. Modern technology has made our lives a lot easier and more convenient, but all of that rest can take a toll on a person’s health. However, there is hope for those who suffer from the effects of a sedentary lifestyle in the form of chiropractic care.

Understanding Sedentary Lifestyles

Studies have shown that the average person sits for around eight hours a day. This doesn’t necessarily mean people who live sedentary lifestyles are lazy or unmotivated; often, people’s jobs necessitate long amounts of time spent sitting at a desk or behind the wheel of a car.

Sedentary lifestyles, also known as “sitting disease,” are linked to a number of different health conditions, including obesity, diabetes, high blood pressure, and unhealthy cholesterol levels. Additionally, sedentary lifestyles can cause musculoskeletal issues, including tight hip flexors, lower back pain, and weak posture.

The Role of Chiropractic Care

Chiropractic care aims to improve an individual’s whole-body health through holistic methods and focuses on the relationship between the spine and the nervous system. Chiropractors use adjustments and modulations to correct misalignments in the body resulting from sedentary habits. By correcting these misalignments, chiropractors can relieve pain, restore proper nerve function, and improve overall health.

Addressing Postural Imbalances

Good posture has a number of benefits to overall health. Improving one’s posture reduces back pain and increases one’s confidence and energy levels. On the other hand, those with incorrect posture experience muscle tension, pain, and fatigue.

Individuals who live sedentary lifestyles often have imbalances in their posture. Constantly hunching over a desk, laptop, or phone can result in rounded shoulders, weak core muscles, and forward head posture. Chiropractors have the skills and training necessary to identify and correct these problems, relieving patients’ pain and enhancing the body’s natural ability to heal itself.

Alleviating Back and Neck Pain

Because improper sitting posture can put extra strain on the spine and surrounding muscles, back and neck pain are other common issues among those who live sedentary lives. Chiropractors are able to pinpoint the root cause of this pain and use targeted adjustments to restore proper alignment in the spine.

Promoting Spinal Health

Chiropractic care isn’t just useful for acute incidents. Regular chiropractic adjustments are a good idea for anyone, especially those who live sedentary lifestyles. Maintaining optimal spinal health can prevent serious spinal conditions from developing and decrease the risk of pain and disability.

Complementary Wellness Strategies

In addition to chiropractic care, individuals suffering from the negative effects of a sedentary lifestyle may benefit from complementary wellness strategies. Chiropractors can recommend exercises that work in conjunction with chiropractic adjustments to improve patients’ overall quality of life.

These complementary strategies may include exercises to strengthen the core, stretches to improve flexibility and relieve tightness, ergonomic devices for one’s desk, and lifestyle modifications to incorporate more movement into one’s daily routines.

To live a healthier lifestyle, try these simple tips:

When sitting for long periods of time, take a break and stand every 30 minutes.

While watching television, playing video games, or using your phone, stand instead of sitting.

If possible, use a standing desk for work. Additionally, you can place a small treadmill under your desk so you can exercise while you work.

Living a sedentary lifestyle can pose a significant threat to one’s health, wellness, and happiness. However, there are many steps people can take to be proactive about their health and limit these negative effects. Chiropractic care, in conjunction with lifestyle changes, exercises, and stretches, can make a big difference in the lives of individuals who spend a significant amount of time sitting or lying down.

If you’re struggling with postural imbalances, musculoskeletal pain, muscle weakness or tightness, or poor overall health due to a sedentary lifestyle, reach out to the professional team at Elevate Wellness. We treat patients of all ages who suffer from migraines and headaches, sciatica, whiplash, neuropathy, auto injuries, and sports injuries, empowering them to live more active, pain-free lives and restoring their vitality.

Proactivity is the best strategy when it comes to combating the issues that sedentary lifestyles can cause. Schedule an appointment at Elevate Wellness today before your problems have a chance to escalate. It’s never too late to make positive changes for a healthier future!

headings.text: Nerve Pain Treatment at Elevate Wellness

pages.bodyCopy:
Nerve pain, also known as neuropathic pain, happens when your nervous system is malfunctioning, either due to nerve damage or other health conditions. Nerve pain can be difficult to diagnose and treat since there are many possible causes. Luckily, people who suffer from nerve pain can find relief through many different treatment options, including chiropractic care.

Understanding Nerve Pain: Definition & Overview

The nervous system has two different components: the central nervous system and the peripheral nervous system. The central nervous system includes the brain and the spinal cord, while the peripheral nervous system comprises all the nerves that spread throughout the rest of the body and into the extremities.

The nervous system is responsible for sending signals throughout the body. When it’s not working correctly or has sustained damage, nerves send the wrong signals to the brain, causing nerve pain.

Symptoms

Nerve pain can be spontaneous, meaning it comes without stimulation. It can feel like a shooting, stabbing, or burning pain; numbness, tingling, or a pins-and-needles feeling may also occur.

Neuropathic pain can also include evoked pain, which is brought on by normally non-painful stimuli including gentle brushing or pressure against the skin. Evoked pain may also mean normally painful stimuli, such as heat or pinpricks, are even more painful.

People with nerve pain may also have trouble sleeping and emotional problems caused by lack of sleep and pain.

Causes

In order to figure out the cause of nerve pain, your healthcare provider will go over your medical history and perform a physical exam in order to find the underlying issue and trace the symptoms.

About 30 percent of all neuropathic pain is caused by diabetes, but there are many other medical conditions and other factors that can cause nerve pain, including:

Alcoholism

HIV infection or AIDS

Disorders affecting the central nervous system including stroke, Parkinson’s disease, and multiple sclerosis (MS)

Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS)

Shingles

Chemotherapy and radiation therapy

Amputation, which can cause phantom pain

Spinal nerve inflammation or compression

Trauma or surgeries with resulting nerve damage

Nerve compression by tumors

Treatment

When treating nerve pain, the goals are to provide pain relief, maintain functionality, and improve the quality of life for the patient along with treating the underlying disease causing the pain. Usually, multimodal therapy, which includes medications, psychological counseling, physical therapy, and sometimes surgery, is needed to treat nerve pain.

Topical treatments like patches, ointments, or creams that contain capsaicin or lidocaine can relieve nerve pain. Opioid analgesics, however, are less effective in treating neuropathic pain, and their negative effects may prevent long-term use.

Nerve blocks given by pain specialists can also relieve neuropathic pain. These treatments include the injection of steroids or anesthetics into the affected nerves.

If nerve pain has not responded to these treatments, spinal cord stimulation, brain stimulation, and peripheral nerve stimulation might help.

Chiropractic Care

Additionally, some causes of nerve pain, including pinched nerves, sciatica, and neuropathy, can be treated with chiropractic care.

Pinched nerves occur when too much pressure is applied to a nerve by surrounding cartilage, bones, tendons, or muscles. With sciatica, the sciatic nerve in the lower back is compressed by a herniated disk or bone spur on the spine. Chiropractic treatment can ease some of the pressure on the nerve, therefore decreasing neuropathic pain.

Prevention

The best way to prevent neuropathic pain is to manage medical conditions that increase your risk of developing it. The details of prevention depend on the specific condition you have, but in general, the following actions help promote nerve health:

Eat lots of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean protein. Ensure you get enough vitamin B-12 by eating meats, eggs, fish, low-fat dairy products, and fortified cereals.

Exercise regularly (with permission from your doctor). At least 30 minutes of exercise three times per week is a good rule of thumb.

Avoid factors that may cause nerve damage, including smoking, repetitive motions, exposure to toxic chemicals, and excessive alcohol use.

Nerve Pain Treatment at Elevate Wellness

At Elevate Wellness, we provide comprehensive chiropractic care for all kinds of musculoskeletal issues, not just nerve pain. If you have lower back pain, headaches or migraines, neck pain or whiplash, injuries related to an auto accident, or sports injuries, we can help you find relief through a personalized care plan and get you back to normal. To schedule an appointment, contact us online or call our office in Bountiful, Utah. We can’t wait to help relieve your pain and improve your quality of life!

pages.bodyCopy:
In the age of the internet, there’s a lot of readily-accessible information out there about chiropractic care. Unfortunately, there’s a lot of misinformation, too, making it easy to get confused about what exactly chiropractic care entails and whether or not it’s right for you. If you want to know the truth about chiropractic care, keep reading to debunk some myths and shed light on the true benefits of chiropractic care.

Myth #1: Chiropractic Care is Painful

With all the videos of chiropractors popping people’s joints and cracking their backs that have been circulating around social media recently, it can be easy to assume that chiropractic care is painful. After all, some of the adjustments can look kind of intense, and the popping noises can be anxiety-inducing.

Despite how it may look, the truth is that chiropractic care actually relieves pain by using gentle, controlled techniques to realign the body’s musculoskeletal system. Any discomfort felt during the process should be minimal and only last for a short time.

Myth #2: Chiropractic Adjustments are Dangerous

One of the most common myths about chiropractic care is that it is dangerous. People love to circulate stories about how chiropractic adjustments can break people’s bones or dislocate their joints. If you’ve never had an adjustment, you might be wary of some of the equipment, tools, and techniques chiropractors use and may have a hard time trusting them to manipulate your body in such a hands-on way.

The truth is that chiropractors undergo rigorous training and education in order to perform safe, effective adjustments for their patients. Because chiropractic treatment is non-invasive and drug-free, it can actually be a safer alternative to other treatment options such as surgery or heavy medication, which can come with complications or negative side effects.

Myth #3: Once You Start, You Can’t Stop

Many people think that once you start receiving chiropractic care, you’ll have to keep going forever in order to achieve long-lasting results. In reality, the frequency and duration of chiropractic treatment depend on many different factors, including the end goals of treatment, the parts of the body affected, the patient’s overall health, and how the body responds to treatment.

In addition to providing chiropractic adjustments, chiropractors develop an individualized treatment plan that includes nutrition, at-home exercises, stretches, and lifestyle recommendations to empower patients to take control of their health. The ultimate goal of chiropractic care is to improve the patient’s life and provide long-term relief, not create dependency.

Myth #4: Chiropractors Aren’t Real Doctors

You’ve probably heard people talk about how chiropractors are not real doctors. However, just because they don’t practice traditional medicine doesn’t mean that they are not qualified medical professionals with extensive training.

In order to become a chiropractor, one must complete training similar to that of medical doctors, including a four-year doctoral program that covers nutrition, physiology, radiology, anatomy, and more. Like other healthcare providers, chiropractors are licensed and regulated to ensure they provide safe, effective care and meet high standards of quality and professionalism. As long as you choose a chiropractor with the proper training and education, you can be sure that your health is in good, capable hands.

Myth #5: Chiropractic Care is Only for Back Pain

Because chiropractic adjustments often focus on the spine, you may think that chiropractic care is only used to treat back pain. In reality, the scope of this treatment goes far beyond the back and extends to all parts of the body. Chiropractors can address many different musculoskeletal issues, including neck pain, headaches, sciatica, joint pain, sports injuries, and even conditions like fibromyalgia and arthritis.

Because the spinal cord sends signals to the brain and throughout the body, adjustments in the spine can affect any part of the body. Chiropractors are trained to know exactly how to manipulate the spine to achieve the desired results in other parts of the body, not just the musculoskeletal system. Chiropractic care is known to relieve constipation, improve organ function, aid proper digestion, increase energy, improve quality of sleep, increase flexibility, and regulate heart rate and breathing.

The reality is that chiropractic care affects the whole body, and the ultimate goal of treatment is to improve patients’ lives by improving their overall health and well-being.

Improve Your Health With Care from Elevate Wellness

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, all our team members are highly qualified to provide chiropractic care and help improve your quality of life. If you want to discover for yourself the benefits of chiropractic care, schedule an appointment with us today!

pages.bodyCopy:
There’s no doubt that technology is a big part of our daily lives. From smartphones to computers to tablets to gaming consoles, we are constantly looking at screens. Although these technological advancements make life easier and increase convenience, they can also have detrimental effects on our health.

One of the most common issues caused by technology is neck pain, commonly referred to as “tech neck.” In this blog post, we’ll cover the causes of tech neck, its impact on health, chiropractic solutions to reduce pain, and ways to prevent tech neck.

Understanding Tech Neck

The term “tech neck” encompasses the pain, discomfort, and postural issues associated with the prolonged use of electronic devices such as computers, tablets, and smartphones. When using these devices, your posture tends to be less-than-optimal, with slouched shoulders, a forward head posture, and a rounded upper back. This position puts strain on the upper spine and neck, which can lead to a range of different musculoskeletal issues.

Why Does Tech Neck Happen?

Prolonged screen time and the poor ergonomic habits that accompany it are the main culprits that cause tech neck. The time we spend hunched over our screens has increased significantly in recent years due to the prevalence of remote work, online learning, and mindless scrolling through social media.

This excessive screen time, combined with decreased postural awareness, can contribute to spinal misalignments and muscular imbalances, which puts unnecessary strain on the upper back, shoulders, and neck.

Impact on Health

The consequences of tech neck go beyond just neck pain, tension, and discomfort. Poor posture can lead to a number of health issues, including:

Muscular imbalances: Prolonged strain can cause muscles in the neck and upper back to become weak or tight, which can cause pain and lead to restricted movement.

Headaches: When you have a forward head posture, the muscles in the neck and shoulders become overworked, leading to tension headaches.

Reduced lung capacity: Believe it or not, poor posture can compress your chest, which restricts lung expansion and may affect your breathing.

Spinal misalignments: Over time, poor posture can cause your spine to gradually shift out of alignment, leading to more severe issues over time.

Degeneration: Chronic poor posture can lead to degenerative issues in the spine, such as arthritis.

Chiropractic Solutions

If you’re experiencing the effects of tech neck, you may want to consider chiropractic care to help you find some relief. Because they are trained to identify spinal misalignments, muscular imbalances, and postural issues, chiropractors can offer you a holistic, comprehensive approach to treating tech neck and other associated problems.

Spinal adjustments: In order to reduce tension and improve your overall posture, chiropractors can perform spinal adjustments, restoring proper alignment to the spine.

Muscle relaxation techniques: To improve flexibility and alleviate muscle tension, chiropractors use various techniques such as massage therapy and targeted stretching.

Postural education: When it comes to reducing the negative effects of tech neck, knowledge is power. Your chiropractor can provide education regarding proper ergonomics and posture to minimize strain while you use your electronic devices.

Customized treatment plans: Because each patient’s needs are unique, the key to effective chiropractic care is a customized treatment plan designed to treat their individual symptoms. Your chiropractor will create an individualized plan to address your specific concerns and promote long-term wellness.

Preventing Tech Neck

While chiropractic care can do a lot to alleviate the symptoms of tech neck, prevention also goes a long way. If your job or lifestyle involves a lot of screen time, try these tips to stop tech neck before it can start:

Ergonomics: Ergonomics refers to the relationship between physical objects and the comfort and efficiency they provide, especially in the workplace. If you work in an office environment, set up your workspace in a manner that encourages proper posture. Keep screens at eye level and consider investing in ergonomic products like chairs and keyboard stands that are designed to provide comfort and ease of use.

Take breaks: It’s easy to get sucked into your work and forget to take breaks. However, incorporating regular breaks from screen time into your routine can relieve tension. Make sure you stand up, stretch, and walk around every once in a while.

Exercise regularly: Regular exercise, including strengthening the neck, back, and core, helps support better posture.

Mindful device use: When using your devices, be mindful of your posture. Lift your screens to eye level instead of hunching over to look down at them.

Comprehensive Chiropractic Care

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we offer comprehensive chiropractic care for many issues, including tech neck. If you want to achieve relief from the effects of tech neck, schedule an appointment with us today.

headings.text: 5 Ways Chiropractic Care Can Complement Traditional Medicine

pages.bodyCopy:
The world of healthcare is constantly evolving and expanding, making it difficult sometimes to find the right path to wellness. Historically, traditional medicine has been the cornerstone of healthcare, offering treatments deeply rooted in scientific research and evidence-based practices. However, there is a growing recognition of a more holistic approach to healthcare that encompasses complementary solutions like chiropractic care. These therapies complement traditional medicine and can play a vital role in enhancing overall well-being.

Understanding the Holistic Approach

Rather than addressing isolated symptoms, the holistic approach to health and wellness focuses on treating the root cause of these symptoms and taking care of the whole person, mind, body, and soul. This philosophy takes into consideration the connections between different aspects of well-being and aims to achieve optimal health by providing balance and harmony within the body.

Chiropractic care is an integral part of the holistic approach and centers around the idea that the body’s musculoskeletal structure, especially the spine, has a significant effect on the body’s overall function. According to the chiropractic philosophy, misalignments or subluxations in the spine can disrupt the body’s natural balance, leading to a variety of health issues. By employing hands-on techniques to adjust the body, chiropractors aim to restore proper alignment and allow the body to heal itself.

5 Ways Chiropractic Care Can Complement Traditional Medicine

Patients with certain conditions may benefit from a multifaceted approach to treatment. When utilized in combination with traditional medicine, chiropractic care can provide enhanced healing and symptom relief.

#1. Pain Management

Chronic pain is a complex issue that is often addressed through medication and surgical intervention. Chiropractic care is a non-invasive alternative to these traditional treatment methods. Chiropractors focus on the root cause of pain, and by realigning the spine and addressing muscular imbalances, they can alleviate discomfort and improve patients’ overall mobility.

#2. Enhanced Healing

After sustaining an injury or undergoing surgery, the body’s natural healing processes are incredibly important. Chiropractic adjustments can facilitate these processes by improving blood flow and nerve function, and when used alongside other medical treatments, it can contribute to faster recovery times.

#3. Stress Reduction

Life is full of stressors, from work to family to everyday responsibilities. Stress has a profound impact on both physical and mental well-being, and although some levels of stress may be unavoidable, there are things you can do to help you manage stressors and alleviate their negative effects. Traditional medicine typically utilizes medication and counseling to address stress. To work in tandem with these treatments and enhance their benefits, chiropractic care can help reduce stress through adjustments that promote relaxation, release tension, and improve circulation.

#4. Improved Immune Function

To fight off illnesses, prevent infections, and maintain good health, a strong immune system is key. Chiropractic care is known to have a positive impact on the immune system by removing causes of interference in the nervous system, allowing the body’s defense mechanisms to function properly.

#5. Long-Term Wellness

The holistic approach to medicine emphasizes prevention and long-term wellness. By incorporating chiropractic care into their wellness routine, individuals can proactively manage their spinal alignment and overall health, reducing the likelihood of future health issues.

Collaboration for Comprehensive Care

As the world of healthcare continues to evolve, embracing a more holistic approach that integrates the strengths of both traditional medicine and complementary therapies like chiropractic care can lead to more comprehensive, personalized wellness. By not only addressing the physical symptoms but also the underlying causes and conditions, individuals can embark on a journey toward optimal well-being that considers every aspect of their health.

To make the most of both traditional medicine and chiropractic care, healthcare providers need to communicate and collaborate. Patients should view their medical team as partners working together to harness the benefits of collaborative care.

Before seeking chiropractic care as a complement to traditional medicine, patients should consult both their primary care physician and a qualified chiropractor. This ensures their treatment plan is well-coordinated, safe, and tailored to their individual needs.

Holistic Healthcare From Elevate Wellness

When it comes to your health, the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we believe in a multifaceted approach to healthcare. Our experienced chiropractors consider all aspects of their patients’ health and create personalized treatment plans to meet their individual needs. To learn more about how chiropractic care can complement traditional medicine and start your journey toward whole-body wellness, contact us today.

pages.metaDescription: In this blog post, we’ll discuss the ways weather affects pain and give tips on managing discomfort, whether it’s related to changing weather conditions or not.
pages.bodyCopy:
Have you ever noticed that the weather conditions can sometimes intensify aches and pains? Does your grandma claim she can tell when it’s going to rain just by the feeling in her knees? It may seem far-fetched, but there’s actually a scientific basis behind this phenomenon.

In this blog post, we’ll delve into the ways weather affects pain and give tips on managing discomfort, whether it’s related to changing weather conditions or not.

Understanding the Basics

Before we get into the complex connections between weather and pain, we first need to talk about the basics.

There are many types of pain, but each can be classified as either acute or chronic. Acute pain is usually the result of an injury or trauma, while chronic pain is experienced over a long period of time and can occur due to conditions such as arthritis or fibromyalgia.

On the other hand, weather involves complicated interactions of various atmospheric elements, including humidity, temperature, precipitation, and barometric pressure. Changes in these variables have the potential to exacerbate discomfort and influence pain perception in individuals already dealing with physiological pain.

The Cold Truth

One of the most significant ways weather affects pain is cold temperatures. Many people report that their arthritis or joint pain worsens during the winter months. There’s actually scientific merit to this phenomenon; chilly weather can constrict muscles and ligaments and cause them to become less pliable, leading to increased stiffness and discomfort in individuals with pre-existing pain conditions.

Furthermore, colder temperatures can affect blood circulation, reducing the flow of oxygen and important nutrients to the affected areas. This lack of circulation can exacerbate pain, making it more challenging for patients to effectively manage their symptoms.

Atmospheric Pressure

Atmospheric pressure, also known as barometric pressure, is another weather variable that can affect pain levels. When atmospheric pressure drops, like before a storm passes through, it can lead to a drop of pressure in the joints, as well, causing tissues to expand and potentially irritating nerves. This can cause increased pain, especially for people with joint conditions. It can also cause headaches in certain individuals.

Conversely, rising atmospheric pressure can have the opposite effect, compressing joint tissues and potentially reducing pain for individuals who experience discomfort when the weather is stormy.

The Humidity Factor

Humidity, or the amount of moisture in the air, can influence pain perception. Some individuals report increased pain and discomfort when humidity levels are high, particularly those with conditions like fibromyalgia. The excess moisture can affect nerve endings and make muscles feel tender or sore. On the other hand, low humidity levels can dry out the skin and mucous membranes, potentially worsening pain for individuals with sinus issues or chronic conditions like dry eye syndrome.

Using a humidifier or dehumidifier to maintain optimal humidity levels indoors can help mitigate some of these effects.

The Power of Sunshine

While cold or rainy weather often worsens pain, sunshine can have the opposite effect. Because sunlight provides the body with vitamin D, which plays an important role in bone health, it can have a positive impact on overall well-being. Insufficient vitamin D has been linked to certain chronic pain like osteoporosis and fibromyalgia, so it’s important to maintain adequate levels of this essential nutrient to protect against pain.

Additionally, natural light can have a mood-boosting effect and help individuals cope better with chronic pain along with reducing feelings of depression or anxiety associated with their condition.

Managing Weather-Related Pain

With the link between weather and pain, it’s crucial to develop strategies to manage your discomfort effectively, especially if you experience chronic pain. Here are some things you can do to find relief from weather-related symptoms:

Stay active: Maintaining mobility through regular exercise is essential. During colder months, try indoor activities such as yoga or swimming to keep your muscles and joints limber.

Maintain a healthy diet: To support overall health and help you manage your pain, make sure you eat a balanced diet rich in nutrients. If you need help developing a meal plan that fits your specific goals, consult with a nutritionist.

Keep hydrated: Ensure you drink plenty of water to help your joints stay lubricated and keep your body functioning optimally.

Consider chiropractic care: Regular chiropractic adjustments can help alleviate pain and improve mobility, regardless of the weather, making this treatment an essential facet of many patients’ pain management strategies.

Conclusion

The experts at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic are committed to providing treatments that help manage both acute and chronic pain, along with educating patients on their conditions to ensure a holistic approach to wellness. By understanding the connection between weather and pain and being proactive in managing your discomfort, you can take steps to enjoy a more comfortable, pain-free life, regardless of the weather conditions.
