headings.text: The Role of Inflammation in Joint Health
Supporting Joint Health at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

pages.bodyCopy:
Joint health is one of the cornerstones of overall well-being. Healthy joints allow you to move freely and live an active, fulfilling life. If you’re looking for a way to alleviate joint discomfort, keep in mind that diet plays a pivotal role. At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we emphasize a whole-body approach to health, and nutrition is a key component of our care.

In this guide, we’ll suggest some foods to add to your diet to support your joint health.

The Role of Inflammation in Joint Health

Before getting into specific foods, it’s important to understand inflammation’s role in joint health. While occasional inflammation is normal and healthy, chronic inflammation can lead to conditions like arthritis, which causes swelling, stiffness, and pain in the joints. By eating foods with anti-inflammatory properties, you can enhance your overall joint health.

Omega-3 Fatty Acids

Omega-3 fatty acids are known for their anti-inflammatory properties. These essential fats work to reduce the production of inflammatory chemicals in the body. Fatty fish such as sardines, mackerel, trout, and salmon are some of the best sources of omega-3s. Chia seeds and flax seeds are rich in alpha-linolenic acid, which is a type of omega-3. Finally, a handful of walnuts can be a convenient snack that boosts your omega-3 intake.

Colorful Fruits and Vegetables

Antioxidants combat oxidative stress and inflammation. Fruits and vegetables are excellent sources of antioxidants, so make sure you add a rainbow of colors to your plate to support your joint health:

Berries: Raspberries, strawberries, and blueberries contain antioxidants such as vitamin C and anthocyanins, which are known for their anti-inflammatory properties.

Leafy greens: Kale and spinach are excellent sources of vitamins and minerals that support joint health.

Cruciferous vegetables: Cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, and broccoli contain sulforaphane, which is known to reduce inflammation.

Fiber-Rich Whole Grains

Fiber isn’t just good for the digestive system, it’s also an essential part of a joint-friendly diet. By promoting a healthy gut microbiome, fiber helps control inflammation and reduces joint pain.

Opting for whole grains is a great way to increase fiber intake. Have a hearty bowl of oatmeal for breakfast or switch out white rice for nutrient-dense brown rice. In addition to being a versatile whole grain, quinoa is also a complete protein, which means it provides all nine of the essential amino acids.

Nuts and Seeds

Nuts and seeds are chock-full of protein, healthy fats, and antioxidants, providing multifaceted joint health benefits. Almonds and sunflower seeds are especially high in anti-inflammatory vitamin E, while pumpkin seeds contain magnesium, a mineral that supports bone and joint health.

Lean Protein

Protein is vital for building, repairing, and maintaining joint tissues. Choose lean sources of protein whenever possible to avoid excessive saturated fats. Chicken and turkey, for example, are great sources of lean protein.

When it comes to plant-based protein, legumes like chickpeas, lentils, and beans are good choices. Soy products like tempeh and tofu are also rich in protein and can be used in a variety of dishes.

Spices and Herbs

Believe it or not, adding certain herbs and spices to your food doesn’t just make it taste better, it can also provide additional anti-inflammatory benefits and support joint health.

For example, turmeric contains curcumin, which is a powerful anti-inflammatory compound. Sprinkle a bit on soups, stews, and even smoothies. Ginger is also known for reducing inflammation and joint pain. Add it to tea, stir-fry, or baked goods. Finally, garlic contains diallyl disulfide, which is another excellent anti-inflammatory.

Healthy Fats

Consuming healthy fats is crucial for maintaining the integrity of joint structures and reducing inflammation. Avocados are packed with antioxidants and monounsaturated fats, while coconut oil contains medium-chain triglycerides, both of which are known to reduce inflammation. Additionally, extra virgin olive oil contains oleocanthal, a compound with anti-inflammatory properties similar to ibuprofen.

Keep Joints Lubricated

Keeping joints lubricated is crucial for reducing inflammation. Drinking plenty of water keeps joint cartilage hydrated and supple, so it’s important to aim for at least eight glasses of water per day. Furthermore, consider hydrating foods like watermelon, oranges, and cucumbers.

Foods to Limit

In addition to eating foods that support joint health, it’s also important to limit intake of those that can exacerbate inflammation, including sugary foods and beverages, processed foods full of unhealthy fats, and excessive alcohol.

The Connection Between Dehydration and Back Pain
Stay Hydrated for a Healthy Spine
The Role of Chiropractic Care in Spinal Health
Quality Care at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

pages.bodyCopy:
As you’re aware, hydration is a key element of achieving and maintaining overall well-being. But did you know that staying hydrated is also crucial for maintaining your spinal health? The spine, which is a central component of your body’s structure and function, relies on proper hydration to perform optimally.

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we are committed to educating our patients on how to live happy, healthy lives and take proper care of their bodies. In this blog post, we’ll discuss the importance of hydration in not just enhancing overall wellness but maintaining optimal spinal health, as well.

Why Hydration Matters for Your Spine

The spine consists of bones, muscles, ligaments, and discs. The intervertebral discs act as cushions between the vertebrae and are particularly dependent on hydration. They’re made of a soft, gel-like substance called the nucleus pulposus, which is surrounded by a tough outer layer.

The nucleus pulposus is made of about 70 to 90 percent water, making the discs flexible and giving them shock-absorbing abilities. When you’re properly hydrated, the spinal discs maintain their elasticity; however, dehydration can cause the discs to become brittle and inhibit their ability to cushion the spine. This can result in discomfort, reduced mobility, and an increased risk of injury.

The Connection Between Dehydration and Back Pain

The consequences of dehydration go beyond just shirts, it can also have a direct impact on your spinal health, causing your intervertebral discs to lose water content, shrink, and become less effective at absorbing impacts. This can cause the space between the vertebrae to shrink, leading to herniated or bulging discs.

Additionally, a lack of hydration can lead to the spine losing its natural curve, contributing to poor posture and alignment. Over time, this can cause chronic back pain, discomfort, and stiffness. Chronic dehydration can also affect the muscles and ligaments surrounding the spine, leading to muscle cramps and spasms and exacerbating conditions like spinal stenosis, sciatica, and herniated discs.

Stay Hydrated for a Healthy Spine

Staying hydrated is a simple yet powerful way to support your spinal health. Aim to drink around four to six cups of water each day; however, your hydration needs may vary depending on your activity level and climate, so it’s essential to listen to your body. It’s especially important to stay hydrated during physical activity, whether it’s working out or doing a physically demanding job.

Consider starting your day by drinking a glass of water to replenish fluids lost during sleep. If you have a hard time remembering to drink water throughout the day, try setting reminders on your phone or tracking water intake through an app. Try to limit the amount of soda or sugary beverages you drink, as they can actually contribute to dehydration.

You can get water through certain foods, as well. Cucumbers, oranges, watermelon, and lettuce are all high in water content and contribute to your daily hydration goals. Adding them to your diet provides a refreshing and nutritious way to get the water you need.

Finally, checking the color of your urine is a simple way to gauge your hydration levels. Light yellow indicates proper hydration, while dark yellow or amber suggests that you need to drink more water.

The Role of Chiropractic Care in Spinal Health

Although hydration plays an essential role in maintaining optimal spinal health, it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Regular chiropractic care is another vital component, helping you keep your spine properly aligned and ensuring its functionality. Chiropractic adjustments aim to relieve pressure on spinal discs, improve posture, and enhance overall mobility.

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we offer individualized care that includes targeted adjustments, therapeutic exercises, and lifestyle recommendations tailored to your personal needs. Combined with proper hydration, chiropractic care can help prevent and alleviate back pain, support long-term spinal health, and improve your quality of life.

Quality Care at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

The importance of staying hydrated cannot be overstated. It’s essential for both spinal health and ensuring your overall well-being. When you make it a priority to drink plenty of water every day, you can protect your intervertebral discs, reduce your risk of back pain, and support your body’s overall function.

Elevate Wellness Chiropractic is here to help you achieve optimal spinal health through comprehensive care and individualized wellness strategies. Contact us today to schedule an appointment as you begin your journey to a healthier, more comfortable life.

headings.text: A Complementary Approach to Mental Health Care

pages.bodyCopy:
Most people associate chiropractic care with relief from musculoskeletal pain, whether it’s joint discomfort or spinal misalignments. However, the effects of chiropractic care extend to more than just physical health; it’s a holistic approach that considers the entire body, including the mind.

Emerging research and patient anecdotes suggest a connection between chiropractic care and mental health, illuminating the ways spinal health influences overall well-being. In this blog post, we’ll discuss how chiropractic care can have a positive impact on mental health.

The Mind-Body Connection

The mind and body are intricately connected, influencing each other in profound and complex ways. In addition to affecting the mind, mental health conditions like chronic stress, depression, and anxiety often manifest physically, causing fatigue, headaches, and muscle tension. The opposite is also true: physical ailments can contribute to mental health issues.

Chiropractic care addresses the mind-body connection by focusing on the nervous system, which plays a key part in regulating mental and emotional health. The spine is home to the spinal cord, a vital component of the central nervous system that transmits signals from the brain to the rest of the body. Spinal misalignments can interfere with these signals, potentially leading to both physical and emotional stress.

Reducing Stress and Anxiety

One of the most significant ways chiropractic care can improve mental health is by reducing stress and anxiety. Spinal misalignments, also known as subluxations, can cause muscle tension and physical discomfort. This, in turn, triggers the body’s stress response, which can lead to excess cortisol, a hormone associated with depression and anxiety.

Chiropractic care aims to correct spinal misalignments, allow the nervous system to function more effectively, and better regulate the production of stress hormones. This can lead to a reduction of anxiety and a sense of overall relaxation. Many patients feel less anxious or stressed after chiropractic sessions, which can have a positive impact on mental health over time.

Enhancing Sleep Quality

Poor sleep can contribute to a wide range of physical and psychological issues, from fatigue to brain fog to mood disorders. Among the factors that can affect sleep are spinal misalignments, which cause disruptive pain and discomfort.

Chiropractic care addresses the root causes of these disruptions, hopefully improving sleep quality. Relieving pressure on the muscles and nerves reduces pain and discomfort, making it easier to fall asleep and stay asleep. Additionally, by reducing stress and promoting relaxation, chiropractic care allows the body to recover from daily stress, leading to a more balanced mental state that’s more conducive to restful sleep.

Boosting Mood and Emotional Well-Being

Chiropractic care can also have a positive effect on mood and emotional well-being. Spinal alignment impacts the central nervous system, which regulates the production and release of mood-regulating neurotransmitters like dopamine and serotonin. Imbalances in these neurotransmitters have been linked to anxiety and depression.

Ensuring proper spinal alignment contributes to optimized nervous system function and supports neurotransmitter production. Therefore, chiropractic care can improve mood, reduce feelings of sadness or depression, and enhance overall emotional well-being.

Supporting Mental Clarity and Focus

When it comes to productivity, whether at work or at home, mental clarity and focus are essential. However, stress, chronic pain, and poor sleep can significantly impair cognitive function, contributing to memory issues, difficulty concentrating, and brain fog. Fortunately, by addressing these underlying issues, chiropractic care can enhance mental clarity and focus.

When proper spinal alignment is restored, the nervous system is able to function properly. After a chiropractic adjustment, patients often experience reduced pain, better sleep, and less stress, helping to improve their cognitive function. When they have a clearer mind, patients can better manage their daily tasks, make decisions more confidently, and have a more positive attitude.

A Complementary Approach to Mental Health Care

By focusing on the physical aspects of mental health, chiropractic care offers a drug-free, non-invasive treatment option for those dealing with mental health challenges. However, while chiropractic care can contribute to enhanced mental health, it’s important to utilize it as part of a comprehensive treatment plan, especially for more serious mental health concerns.

Chiropractic care is most effective when combined with other treatments, such as therapy, exercise, a healthy diet, and medication (when prescribed). It’s an excellent complement to traditional treatments, offering a more holistic approach to mental health management and acknowledging the deep connection between the body and mind.

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we understand that chiropractic care is more than just a solution for back pain. If you’re seeking to improve your mental and emotional well-being, give chiropractic care a try. Schedule an appointment with us today to take the first step toward a more balanced, healthy life.

headings.text: Integrating Chiropractic Care into Your Running Routine
Enhance Your Performance with Elevate Wellness

pages.bodyCopy:
It’s fall, which means the summer heatwaves are over. It’s the perfect time to go for a run outdoors and enjoy the crisp autumn air. As you seek to enhance your running performance and avoid injuries, consider the potential of chiropractic care.

This often overlooked yet highly effective approach to injury prevention and recovery goes beyond addressing back pain, it can play a vital role in optimizing your athletic performance, reducing recovery times, and preventing future injuries. In this blog post, we’ll dive into how chiropractic care can benefit runners and keep them on track.

5 Ways Chiropractic Care Helps Runners

As a high-impact sport, running places significant stress on the body, from the spine and joints to the muscles. Many runners sustain injuries such as runner’s knee, shin splints, IT band syndrome, and plantar fasciitis. Fortunately, chiropractic care can be an effective way to give the body the tools it needs to perform optimally.

1. Improved Biomechanics

One of the main goals of chiropractic care is ensuring the musculoskeletal system is properly aligned. Running requires a lot of repetitive motion, which means that even a slight imbalance or misalignment can cause the body to compensate with movement patterns that put undue stress on certain joints and muscles, increasing wear and tear on the body.

By using manual adjustments and other techniques, chiropractors aim to restore alignment to the spine and joints and ensure proper biomechanics, which allow the body to move more efficiently, enhance running performance, and reduce the risk of injury.

2. Injury Prevention and Recovery

One of runners’ biggest challenges is avoiding injury. Regular chiropractic adjustments are key to maintaining optimal musculoskeletal health and ensuring imbalances are corrected before they can escalate into significant injuries that put runners on the sidelines. Chiropractors are able to detect and address areas of misalignment or tension that make a runner more likely to sustain common injuries like knee pain or shin splints.

However, even the most careful runners sometimes get injured. Whether it’s a strain, sprain, or overuse injury, chiropractic care can help them recover faster. A combination of soft tissue therapies, spinal adjustments, and rehabilitation exercises help improve circulation, reduce inflammation, and promote better healing. By addressing the root cause of the injury rather than just the symptoms, chiropractic treatment can help prevent recurring injuries.

3. Enhanced Flexibility and Range of Motion

As runners push their bodies to the limit, flexibility and mobility are crucial. Chiropractic care helps maintain or increase range of motion by promoting overall joint health. Targeted adjustments can alleviate tension and stiffness in the joints, ensuring the body can perform its best.

With an enhanced range of motion, runners are less likely to experience cramps, strains, or muscle tightness. Increased mobility allows for smoother movements, which can improve running efficiency.

4. Better Posture and Running Form

For runners to maintain efficiency and prevent injury, they need proper posture. Postural issues such as slouching shoulders or forward head carriage can negatively affect their form, leading to improper foot strike, overpronation, or other issues. These small deviations can cause more serious problems down the road, including IT band syndrome or persistent back pain.

Chiropractors can evaluate and correct postural issues, helping runners maintain proper alignment, optimize their form, reduce fatigue, and prevent unnecessary muscle and joint strain.

5. Natural Pain Relief

One of the most significant advantages of chiropractic care is its drug-free approach to managing pain. Runners may be tempted to reach for painkillers or anti-inflammatory medications to continue training, especially those dealing with chronic pain. However, these drugs simply mask pain without addressing its underlying cause.

Chiropractic care, on the other hand, offers a natural and effective pain management solution. Chiropractors can use various techniques to reduce pain and inflammation without the need for medication. This approach allows runners to recover and heal more holistically and continue training with fewer side effects.

Integrating Chiropractic Care into Your Running Routine

If you’re a runner looking to integrate chiropractic care into your training routine, follow these tips:

Schedule regular adjustments, even if you’re not currently experiencing pain, to maintain alignment and prevent injury.

Address minor pain and discomfort before they become more serious issues.

Incorporate the stretches and exercises recommended by your chiropractor.

Communicate with your chiropractor regarding your training goals so they can help you achieve peak performance.

Enhance Your Performance with Elevate Wellness

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we specialize in helping athletes enhance their physical performance and keep their bodies running smoothly. If you’re a runner looking to bring your speed and endurance to the next level, schedule an appointment with us today!

Headache

Home - Headache

About one in six people in the United States experiences headaches, making them one of the most common health complaints. Whether they occur occasionally or several times a week, headaches can interfere with work, sleep, and daily activities. If you find yourself often relying on medication for relief, chiropractic care could be the natural alternative you need.

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we focus on identifying the source of your headaches and creating a personalized treatment plan to reduce their frequency and severity.

Common Types of Headaches

There are several types of headaches, and understanding the difference can help you determine the best course of treatment.

Tension Headaches, These are the most common type of headache people experience, and they are often linked to muscle tension in the neck and shoulders. People often experience a dull, aching pain around the forehead or the back of the head.

Cervicogenic Headaches, These headaches are caused by problems in the neck, such as joint dysfunction, poor posture, arthritis, or muscle tightness. Pain may start at the base of the skull and radiate toward the forehead or behind the eyes.

Migraine Headaches, Migraines are more intense and may include symptoms, such as throbbing pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light or sound. While migraines can have multiple triggers, spinal misalignment and muscle tension can contribute to their frequency.

Cluster Headache, Cluster headaches cause pain on one side of the head. They can last from 15 minutes up to three hours and occur daily for weeks to months at the same time each day. They are often caused by pressure on the trigeminal nerve, a three-part nerve in your head.

Headaches can also be caused by the food you eat and staring at digital screens for prolonged periods.

How Chiropractic Care Can Help

The Elevate Wellness Chiropractic team focuses on helping you identify the underlying cause of your headaches, focusing on the spine and nervous system. When joints are restricted or muscles are tight, they can irritate nerves and contribute to headache pain.

Our care includes spinal adjustments, soft tissue therapy, stretching, and posture correction. These techniques:

Restore proper spinal alignment

Reduce muscle tension in the neck and shoulders

Improve posture and mobility

Relieve pressure on nerves

Support the body’s natural healing process

We also develop personalised treatment plans that may include lifestyle changes, ergonomic advice, and exercises to help you find daily relief.

Many patients expereince fewer headaches and less severe symptoms with regular chiropractic care.

What to Expect During Your Visit

Your first visit will include a comprehensive evaluation to determine the possible causes of your headaches. This may involve:

Reviewing your health history

Discussing your headache patterns and triggers

Performing a physical and spinal examination

Evaluating posture and movement

Based on your evaluation, your chiropractor will recommend a customized treatment plan

At-Home Headache Relief

In addition to our in-office care, our team can help you establish an at-home treatment plan. Some great ways to relieve your symptoms in between appointments with your chiropractic team include:

Using a cold or warm compress

Resting in a dark, quiet room

Drinking plenty of water

Taking a break from screens

Improving your posture

Taking a warm shower or bath

While these at-home treatments can help you alleviate symptoms, it is always best to receive expert support for chronic discomfort. Our team can help you find relief sooner than if you attempt care on your own.

Find Relief from Headaches

Headaches don’t have to be a regular part of your life. The Elevate Wellness Team can treat the root cause of your pain so you can feel better and function at your best. If headaches are interfering with your daily routine, our team can help. Contact our office in Bountiful or Clinton, Utah, today to schedule an appointment and learn how chiropractic care may help you find lasting relief.

+Can poor posture cause headaches?

Yes. Poor posture, especially from looking down at phones or sitting at a computer for extended periods, can strain the muscles and joints of the neck. This increased tension may contribute to headaches.

+Can chiropractic care prevent future headaches?

For headaches related to neck dysfunction, muscle tension, or posture, chiropractic care combined with stretching, strengthening exercises, ergonomic improvements, and healthy lifestyle habits may help reduce the frequency or severity of future headaches.

+How many chiropractic visits will I need?

The number of visits depends on the cause of your headaches, how long you’ve had symptoms, your overall health, and how your body responds to treatment. Some patients notice improvement within a few visits, while others with chronic conditions may require a longer treatment plan.

+How do I know if my headache is coming from my neck?

Headaches caused by neck problems often begin at the base of the skull and may radiate toward the forehead, temples, or behind the eyes. They are frequently accompanied by neck pain or stiffness.

Whiplash

Home - Whiplash

Whiplash is one of the most common injuries after car accidents, sports collisions, and sudden falls. Even low-speed impacts can cause serious strain to the neck and upper spine. At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we provide gentle, effective whiplash treatment designed to reduce pain, restore movement, and help your body heal naturally.

If you’re experiencing neck pain, stiffness, headaches, or discomfort after an accident, investing in early chiropractic care can make a big difference in your recovery.

What is Whiplash?

Whiplash occurs when your head is suddenly thrown forward and backward, placing excessive force on the neck and spine. This rapid motion can sprain and damage muscles and ligaments, spinal joints, discs and soft tissues, and nerves in the neck and upper back

Whiplash symptoms don’t always appear right away. Many people feel fine initially after an accident, only to develop pain and stiffness a few days, weeks, or even months later.

Common Whiplash Symptoms

Whiplash symptoms vary from person to person, but after an accident, people typically experience:

Neck pain and stiffness

Headaches (often starting at the base of the skull)

Shoulder or upper back pain

Reduced range of motion

Dizziness

Irritability

Fatigue or trouble sleeping

Tingling or numbness in the arms

Jaw pain or difficulty sleeping

Vision problems

Muscle weakness

Memory loss

Depression and anxiety

If left untreated, whiplash can lead to chronic pain and long-term mobility issues.

Whiplash Severity

Whiplash is classified into grades based on severity:

Grade 0: No pain or physical symptoms

Grade I: Pain and stiffness, but no physical signs of injury

Grade II: Decreased range of motion and muscle spasms

Grade III: Neurological signs like numbness, tingling, or weakness, as well as swelling and inflammation

Grade IV: This is the most severe and includes the presence of fractures or dislocations of the cervical spine. If you experience this grade, you should seek emergency care.

How Chiropractic Care Helps Whiplash

Chiropractors focus on restoring proper alignment and movement in the spine, which is often disrupted during a whiplash injury. Our approach is customized to your condition and comfort level.

Chiropractic treatment may include:

Gentle spinal adjustments to improve joint function

Soft tissue therapy to reduce muscle tension and inflammation

Range of motion exercises to restore flexibility

Postural guidance and at-home care to support healing

Rehabilitation exercises to strengthen the neck and upper back

We use techniques designed specifically for injury recovery. We don’t believe in aggressive or one-size-fits-all care.

Why Early Treatment Matters

Waiting too long after a whiplash injury to receive treatment allows inflammation and joint dysfunction to worsen. Early chiropractic care can reduce pain and stiffness faster, lower inflammation, prevent scar tissue buildup, improve long-term outcomes, and lower the risk of chronic neck pain

Even if the accident was minor, you should still get evaluated by your primary care doctor.

Whiplash Care After a Car Accident

If you developed whiplash due to a car accident, chiropractic care may be covered by auto insurance. Our office can help you with documentation and coordinate care so you can focus on healing, not paperwork.

Take a Step Toward Whiplash Relief

Whiplash can affect more than just your neck; it can disrupt your daily life, make it hard to sleep, and affect your overall well-being. Chiropractic care offers a safe, natural approach to relieving pain, restoring mobility, and supporting long-term healing after an accident or injury. With personalized treatment and a focus on gentle recovery, our team can help you feel better and get back to living comfortably.

Don’t wait for symptoms to worsen. Schedule an initial evaluation in Bountiful or Clinton, Utah, today and start on the path toward lasting relief.

ELEVATE YOUR WELLNESS

Schedule Your Chiropractic Appointment Today for Whiplash Treatment

or

Frequently Asked Questions

+How soon should I see a chiropractor after whiplash?

You should seek an evaluation as soon as possible after an accident, even if your symptoms seem minor. Early assessment can help identify potential injuries and guide appropriate care.

+How long does whiplash take to heal?

Recovery varies depending on the severity of the injury and individual factors. Some people recover within a few weeks, while others may experience symptoms for longer.

+Do I need an X-ray after a whiplash injury?

Not everyone needs imaging. Your healthcare provider or chiropractor can determine whether X-rays or other imaging are appropriate based on your symptoms and examination.

+When should I seek emergency care for whiplash?

Seek immediate medical attention after a serious accident or if you experience severe or worsening pain, significant weakness or numbness, difficulty walking, loss of bladder or bowel control, confusion, or loss of consciousness.

Tension Headaches

Home - Tension Headaches

Tension headaches are the most common type of headache, often described as a constant, dull pressure or ache in the head, forehead, or neck. While they’re frequently linked to stress, poor posture, or muscle tension, they can also occur due to spinal misalignment or tight muscles in the neck and upper back. If you’re tired of suffering from constant head pain, Elevate Wellness Chiropractic can help by providing natural, drug-free relief.

What Are Tension Headaches?

A tension headache is a headache that often feels like a tight band wrapped around your head. It typically causes mild to moderate pain that feels steady rather than throbbing. Many people also experience tightness or pressure across the forehead or temples, neck or shoulder stiffness, scalp tenderness, and fatigue or difficulty concentrating

Unlike migraines, tension headaches don’t typically cause nausea or sensitivity to light, but they can still significantly interfere with work, sleep, and daily life, especially when they become frequent or chronic.

There are three main types of tension headaches:

Infrequent Episodic, You typically have headaches one day a month or less (under 12 days per year).

Frequent Epsodic, You experience headaches one to 14 days every month for at least three months (12 to 179 days per year).

Chronic, You experience headaches 15 or more days per month for over three months (180 or more days per year).

Common Causes of Tension Headaches

Tension headaches often develop when muscles in the neck, shoulders, and upper back become tight or strained. Common contributing factors include:

Poor posture, especially from prolonged sitting or screen use

Stress, anxiety, depression, and emotional tension

Neck or upper back misalignments

Muscle imbalance or weakness

Jaw tension, TMD, or teeth grinding

Repetitive movement or overuse injuries

Eye strain

Fatigue, dehydration, or skipping meals

When the spine is not moving properly, surrounding muscles may tighten to compensate, leading to ongoing tension and worsening headache pain.

How Chiropractic Care Helps Tension Headaches

Chiropractic care focuses on correcting spinal misalignments, improving joint mobility, and reducing muscle tension that can trigger headaches. By addressing the root cause, not just the symptoms, chiropractic treatment can bring lasting relief.

Chiropractic care may help reduce headache frequency and intensity, relieve neck and shoulder tension, improve posture and spinal alignment, increase range of motion in the neck, and support better nervous system function.

Many patients experience fewer headaches and improved comfort after regular chiropractic care.

Our Approach to Treating Tension Headaches

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we take a personalized approach to tension headache treatment. Your care plan may include:

Chiropractic adjustments to improve alignment in the neck and upper spine

Soft tissue therapy to relax tight muscles and reduce trigger points

Laser spinal decompression to reduce stress and tension

Postural guidance to address habits that contribute to muscle strain

Stretching and strengthening exercises to support long-term relief

Lifestyle recommendations to help manage stress and prevent future episodes

Treatments will depend on your specific symptoms, health history, and daily activities.

When to Seek Chiropractic Care for Headaches

You may benefit from chiropractic care if:

You experience frequent or recurring tension headaches

Headaches are accompanied by neck stiffness or shoulder pain

Over-the-counter medications only provide temporary relief

Headaches worsen with stress or prolonged sitting

You want a natural, non-invasive treatment option

Early care can help prevent tension headaches from turning into a chronic problem. And even if you are not currently experiencing symptoms, we recommend coming in for regular chiropractic care to maintain proper spine health and keep your body fully functional.

Schedule a Consultation

If tension headaches affect your quality of life, a chiropractor can address the underlying cause of your pain and provide long-term relief. Contact our office in Bountiful or Clinton, Utah, today to schedule a consultation and learn how chiropractic treatment can help you live a better quality of life.

Tension headaches can last anywhere from a few hours to several days. Frequent or persistent headaches should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.

+When should I see a chiropractor for tension headaches?

Consider an evaluation if your headaches occur frequently, keep returning, are associated with neck pain or stiffness, or interfere with your daily activities.

Massage therapy may help relieve muscle tension and promote relaxation, which may be beneficial for people whose headaches are associated with tight muscles or stress.

+How can I prevent tension headaches?

Spinal Disc Injuries

Home - Spinal Disc Injuries

Your spine is made up of vertebrae separated by discs, cushion-like structures that absorb shock and allow flexibility. When these discs become damaged or displaced, you can experience pain, limited mobility, and nerve-related symptoms. Fortunately, Elevated Wellness Chiropractic has the expertise, tools, and knowledge to help you find relief from spinal disc injuries. We can find the source of your discomfort and develop a personalized plan to get you back to full health.

What is a Spinal Disc?

A spinal disc, or intervertebral disc, is a spongy cushion between your vertebrae that acts as a shock absorber. It connects the bones and allows your spine to bend, twist, and flex. It consists of an outer layer (annulus firbosus) and an inner core (nucleus pulposus).

Annulus Fibrosus, A strong, outer layer made of cartilage and collagen fibers.

Nuclear Pulpous, The gel-like inner core that provides cushioning and distributes pressure.

There are 23 discs in the spine, located between the 33 vertebrae.

Different Types of Disc Degeneration

Herniated Disc, The soft, jelly-like center pushes through a crack in the tough outer layer, irritating nearby nerves and causing sharp pain, numbness, or weakness, often in the lower back or neck

Bulging Disc, The disc’s outer layer bulges outward into the spinal canal, often due to age-related wear. However, unlike a herniated disc, it doesn’t create a tear. It often results in numbness, tingling, or pain in the arms, legs, neck, or back, though some people have no symptoms.

Degenerated Disc, Denerative disc disease refers to the natural age-related wear-and-tear on the spinal discs, causing them to lose water, flatten, crack, and become less effective at cushioning and supporting the spine. It can cause pain, stiffness, numbness, or weakness if nerves get pinched.

Thinning Disc, This is a stage of degenerative disc disease, where age causes spinal discs to thin and become less flexible. You can feel pain, stiffness, and potential nerve compression as the space between the vertebrae shrinks. Not all people who experience degenerative disc disease will have thinning discs, as they could also have bulging or herniation.

How Chiropractic Care Helps

Chiropractic care offers a non-surgical approach to managing spinal disc injuries. Techniques include:

Spinal Manipulation, Chiropractic adjustments can correct areas of the spine that interfere with proper nervous system communication. They can also restore motion and function to the spine and reduce pain and inflammation.

Spinal Decompression, Spinal decompression treatment helps people with bulging or herniated discs make a full recovery and avoid surgery. It stimulates the body’s natural healing capabilities to restore the spine back to its proper state, reduce pressure on the nerve root, and stop pain.

Soft Tissue Therapy, We will apply pressure to certain points on the body and move specific muscle groups to help alleviate the pain from spinal disc injuries.

Targeted Exercise & Rehabilitation, We will recommend exercises and stretches to perform at home to help you reduce stress on the spine and prevent recurrence.

If you experience persistent back or neck pain, numbness, or weakness, you should seek professional care. Early intervention can reduce symptoms, improve function, and prevent chronic issues.

Our team focuses on identifying the root cause of pain and restoring motion to the spine through natural, drug-free treatments. Our goal is to help you live a better quality of life and enhance your overall health and wellness. We are dedicated to only suggesting treatments that will reduce the risk of future injuries or pain.

Reduce Spinal Pain and Long-Term Damage With Chiropractic Care

Spinal disc injuries can be painful and disruptive, but with the right care, relief and improved mobility are possible. Chiropractic treatment offers a safe, non-surgical approach to reducing pain, restoring function, and supporting long-term spinal health. Early intervention and a personalized treatment plan can make a significant difference in your recovery and overall quality of life.

Seek immediate medical attention if you experience significant or worsening weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness around the groin or inner thighs.

You should seek an evaluation if you have persistent back or neck pain, pain that radiates into an arm or leg, numbness, tingling, or weakness.

Some disc injuries improve with conservative care and time. Treatment recommendations depend on the severity of symptoms and the underlying cause.

What is the Sciatic Nerve?

Your sciatic nerve is located in your lower back and branches through your hips, buttocks, and down each leg, reaching just below your knee. It is the longest and thickest nerve in the body and is formed by the merging of five nerve roots at the base of your spinal cord.

You have two on each side of your body, and they help with sensory and motor function in the lower limbs, including the lower leg, back of the thigh, calf, and foot.

What Is Sciatica?

Sciatica refers to the irritation or compression of the sciatic nerve. It typically causes an intense, sharp pain, tingling sensation, or numbing feeling that radiates from the lower back down through the buttocks and leg. It affects up to 40% of people at some point in their lives.

Sciatica is often caused by:

Bone spurs

Sharp, burning, or shooting pain down one leg

What Are Peripheral Nerves?

The peripheral system includes the entire network of nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. These nerves relay messages to and from the body’s organs, limbs, and senses and are divided into three different groups:

Sensory nerves that help your skin feel temperature, pain, vibration, and touch.

Motor nerves that control muscle movement.

Autonomic nerves that control certain functions, such as blood pressure, sweating, heart rate, digestion, and bladder function.

What is Neuropathy?

Neuropathy refers to the damage or dysfunction of the peripheral nerves, which often causes pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness in the hands, feet, or other parts of the body. This condition can significantly affect someone’s ability to perform daily activities.

Causes of Neuropathy

Neuropathy can be caused by a wide range of factors, including:

Type 2 Diabetes

Autoimmune disorders, such as Multiple Sclerosis (MS)

Infections, such as shingles

Physical trauma

Exposure to toxins

Certain medications, including chemotherapy drugs

Vitamin and nutrient deficiencies

Symptoms of Neuropathy

Neuropathy symptoms can vary depending on which nerves are affected and the underlying cause. However, common symptoms typically include the following:

Sensory Changes

Numbness or tingling

Burning or prickling sensations

Sensitivity to touch or cold

Loss of sensation in the feet, hands, or other extremities

Autonomic Dysfunction

Dizziness or lightheadedness

Difficulty controlling blood pressure or heart rate

Digestive problems

Bladder problems

Sexual dysfunction

Other Symptoms

Pain in the arms, legs, or feet

Muscles twitches

Fatigue or difficulty sleeping

Changes in skin temperature or color

Migraine

Home - Migraine

Around 35 million Americans suffer from migraines each year. A migraine is more than just a headache, it is a debilitating condition that can interfere with work, family time, and your day-to-day life. At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we address the underlying causes of migraine pain, helping patients find relief instead of just masking symptoms. Call us today if you want to learn more or schedule an appointment.

What is a Migraine?

A migraine is a neurological disease that often causes severe throbbing headaches, typically located on one side of the head. The headache phase usually lasts a few hours, but symptoms can last for days or weeks, interfering with your daily life.

Common Causes

While the exact cause of migraines is not fully understood, changes in brain activity, nerve pathways, and chemicals, as well as genetics are believed to play a role. Several factors can trigger a migraine attack, including:

Stress or hormonal fluctuations.

Poor diet or eating habits.

Interrupted sleep patterns.

Changes in weather patterns.

Changes in medication.

Spinal misalignment, poor posture, nerve irritation, or past injuries.

Those who are at a higher risk of experiencing migraines include women, native Hawaiian or Pacific Islanders, people with a family history of migraines, or those experiencing depression, anxiety, and sleep problems.

Common Symptoms

Everyone experiences migraines differently. But many people usually have one or more of the following symptoms:

One or two days before a migraine sets in, people may experience:

Constipation.

Mood changes.

Neck stiffness.

Increase urination.

Fluid retention.

Frequent yawning.

During an attack, they may experience:

A throbbing, pulsating, or pounding headache on one or both sides of the head.

Nausea and vomiting.

Sensitivity to light, sound, smell, or touch.

Fatigue.

Dizziness.

Difficulty concentrating.

During an attack, people may experience “aura” or reversible symptoms of the nervous system, which include:

Visual disturbances, such as flashing lights, zigzag lines, or blind spots, or vision loss.

A feeling of pins and needles in the arms or legs.

Weakness or numbness in the face or one side of the body.

Trouble speaking.

After an attack, people may experience a “migraine hangover” with symptoms such as fatigue, body aches, and feeling drained, confused, or worn out for a day.

After you have determined whether you suffer from headaches or migraines, you should consider chiropractic treatment if nothing else is helping your symptoms.

Children vs. Adults

While adults may experience these intense headaches more often, children can also suffer from them, however they are often undiagnosed. Around one out of 10 children have these intense headaches, and about three out of 10 teens have them. Although migraines are more common in adult women, boys are more likely to have attacks before puberty. Some research has linked infant colic to developing headaches.

How Chiropractic Care Helps Migraines

Migraines are often linked to tension in the neck and spine, poor posture, or nerve irritation. Gentle chiropractic adjustments can restore proper alignment, improve nerve function, and reduce muscle tension, helping decrease the frequency and intensity of episodes.

Chiropractic care for migraines may include:

Gentle spinal adjustments.

Soft tissue therapy to release muscle tension.

Lifestyle and stress management tips.

Spinal decompression.

Benefits of Chiropractic Care for Migraines

Advanced Non-Surgical Treatment for Pain Relief

Home - Spinal Decompression

In addition to chiropractic care, Elevate Wellness Chiropractic provides non-surgical spinal decompression therapy to help with herniated discs or other conditions find relief from pain without having to undergo surgery. Call us today if you want to learn more or schedule a free consultation.

Spinal Decompression

Spinal decompression treatment works especially well for people suffering from bulging or herniated discs. We have helped people avoid surgery and make a full recovery from disc conditions. If you’re tired of dealing with severe back pain, come into our office for spinal decompression; we have seen life-changing results every day.

What is Spinal Decompression?

Spinal decompression stimulates the body’s natural healing capabilities to restore the spine back to its proper state. Using a sophisticated FDA-approved machine, we gently stretch the spine to decompress the discs. The machine senses the way your muscles resist when force is applied to the muscles, and if your muscles are resistant, the machine senses this and automatically adjusts the force and cycle stretch to help release muscle tension.

This negative pressure causes bulging or herniated discs to retract into place, reducing pressure on the nerve root and stopping pain. This treatment can also stimulate the flow of water, oxygen, and nutrients into the discs, boosting the healing process.

Spinal decompression works well for people suffering from:

Degenerative disc disorders

Bulging or herniated discs

Sciatica pain

Injured spinal nerve roots

Worn spinal joints

Back or neck pain

Failed back surgery

Stenosis

Spondylolisthesis

Muscle weakness

Disrupted sleep due to pain or muscle cramping

Laser Decompression Therapy

Unlike drug treatments that only mask the pain and don’t treat it, laser decompression therapy heals the body by treating it as a whole. If you are suffering from pain down your legs, back, and buttocks, you may benefit from this treatment. Call our office today if you want to make an appointment or learn more.

What is Laser Decompression Therapy?

Laser decompression therapy involves emitting light energy into the muscles and spine, where it penetrates the damaged tissue and stimulates the body’s natural healing capabilities.

When you injure your spinal discs, they become inflamed, and the nerves and surrounding tissue become compressed, leading to pain throughout the back, buttocks, and legs. Laser decompression therapy helps heal the inflammation and gently bring discs back into proper alignment.

Laser decompression works well for people suffering from:

Disrupted sleep due to pain or muscle cramping

Degenerative disc disorders

Bulging or herniated discs

Sciatica pain

Back or neck pain

Download Dr. Simmond’s explanation about spinal decompression and learn how he can relieve your pain without surgery by clicking on the box below.

Your First Visit

When you schedule your free consultation, you will first sit down with Dr. Simmonds for 10 to 15 minutes and tell him about your pain and what you’ve been experiencing. If he determines that you have a disc condition that could warrant spinal decompression, we will recommend a complete evaluation that includes a thorough spinal exam, as well as X-rays and potentially an MRI.

Once we have performed a full evaluation, Dr. Simmonds will determine whether you’re a good candidate for care and provide a recommended treatment plan based on the nature and severity of your condition. We want you to have a full picture so you can make a well-informed decision about your health.

Typical spinal decompression treatment lasts between 20 to 30 minutes. An average patient will require between 20 and 30 treatments, although some patients see improvement in as little as three sessions. However, if you have a degenerative disc disease, you may require more treatment to deal with the pain. The exact number of appointments will vary based on the individual and how they respond to treatment.

If you’re suffering from unbearable back pain, schedule an evaluation at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic in Bountiful or Clinton, Utah. We can determine the source of your pain, recommend treatment, schedule care, and get you back to doing the things you love and weren’t able to do because of your condition.

Not everyone is a candidate. A thorough evaluation of your medical history, symptoms, and spinal condition can help determine whether spinal decompression is appropriate for you.

Some patients report reduced pain, less pressure, or improved mobility after treatment. Results vary, and your provider may recommend combining decompression with other therapies, exercises, or lifestyle changes for the best outcome.

pages.bodyCopy:
Pregnancy Chiropractor

Home - Pregnancy Chiropractor

Growing your family can be an incredibly exciting time in your life. However, as you progress through your pregnancy, it isn’t uncommon to experience discomfort. Whether from widening hips, increased pressure on your back, or swelling limbs, it can be difficult to find relief. With the support of our pregnancy chiropractors, you can move through this life change more comfortably.

Our reliable pregnancy chiropractors are dedicated to helping you relieve minor tension and major aches. We provide gentle care to ensure you and your baby are comfortable and safe throughout your treatment. If you’re tired of the discomfort that accompanies your pregnancy, trust Elevate Wellness Chiropractic’s expert team.

Common Discomfort During Pregnancy

Pregnancy is an exciting time in your life, but it also brings many physical changes that can contribute to increased discomfort. One of the most common complaints our pregnancy chiropractors hear about is lower back pain due to increased weight and sift in your body’s center of gravity.

As you approach your due date, you may also experience pelvic pain as your ligaments loosen in preparation for childbirth. This pain, coupled with your back pain, may result in sciatica, characterized by sharp pain that radiates from the lower back down the legs, which can limit your mobility.

As the uterus expands, it can put pressure on the digestive system, leading to bloating, heartburn, and constipation. Swelling in the feet and ankles is also common due to increased fluid retention and circulation changes. Additionally, some women suffer from round ligament pain, a sharp discomfort in the lower belly or groin.

These aches and pains can make everyday tasks more challenging, but many discomforts can be alleviated with proper care and support. If you’re dealing with increasing discomfort as you advance through your pregnancy, turn to our team of reliable chiropractors at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic for support.

The Benefits of Working with a Pregnancy Chiropractor

At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, our pregnancy chiropractors specialize in gentle, targeted adjustments to help alleviate common pregnancy discomforts. As you go through your pregnancy and the stress on your body increases, reaching out to a trusted chiropractor for support becomes essential. Receiving chiropractic care throughout your pregnancy is incredibly beneficial for many reasons, including:

Relieve Discomfort: Alleviate common issues like back pain, sciatica, and pelvic discomfort caused by your body’s shifting weight and hormonal changes.

Promote Pelvic Alignment: Create more space for the baby to move into the optimal birth position, reducing your risk of breech presentation.

Support Better Posture: Prevent poor posture and strain on your muscles and joints as you experience bodily changes.

Drug-Free Pain Management: Experience pain relief while avoiding medications you cannot take while pregnant.

Improve Overall Well-Being: Feel more comfortable, energized, and prepared for childbirth with the support of our pregnancy chiropractors.

While discomfort is a common reason for individuals to reach out to schedule chiropractic care, you can also take a proactive approach. Whether you’re experiencing pain or want to support your body as it changes, contact Elevate Wellness Chiropractic today to schedule and enjoy every second of your pregnancy.

When to Schedule Chiropractic Care

Pregnant women can begin chiropractic care at any stage of pregnancy, but many choose to start in the first trimester to help their bodies adapt to early changes. Regular visits throughout pregnancy can promote spinal alignment and help manage discomfort as the baby grows, which can prepare you for upcoming bodily changes.

As you progress into the second trimester, you may notice weight increases and posture shifts. Chiropractic adjustments can help reduce the strain on your back and pelvis that accompanies these bodily changes. Many women find that consistent care during this stage prevents more severe pain in the later months.

The third trimester is often when women experience the most discomfort due to the baby’s size and position. You may notice sharp pain around your hips as they begin to widen and prepare for birth. Chiropractic care during this stage can help alleviate pressure on the pelvis and lower back while encouraging optimal fetal positioning for delivery.

No matter what stage you’re at in your pregnancy, you can trust that our pregnancy chiropractors are here and ready to help. We can support you through your discomfort and ensure your body is prepared for your upcoming birth.

Supporting You Through Your Pregnancy

If you want to feel your best during your pregnancy, trust our pregnancy chiropractors at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic. For years, we’ve provided expert chiropractic care to patients across the Wasatch Front. No matter what discomfort you’re experiencing, you can trust that we’re committed to helping you find relief.

When you’re ready to schedule an appointment with our expert team, don’t hesitate to contact us today.

When provided by a qualified chiropractor with experience in prenatal care, chiropractic treatment can be a safe option for many pregnant women. Techniques are modified to accommodate your changing body and comfort level.

+When should I start seeing a chiropractor during pregnancy?

You can discuss chiropractic care at any stage of pregnancy. Many women seek care when discomfort begins, while others choose regular visits to help manage changes throughout pregnancy.

+Can I see a chiropractor after giving birth?

Yes. Postpartum chiropractic care may help address back, neck, hip, and pelvic discomfort that can develop from pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, or caring for a newborn.

+How often should I see a chiropractor while pregnant?

Visit frequency varies based on your symptoms, stage of pregnancy, and individual needs. Your chiropractor can recommend a personalized care plan.

pages.bodyCopy:
Back Specialist

Home - Back Specialist

A 2019 study performed by the Centers for Disease Control found that three in five adults in the U.S. experience some form of back pain across their lives. While this pain may start as a minor twinge, it can quickly evolve into more significant discomfort that disrupts your everyday activities. That’s where our back specialists at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic come in.

We understand how frustrating it can be to deal with chronic pain, which is why we provide patients across the Wasatch Front with reliable chiropractic care. Whether you need spinal adjustments or chiropractic massage, we help patients develop a customized treatment plan to alleviate pain and restore strength and mobility.

Why Do You Have Back Pain?

The hardest part of dealing with back pain is identifying the root cause of your discomfort. As you get older, it seems like you can hurt your back doing a variety of activities you’ve done throughout your life. Often, you need a thorough examination from a trusted back specialist to determine what may be causing your discomfort. Some common reasons adults across the U.S. experience back pain include:

Muscle or ligament strains from heavy lifting or sudden, unexpected movements

Bulging or ruptured disks that press on the spinal nerves

Sciatica, a condition that causes weakness and pain along the sciatic nerve

Hunching or slouching for prolonged periods, especially if you work in an office setting

Injuries caused by participating in contact sports or car accidents

No matter why you’re experiencing back pain, our back specialists at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic in Bountiful and Clinton are here to provide you with relief. We can help you identify the cause of your lingering back pain and create a comprehensive, personalized plan to ensure comfort is within reach.

Restoring Alignment and Function

When your spine is misaligned, it can lead to chronic pain, reduced mobility, and increased stress on your muscles and joints. At Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, we focus on restoring alignment to improve overall function and relieve discomfort. We correct misalignments that cause nerve irritation, muscle tension, and restricted movement through gentle adjustments.

In addition to spinal adjustments, our back specialists incorporate complementary therapies such as soft tissue work, corrective exercises, and mobility training to ensure long-lasting results. Our goal is to relieve your pain and restore optimal spinal function so you can move freely and live without discomfort.

If you’ve struggled with back pain for a while, our back specialists at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic are dedicated to helping you feel better. Don’t let this chronic pain get you down for one more day. Instead, rely on our team for support and trust that a decrease in discomfort is just an appointment away.

Lifestyle and Posture Guidance for Long-Term Relief

Maintaining a healthy spine requires more than an in-office treatment with our back specialists. You also need to make smart choices in your daily routine. Poor posture, prolonged sitting, and improper movement can contribute to chronic pain and spine misalignment. Some changes you can make to improve your back health include:

Practice Good Posture: Keep your shoulders back and spine aligned, and avoid slouching when sitting or standing.

Optimize Your Workstation: Use an ergonomic chair, adjust your monitor to eye level, and take frequent breaks to move around.

Lift Properly: Bend at the knees, keep your back straight, and use your legs to lift heavy objects instead of straining your back.

Stay Active: Engage in regular stretching and strengthening exercises to support your spine and prevent stiffness.

Choose Supportive Footwear: Wear shoes with proper arch support to help you maintain spinal alignment.

Sleep in a Spine-Friendly Position: Use a supportive mattress and pillow to keep your spine in a neutral position while sleeping.

By implementing these habits, in addition to visiting our back specialists, you can protect your spine, prevent recurring pain, and enjoy long-term relief. If you need additional support, we will provide personalized guidance to ensure you maintain a strong, healthy back for years to come.

Trust Our Back Specialist to Help You Achieve a Pain-Free Back

Back pain can be a plague on your day-to-day life, but with the support of our back specialists at Elevate Wellness Chiropractic, this discomfort is a thing of the past. Our team provides expert chiropractic support to patients in Bountiful and Clinton, helping them feel their best once again. Yes. Regular exercise can strengthen the muscles that support your spine while improving flexibility, balance, and posture. Activities such as walking, swimming, stretching, and core strengthening exercises are commonly recommended.

Yes. Poor posture places additional stress on the muscles, joints, and discs of the spine. Sitting for long periods, looking down at electronic devices, and having an improper workstation setup can all contribute to chronic back discomfort.

For many patients with mechanical back pain, chiropractic adjustments are considered safe when performed after a thorough examination by a licensed chiropractor. Your provider will evaluate your condition and determine the safest treatment approach for your specific needs.

pages.bodyCopy:
Chiropractic Care

Home - Chiropractic

At Elevate Wellness, we focus on treating your whole body. We don’t believe in simply masking symptoms; we want to find and treat the source of your pain and dysfunction and restore your body to its proper form. We can accomplish these goals through chiropractic care.

What is Chiropractic Care?

Chiropractic care is a therapeutic treatment designed to treat problems in the musculoskeletal and nervous systems. It is sometimes referred to as spinal manipulation or joint manipulation. Through this treatment, we can help patients find relief from back, neck, joint, arm, and leg pain, as well as headaches and migraines. We can also help you improve your posture.

Chiropractic care involves making adjustments. When chiropractors adjust your back, they use their hands or small instruments to apply quick, controlled force to a joint or stretch a joint to help align the vertebrae in your spine if they are off center and solve any subluxations, which is when a joint is partially pushed or pulled out of its normal position.

You may feel and hear popping or cracking sounds when getting adjusted. These are gases, such as oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide, being released from your joints. It’s completely normal and should be no cause for alarm.

Do Adjustments hurt?

If you have a really inflamed section of your body, you may feel some discomfort while being adjusted; you may also feel a bit sore or stiff after treatment. However, you should not feel any severe or throbbing pain. You should only feel a release of tension or pressure in the part of your body being treated.

You can apply ice to the treated parts of your body to relieve any soreness or stiffness if you feel uncomfortable.

The Gonstead Technique

The Gonstead Technique, named after its creator, Dr. Clarence Gonstead, focuses on the core foundation and intervertebral discs. He believed that in order for you to have maximum balance and stability, you need to have your pelvis, vertebrae, and legs level. This technique allows chiropractors to focus on intervertebral misalignments, motion disturbances, and nerve dysfunction.

Over time, you may develop misalignments that can separate, twist, or tilt the vertebrae and pinch or compress nerves, leading to pain. These subluxations can lead to a number of ailments throughout the body.

Our chiropractors will integrate the core Gonstead elements, which include:

Visualization, This involves looking at the patient carefully to document anything off between the hips, ears, and shoulders, as well as anything wrong with the patient’s posture and gait.

Instrumentation, Chiropractors will use a Nervoscope to locate areas of inflammation and where there are any subluxations.

Palpation, This is the hands-on part of the examination that helps the chiropractor locate any more subluxations or other areas of concern.

X-Rays, You will get full spine X-rays to analyze your posture and recommend corrective measures.

Patient Symptoms, Our chiropractors will take the time to listen to you, learn your health history, and understand why you are at our office.

While we focus primarily on the Gonstead Technique, we have studied and mastered several techniques to improve your spinal health and reduce nervous system interference. We also strive to stay educated about the latest technologies. As a result, we can provide many different adjustments, so don’t hesitate to let us know about an experience or technique you received in the past that helped you; we can deliver what you are looking for and more.

What to Expect During Your Visit to Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

When you visit our office, we will discuss your health history and perform an examination. Our examination process will include X-rays, a series of tests, including use of the nervoscope, and analysis. Dr. Simmonds will sit down and discuss the current health issues you are experiencing and creating a specialized treatment plan, which may include more appointments and stretches or exercises to complete at home.

Back Pain

Home - Back Pain

Many adults experience upper and lower back pain. Whether you experience discomfort when you first wake up, after sitting for long stretches at work, or completing daily activities, back pain can affect your whole day, making it hard to function and limiting your range of motion.

Back pain is one of the most common reasons people seek chiropractic care, and it’s also one of the most treatable. At Elevate Wellness, we target back pain at its source, offering personalized care plans designed to relieve discomfort and restore mobility without the need for drugs or surgery. Call us today if you’re experiencing back pain, and we can set you up with an appointment to get you more aligned.

Causes Of Back Pain

Back pain can result from a variety of issues. When you book an appointment at Elevate Wellness, we can help determine the source of your pain.

Muscle Strain and Sprains, Lifting heavy objects without bending your knees or twisting your back can strain muscles and ligaments. Twisting, bending, or reaching awkwardly or overusing your muscles can also strain your back muscles and lead to pain.

Disc Problems, Herniated or bulging discs and degenerative disc disease can cause nerve compression and back pain. This pain can radiate down into your hips, butt, and legs.

Spinal Stenosis, This condition involves a narrowing of the spinal canal, which can compress the spinal cord and nerves, causing pain and other symptoms.

Both spinal stenosis and herniated discs can cause sciatica, a painful condition caused by irritation or compression of the sciatic nerve. This can lead to pain in the lower back and down the legs, as well as numbness, weakness, and tingling.

Poor Posture, Poor posture can strain the muscles and ligaments supporting the spine, leading to pain and discomfort.

Spinal Misalignment, When vertebrae are out of their normal alignment, it can put pressure on nerves, leading to pain, muscle spasms, and even numbness.

Car and Sport Injuries, Car and sport injuries can lead to muscle damage, ligament damage, disc displacement, and even spinal fractures, all of which can cause pain and discomfort.

How Chiropractic Care Can Help

Chiropractic care has been proven to help the body heal naturally and work to lower inflammation. We offer safe, effective, and non-invasive treatments such as:

Spinal Adjustments, Chiropractors use controlled force to adjust the spine, restoring proper alignment and movement, relieving pressure on nerves, and reducing pain and inflammation.

Massage Therapy and Soft Tissue Work, Chiropractors can use massage therapy, stretching, and other techniques to relieve muscle tension, reduce spasms and inflammation, and improve circulation in the back.

Therapeutic Exercises, You can practice and learn exercises that strengthen supporting muscles in your back and improve your posture.

Postural and Ergonomic Coaching, Chiropractors can help you improve your posture and workplace ergonomics to prevent future pain and support healing. They can also provide general lifestyle advice to support overall health and well-being.

Additional Benefits

When you seek treatment for your back pain, you do more than just realign your spine and reduce pain. Your back is connected to the nervous system and tissues throughout your body. Treatment can benefit your digestive system, reduce pregnancy symptoms, improve your immune system, and more. Chiropractic care can give you an overall better quality of life.

Why Choose Elevated Wellness?

At Elevate Wellness, we understand back injuries and pain and can get your spine back in alignment, no matter if you have lower disc discomfort or upper back pain. Our chiropractor, Dr. Simmonds, will discuss your current health issues and goals, so that you can receive personalized treatment and excellent care. If you are suffering from lower or upper back pain that’s disrupting your daily life, give our office in Clinton or Bountiful, Utah, a call, and we can help you live pain-free.

Stress can contribute to muscle tension, particularly in the neck, shoulders, and lower back. Over time, chronic muscle tightness may increase discomfort and reduce mobility. Managing stress through exercise, stretching, adequate sleep, and relaxation techniques may help reduce symptoms.

+Is it normal for back pain to come and go?

Some conditions cause intermittent pain that flares up with certain activities or prolonged sitting. However, recurring back pain should be evaluated to identify the underlying cause and reduce the risk of future episodes.

Yes. Regular exercise can strengthen the muscles that support your spine while improving flexibility, balance, and posture.

It depends on your surgical history and current condition. Many people who have had back surgery may still benefit from chiropractic care, but your chiropractor will perform a thorough evaluation and modify treatment as needed to ensure your safety.

NOTICE OF PRIVACY PRACTICES (NPP) OF Elevate Wellness Chiropractic

Effective Date: February 16, 2026

THIS NOTICE DESCRIBES HOW MEDICAL INFORMATION ABOUT YOU MAY BE USED AND DISCLOSED AND HOW YOU CAN GET ACCESS TO THIS INFORMATION. PLEASE REVIEW IT CAREFULLY.

1. Our Legal Duty

Elevate Wellness Chiropractic is required by applicable federal and state law to maintain the privacy of your Protected Health Information (PHI) and to provide you with this Notice detailing our legal duties and privacy practices. We are required to abide by the terms of this Notice currently in effect and to notify you following a breach of unsecured PHI.

We reserve the right to change our privacy practices and the terms of this Notice at any time, provided such changes are permitted by applicable law. We reserve the right to make the changes in our privacy practices and the new terms of our Notice effective for all health information that we maintain, including health information we created or received before we made the changes.

2. Alignment with 42 CFR Part 2 (Substance Use Disorder Records)

Pursuant to the CARES Act and the 2024 Final Rule, if we create, receive, maintain, or transmit Substance Use Disorder (SUD) records protected by 42 CFR Part 2 (“Part 2 records”), we apply the following protections in addition to HIPAA:

Consent and Permitted Uses/Disclosures: We will obtain your written consent before using or disclosing Part 2 records for treatment, payment, and healthcare operations (TPO).

TPO and Redisclosure: Once we have your initial written consent for TPO, we may use and disclose those records as permitted by HIPAA. This includes “redisclosure”, meaning other healthcare providers or insurance companies who receive your records from us may also use and disclose them for TPO purposes as permitted by HIPAA, unless you revoke your consent.

Legal Protections in Proceedings: Your Part 2 records (and any testimony derived from them) are strictly protected and generally may not be used to initiate or substantiate criminal, civil, administrative, or legislative investigations or proceedings against you without a specific court order or your written consent.

Record of Shared Information: For Part 2 records, you have a right to a list (an accounting) of disclosures made through an electronic health record for TPO purposes for up to 3 years prior to your request.

3. Uses and Disclosures of Health Information

We may use and disclose your PHI for the following purposes:

Treatment: We may disclose your PHI to a physician, nurse, or other healthcare provider providing treatment to you.

Payment: We may use and disclose your PHI to obtain payment for services we provide to you.

Healthcare Operations: We may use and disclose your PHI in connection with our healthcare operations, including quality assessment and improvement activities.

Marketing and Sale of PHI: We will not sell your PHI or use your PHI for marketing purposes that involve financial remuneration from a third party without your express written authorization.

Fundraising: We may contact you for fundraising efforts. You have the right to opt out of receiving such communications at any time.

Disclosures to Family and Friends: Unless you object, we may disclose PHI to a family member or friend involved in your care or payment.

State-Specific Protections (Idaho & Utah): We follow more restrictive state laws regarding HIV/AIDS status (Idaho Code § 39-606), genetic testing (Utah Code § 26B-8-401), and mental health records.

4. Patient Rights

Access and Third-Party Directives: You have the right to inspect or obtain copies of your PHI. You may request these records in digital/electronic format. You also have the right to direct us to send a copy of your PHI directly to another person or entity (a third-party directive) if your request is in writing, signed, and clearly identifies the designated person and where to send the information. We may charge a reasonable, cost-based fee.

Record of Shared Information: You have the right to receive a list of instances in which we or our business associates disclosed your PHI for purposes other than treatment, payment, healthcare operations, and certain other activities.

Restriction: You have the right to request additional restrictions on our use or disclosure of your PHI. We must agree to a request to restrict disclosure of PHI to a health plan if the disclosure is for the purpose of carrying out payment or healthcare operations and the PHI pertains solely to a healthcare item or service for which you have paid us in full out-of-pocket.

Amendment: You have the right to request that we amend your PHI. Your request must be in writing and explain the reason for the amendment.

Confidential Communications: You have the right to request that we communicate with you in a specific manner or at a specific location.

Personal Representative: If you have given someone medical power of attorney or if someone is your legal guardian, that person can exercise your rights and make choices about your PHI. We will confirm the person’s authority before we take any action.

Paper Copy: You have the right to a paper copy of this Notice at any time, even if you have agreed to receive it electronically.

Revocation: You may revoke any authorization or consent you provided in writing at any time, except to the extent we have already taken action in reliance on it.

5. Breach Notification

In the event of a breach of your unsecured PHI, we will notify you as required by law. Notifications will be made via first-class mail (or email if you have opted in) without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 days following the discovery of the breach.

6. Changes to this Notice

We reserve the right to change our privacy practices. If we make material changes, we will post the updated Notice on our website and make copies available in our office.

7. Complaints and Contact Information

If you believe your privacy rights have been violated, you may file a complaint with us or the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. We will not retaliate against you in any way for filing a complaint.

To file a complaint with us:

Privacy Officer: [Privacy Officer Name/Title]Telephone: [Phone Number]Email: [Email Address]Address:Elevate Wellness Chiropractic[Physical Address]

To file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services:Online: Office for Civil Rights (OCR) Complaint Portal at https://ocrportal.hhs.gov

Sciatica Treatment

Your sciatic nerve sits in your lower back and branches through your hips, buttocks, and down each leg. When this nerve becomes pitched or inflamed, it can cause a dull ache or sharp, burning pain around your spine and buttocks and down one leg. If you’re experiencing sciatica, Elevate Wellness Chiropractic can help you find relief.

Sciatica pain is usually caused by a herniated disk or bone spur on the spine that compresses the nerve. This pressure causes inflammation and numbness in your leg, eventually leading to pain radiating throughout your body.

At Elevate Wellness, we can use spinal manipulation and decompression, massage therapy, and other techniques to relieve pitching and stabbing pain, reduce inflammation, and restore range of motion. Spinal decompression is especially effective if your sciatic pain is due to a herniated disk.
